plain_english_summary: Lets the Central Government, by order published in the Official Gazette, make provisions necessary to remove any difficulty in giving effect to the Code, within a limited window after commencement.

title: Repeal and savings
text: (1) The following enactments are hereby repealed, namely:— 1. The Employee's Compensation Act, 1923; 2. The Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948; 3. The Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952; 4. The Employment Exchanges (Compulsory Notification of Vacancies) Act, 1959; 5. The Maternity Benefit Act, 1961; 6. The Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972; 7. The Cine-Workers Welfare Fund Act, 1981; 8. The Building and Other Construction Workers' Welfare Cess Act, 1996; 9. The Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act, 2008. (2) Notwithstanding such repeal,— (a) anything done or an

sub_structure.1: (1) The following enactments are hereby repealed, namely:— 1. The Employee's Compensation Act, 1923; 2. The Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948; 3. The Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952; 4. The Employment Exchanges (Compulsory Notification of Vacancies) Act, 1959; 5. The Maternity Benefit Act, 1961; 6. The Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972; 7. The Cine-Workers Welfare Fund Act, 1981; 8. The Building and Other Construction Workers' Welfare Cess Act, 1996; 9. The Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act, 2008.
sub_structure.2: (2) Notwithstanding such repeal,— (a) anything done or any action taken under the enactments so repealed including any rule, regulation, notification (including the notifications issued by the States), scheme, appointment, order or direction made thereunder or any benefit provided or given under any provision of such enactments, rules, regulations, notifications or schemes made thereunder for any purpose shall be deemed to have been done or taken or provided for such purpose under the corresponding provisions of this Code including any rule, regulation, notification, scheme, appointment, order or direction made thereunder and shall be in force to the extent they are not contrary to the provisions of this Code including any rule, regulation, notification, scheme, appointment, order or direction made thereunder till they are repealed under the corresponding provisions of this Code including any rule, regulation, notification, scheme, appointment, order or direction made thereunder by the appropriate Government; (b) the Employees' Provident Funds Scheme, 1952, the Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme, 1976, the Employees' Pension Scheme, 1995 and the Tribunal (Procedure) Rules, 1997 framed or made under the Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 and the rules, regulations and schemes made or framed under the Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948, shall remain in force, to the extent they are not inconsistent with the provisions of this Code for a period of one year from the date of commencement of this Code; (c) any exemption given under any enactments so repealed shall continue to be in force till its validity expires or it ceases to be in operation under the provisions of this Code or till any direction is made thereunder for such purpose.
sub_structure.3: (3) Without prejudice to the provisions of sub-section ( 2), the provisions of section 6 of the General Clauses Act, 1897 shall apply to the repeal of such enactments. Power to remove difficulties. Repeal and savings. 8 of 1923. 34 of 1948. 19 of 1952. 31 of 1959. 53 of 1961. 39 of 1972. 33 of 1981. 28 of 1996. 33 of 2008. 19 of 1952. 34 of 1948. 10 of 1897.

plain_english_summary: Repeals nine earlier social security laws (including the Employee's Compensation Act 1923, ESI Act 1948, EPF Act 1952, and Payment of Gratuity Act 1972) while saving actions already taken, pending proceedings and rights accrued under them.

title: Short title, extent, commencement and application

sub_structure.1: (1) This Act may be called the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970.
sub_structure.2: (2) It extends to the whole of India.
sub_structure.3: (3) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Act.
sub_structure.4: (4) It applies to every establishment where twenty or more workmen are (or were, in the preceding twelve months) employed as contract labour, and to every contractor who employs (or employed in the preceding twelve months) twenty or more such workmen; the appropriate Government may, after two months' notice, extend the Act to establishments or contractors employing fewer than twenty workmen.
sub_structure.5: (5) The Act does not apply to establishments where only intermittent or casual work is performed; if a dispute arises over whether work is intermittent or casual, the appropriate Government decides after consulting the Central or State Board, and its decision is final. Work is not treated as intermittent if it was performed for more than 120 days in the preceding twelve months, or is seasonal and performed for more than 60 days in a year.

plain_english_summary: Names the Act, extends it across India, sets a government-notified commencement date, applies it to establishments and contractors with 20+ contract workmen (extendable to smaller ones), and excludes purely intermittent or casual work (defined by a 120-day or 60-day seasonal threshold).

title: Definitions
text: (1) In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires,—

sub_structure.a: "appropriate Government" means the Central Government for establishments where the Central Government is the appropriate Government under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, and the State Government for any other establishment.
sub_structure.b: A workman is deemed employed as "contract labour" when hired in connection with an establishment's work by or through a contractor, with or without the principal employer's knowledge.
sub_structure.c: "contractor" means a person who undertakes to produce a given result for an establishment (other than merely supplying goods) through contract labour, or who supplies contract labour for the establishment's work, and includes a sub-contractor.
sub_structure.d: "controlled industry" means an industry whose control by the Union has been declared expedient in the public interest by a Central Act.
sub_structure.e: "establishment" means any office or department of the Government or a local authority, or any place where an industry, trade, business, manufacture or occupation is carried on.
sub_structure.f: "prescribed" means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
sub_structure.g: "principal employer" means the head of a government office/department (or an officer they specify), the owner/occupier of a factory (or its named manager), the owner/agent of a mine (or its named manager), or, for any other establishment, the person responsible for its supervision and control.
sub_structure.h: "wages" has the meaning assigned to it in the Payment of Wages Act, 1936.
sub_structure.i: "workman" means a person doing skilled, semi-skilled or unskilled manual, supervisory, technical or clerical work for hire or reward in connection with an establishment's work, but excludes persons employed mainly in a managerial or administrative capacity, supervisory employees drawing wages above five hundred rupees a month or exercising mainly managerial functions, and certain out-workers who process materials at home or off-site premises not controlled by the principal employer.

plain_english_summary: Defines the Act's key terms, notably who counts as 'contract labour', 'contractor', 'establishment', 'principal employer', and 'workman' (with specific carve-outs for managers, higher-paid supervisors, and home-based out-workers).

title: Central Advisory Board

sub_structure.1: (1) The Central Government shall constitute a Central Advisory Contract Labour Board to advise it on matters arising from the Act's administration and to carry out other assigned functions.
sub_structure.2: (2) The Central Board consists of a Chairman appointed by the Central Government, the Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) ex-officio, and 11 to 17 nominated members representing the Government, Railways, coal and mining industries, contractors, workmen, and other relevant interests.
sub_structure.3: (3) The number of members per category, their terms and conditions of service, procedure, and how vacancies are filled shall be prescribed, with the workmen's representation never less than that of principal employers and contractors combined.

plain_english_summary: Sets up a tripartite Central Advisory Contract Labour Board to advise the Central Government, specifying its composition (government, industry, contractor and worker representatives) and guaranteeing workers at least as much representation as employers and contractors combined.

title: State Advisory Board

sub_structure.1: (1) A State Government may constitute a State Advisory Contract Labour Board to advise it on matters arising from the Act's administration and to carry out other assigned functions.
sub_structure.2: (2) The State Board consists of a Chairman appointed by the State Government, the Labour Commissioner (or nominee) ex officio, and 9 to 11 nominated members representing the Government, industry, contractors, workmen, and other relevant interests.
sub_structure.3: (3) The number of members per category, terms and conditions, procedure, and vacancy-filling shall be prescribed, with workmen's representation never less than that of principal employers and contractors combined.

plain_english_summary: Allows each State Government to set up its own tripartite Advisory Board mirroring the Central Board's structure and the same guaranteed worker representation.

title: Power to constitute committees

sub_structure.1: (1) The Central or State Board may constitute committees for any purpose it thinks fit.
sub_structure.2: (2) A committee shall meet at prescribed times and places, following prescribed procedure.
sub_structure.3: (3) Committee members are paid prescribed fees and allowances for attending meetings, except government or public-corporation officers, who receive no fee.

plain_english_summary: Lets the Advisory Boards form sub-committees for specific purposes, with prescribed meeting procedures and fees (except for government/public-body officer members, who aren't paid).

chapter_title: REGISTRATION OF ESTABLISHMENTS EMPLOYING CONTRACT LABOUR
title: Appointment of registering officers
text: The appropriate Government may, by a notified order, appoint Gazetted Officers as registering officers for this Chapter's purposes, and define the territorial limits of their powers.
plain_english_summary: Allows the appropriate Government to appoint Gazetted Officers as registering officers and define their jurisdiction for registering establishments.

chapter_title: REGISTRATION OF ESTABLISHMENTS EMPLOYING CONTRACT LABOUR
title: Registration of certain establishments

sub_structure.1: (1) Every principal employer of a covered establishment must apply to the registering officer for registration within a government-fixed period, though late applications may still be entertained for sufficient cause.
sub_structure.2: (2) If the application is complete, the registering officer shall register the establishment and issue a certificate of registration with prescribed particulars.

plain_english_summary: Requires principal employers to apply for establishment registration within a set deadline (with late-filing leniency for good cause), after which a complete application results in a registration certificate.

chapter_title: REGISTRATION OF ESTABLISHMENTS EMPLOYING CONTRACT LABOUR
title: Revocation of registration in certain cases
text: If the registering officer is satisfied that a registration was obtained by misrepresentation or suppression of a material fact, or has otherwise become useless or ineffective, the officer may, after hearing the principal employer and with the appropriate Government's prior approval, revoke the registration.
plain_english_summary: Allows a registering officer, with government approval and after hearing the employer, to cancel a registration obtained through misrepresentation or that has become ineffective.

chapter_title: REGISTRATION OF ESTABLISHMENTS EMPLOYING CONTRACT LABOUR
title: Effect of non-registration
text: No principal employer of a covered establishment shall employ contract labour after the registration deadline has passed without registering, or after the establishment's registration has been revoked under section 8.
plain_english_summary: Bars an employer from using contract labour once the registration deadline has lapsed unregistered, or once its registration has been revoked.

chapter_title: REGISTRATION OF ESTABLISHMENTS EMPLOYING CONTRACT LABOUR
title: Prohibition of employment of contract labour

sub_structure.1: (1) The appropriate Government may, after consulting the Central or State Board, prohibit by notification the employment of contract labour in any process, operation or work in an establishment, notwithstanding anything else in the Act.
sub_structure.2: (2) Before issuing such a notification, the Government must consider the contract labour's working conditions and benefits, and factors such as whether the work is incidental/necessary to the establishment's core activity, whether it is of a perennial nature, whether it is ordinarily done by regular workmen, and whether it justifies employing a considerable number of whole-time workmen; the Government's decision on whether work is of a perennial nature is final.

plain_english_summary: Gives the appropriate Government power, after Board consultation, to ban contract labour altogether for particular kinds of work, guided by factors like whether the work is core, ongoing, and substantial enough to warrant regular employees.

title: Appointment of licensing officers
text: The appropriate Government may, by a notified order, appoint Gazetted Officers as licensing officers for this Chapter's purposes and define the territorial limits of their powers.
plain_english_summary: Allows the appropriate Government to appoint Gazetted Officers as licensing officers with defined jurisdiction over contractor licensing.

title: Licensing of contractors

sub_structure.1: (1) From a government-notified date, a covered contractor may not undertake or execute any work through contract labour except under a licence issued by the licensing officer.
sub_structure.2: (2) A licence may include conditions on hours of work, wage fixation, and other amenities as the appropriate Government thinks fit under the rules, and is issued on payment of prescribed fees and, if applicable, a security deposit.

plain_english_summary: Requires contractors to hold a licence before engaging contract labour, with the licence able to set conditions on hours, wages and welfare amenities, issued on payment of fees and a possible security deposit.

title: Grant of licences

sub_structure.1: (1) A licence application must be made in the prescribed form, stating the establishment's location, the nature of work for which contract labour is needed, and other prescribed particulars.
sub_structure.2: (2) The licensing officer may investigate the application following prescribed procedure.
sub_structure.3: (3) A granted licence is valid for the period specified and may be renewed on payment of prescribed fees and conditions.

plain_english_summary: Sets out the licence application process (prescribed form, officer investigation) and provides for time-limited licences that can be renewed.

title: Revocation, suspension and amendment of licences

sub_structure.1: (1) If the licensing officer is satisfied that a licence was obtained by misrepresentation or suppression of a material fact, or that the holder failed without reasonable cause to comply with its conditions or contravened the Act or rules, the officer may, after giving the holder a chance to show cause, revoke or suspend the licence or forfeit all or part of the security deposit, without prejudice to any other penalty.
sub_structure.2: (2) Subject to any applicable rules, the licensing officer may vary or amend a licence.

plain_english_summary: Allows a licensing officer, after a show-cause opportunity, to revoke, suspend or amend a contractor's licence (and forfeit its security deposit) for misrepresentation or breach of licence conditions.

title: Appeal

sub_structure.1: (1) A person aggrieved by an order under sections 7, 8, 12 or 14 may appeal, within thirty days of the order's communication, to a government-nominated appellate officer, who may condone delay for sufficient cause.
sub_structure.2: (2) The appellate officer shall dispose of the appeal as expeditiously as possible after giving the appellant a hearing.

plain_english_summary: Gives a right of appeal, within 30 days, against registration, revocation, or licensing decisions, to a government-nominated appellate officer who must decide promptly after a hearing.

chapter_title: WELFARE AND HEALTH OF CONTRACT LABOUR
title: Canteens

sub_structure.1: (1) The appropriate Government may make rules requiring one or more canteens to be provided and maintained by the contractor in covered establishments where contract-labour work is likely to continue for a prescribed period and where 100 or more contract labourers are ordinarily employed by a contractor.
sub_structure.2: (2) Such rules may cover the date by which canteens must be provided, the number and construction/accommodation/furniture standards, and the food and charges permitted.

plain_english_summary: Requires canteens at larger contract-labour worksites (100+ workers on an ongoing basis), with the government able to prescribe canteen numbers, standards, and food/pricing rules.

chapter_title: WELFARE AND HEALTH OF CONTRACT LABOUR
title: Rest-rooms

sub_structure.1: (1) Where contract labour must halt overnight for a covered establishment's work likely to continue for a prescribed period, the contractor must provide and maintain rest-rooms or suitable alternative accommodation within a prescribed time.
sub_structure.2: (2) Such rest-rooms or accommodation must be sufficiently lit and ventilated and kept clean and comfortable.

plain_english_summary: Requires contractors to provide adequately lit, ventilated and clean overnight rest-rooms (or equivalent accommodation) for contract labour who must stay overnight for the work.

chapter_title: WELFARE AND HEALTH OF CONTRACT LABOUR
title: Other facilities
text: Every contractor employing contract labour on a covered establishment's work must provide and maintain a sufficient supply of wholesome drinking water at convenient places, a sufficient number of prescribed-type latrines and urinals conveniently located, and washing facilities.
plain_english_summary: Obliges contractors to provide drinking water, latrines/urinals, and washing facilities for contract labour.

chapter_title: WELFARE AND HEALTH OF CONTRACT LABOUR
title: First-aid facilities
text: The contractor must provide and maintain a first-aid box with prescribed contents, readily accessible during all working hours, at every place where contract labour is employed.
plain_english_summary: Requires contractors to keep a readily accessible, properly stocked first-aid box at every contract-labour worksite.

chapter_title: WELFARE AND HEALTH OF CONTRACT LABOUR
title: Liability of principal employer in certain cases

sub_structure.1: (1) If a contractor fails to provide a required amenity under sections 16-19 within the prescribed time, the principal employer must provide it within a prescribed time instead.
sub_structure.2: (2) The principal employer may recover the expenses incurred from the contractor, either by deducting from amounts owed to the contractor or as a debt.

plain_english_summary: Makes the principal employer step in and provide welfare amenities if the contractor fails to, while letting the employer recover the cost from the contractor.

chapter_title: WELFARE AND HEALTH OF CONTRACT LABOUR
title: Responsibility for payment of wages

sub_structure.1: (1) The contractor is responsible for paying wages to each contract labourer, within a prescribed time.
sub_structure.2: (2) The principal employer must nominate a representative to be present at wage disbursement and certify the amounts paid.
sub_structure.3: (3) The contractor must ensure wages are disbursed in the presence of the principal employer's authorised representative.
sub_structure.4: (4) If the contractor fails to pay wages on time or pays short, the principal employer is liable to pay the full or unpaid balance to the contract labour, and may recover that amount from the contractor by deduction or as a debt.

plain_english_summary: Makes the contractor primarily responsible for timely wage payment (witnessed and certified by the principal employer's representative), with the principal employer stepping in to pay any shortfall and recovering it from the contractor afterward.

title: Obstructions

sub_structure.1: (1) Obstructing an inspector, or refusing/wilfully neglecting to give reasonable facilities for an authorised inspection, examination, inquiry or investigation, is punishable with imprisonment up to three months, or a fine up to five hundred rupees, or both.
sub_structure.2: (2) Wilfully refusing to produce a required register or document, or preventing (or attempting to prevent) any person from appearing before or being examined by an inspector, carries the same punishment.

plain_english_summary: Penalizes obstructing an inspector or withholding required records/testimony with up to 3 months' imprisonment and/or a Rs. 500 fine.

title: Contravention of provisions regarding employment of contract labour
text: Contravening any Act provision or rule prohibiting, restricting or regulating contract labour employment, or any licence condition, is punishable with imprisonment up to three months, or a fine up to one thousand rupees, or both, with an additional fine up to one hundred rupees per day for continuing contravention after a first conviction.
plain_english_summary: Sets penalties (up to 3 months' imprisonment and/or Rs. 1,000 fine, plus daily fines for continued violation) for breaching contract-labour employment restrictions or licence conditions.

title: Other offences
text: Contravening any provision of the Act or rules for which no other penalty is specified elsewhere is punishable with imprisonment up to three months, or a fine up to one thousand rupees, or both.
plain_english_summary: Provides a residual penalty (up to 3 months' imprisonment and/or Rs. 1,000 fine) for any Act or rule violation not covered by a more specific penalty provision.

title: Offences by companies

sub_structure.1: (1) If the offender is a company, the company and every person in charge of and responsible for its business at the time of the offence are deemed guilty and liable, unless that person proves the offence occurred without their knowledge or that they exercised due diligence to prevent it.
sub_structure.2: (2) Where the offence is proved to have been committed with the consent, connivance, or attributable negligence of a director, manager, managing agent or other officer, that person is also deemed guilty and liable.

plain_english_summary: Makes a company and its responsible officers liable for company offences (subject to a due-diligence defence), with extended liability for officers whose consent, connivance, or negligence caused the offence.

title: Cognizance of offences
text: No court shall take cognizance of an offence under this Act except on a complaint by, or with the prior written sanction of, the inspector, and no court inferior to a Presidency Magistrate or a Magistrate of the first class shall try an offence under this Act.
plain_english_summary: Restricts prosecutions to inspector-initiated or inspector-sanctioned complaints, and sets a minimum court level for trials.

title: Limitation of prosecutions
text: No court shall take cognizance of an offence under this Act unless the complaint is made within three months of the offence coming to an inspector's knowledge, except for disobeying a written inspector's order, where the limit is six months from the alleged offence.
plain_english_summary: Sets a 3-month limitation period for most prosecutions (6 months for disobeying a written inspector's order), running from when the inspector learns of the offence.

title: Inspecting staff

sub_structure.1: (1) The appropriate Government may, by notification, appoint inspectors for the Act's purposes and define their local jurisdiction.
sub_structure.2: (2) Within their jurisdiction, an inspector may enter and inspect premises where contract labour is employed to examine registers/records/notices and demand their production; examine any person reasonably believed to be a workman there; require information about who work is given out to and payments made; seize or copy relevant registers/records for a suspected offence; and exercise other prescribed powers.
sub_structure.3: (3) A person required to produce documents or give information is deemed legally bound to do so under the Indian Penal Code's provisions on refusing to give evidence or information to a public servant.
sub_structure.4: (4) The Code of Criminal Procedure's search-and-seizure provisions apply to inspections under this section as they would to a warrant-based search.

plain_english_summary: Empowers the appropriate Government to appoint inspectors with entry, examination, information-demanding, and document-seizure powers, backed by Penal Code obligations to cooperate and CrPC search-and-seizure procedure.

title: Registers and other records to be maintained

sub_structure.1: (1) Every principal employer and contractor must maintain prescribed registers and records on contract labour employed, work performed, and wages paid.
sub_structure.2: (2) Every principal employer and contractor must display prescribed notices at the establishment about hours of work, nature of duty, and other prescribed information.

plain_english_summary: Requires both principal employers and contractors to keep prescribed records on contract labour and to publicly display notices about working conditions.

title: Effect of laws and agreements inconsistent with this Act

sub_structure.1: (1) The Act overrides any inconsistent law, agreement, contract of service, or standing order, except that contract labour keeps any more-favourable benefits they already had under such an agreement/order for a given matter, even while receiving Act benefits for other matters.
sub_structure.2: (2) Nothing in the Act prevents contract labour from separately agreeing with the principal employer or contractor for more favourable rights or privileges than the Act provides.

plain_english_summary: Gives the Act overriding effect over inconsistent laws and agreements, while preserving any more-favourable existing benefits and allowing future agreements for even better terms.

title: Power to exempt in special cases
text: In an emergency, the appropriate Government may, by notification, direct that all or any provisions of the Act or its rules shall not apply, subject to specified conditions and for a specified period, to any establishment, class of establishments, or class of contractors.
plain_english_summary: Lets the appropriate Government temporarily exempt establishments or contractors from the Act during an emergency.

title: Protection of action taken under this Act

sub_structure.1: (1) No suit, prosecution or legal proceeding lies against a registering officer, licensing officer, other government servant, or Central/State Board member for anything done or intended in good faith under the Act or its rules/orders.
sub_structure.2: (2) No suit or legal proceeding lies against the Government for damage caused or likely to be caused by anything done or intended in good faith under the Act or its rules/orders.

plain_english_summary: Shields officials and the Government from legal liability for actions taken in good faith while implementing the Act.

title: Power to give directions
text: The Central Government may give directions to a State Government on the execution of the Act's provisions within that State.
plain_english_summary: Allows the Central Government to direct State Governments on how the Act is carried out in their states.

title: Power to remove difficulties
text: If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the Act, the Central Government may, by order published in the Official Gazette, make provisions (not inconsistent with the Act) necessary or expedient to remove the difficulty.
plain_english_summary: Gives the Central Government power to issue orders resolving practical difficulties in implementing the Act.

title: Power to make rules

sub_structure.1: (1) The appropriate Government may, subject to prior publication, make rules to carry out the Act's purposes.
sub_structure.2: (2) Such rules may cover matters including: Board membership numbers and terms; committee meeting procedure and fees; the manner of establishment registration and fees; licence application forms and particulars; licence investigation procedure; licence forms, conditions, fees and security deposits; circumstances for varying licences; appeal forms and procedure; timelines for welfare facilities (and principal-employer default provisions); canteen/rest-room/latrine/urinal numbers and types; first-aid box contents; wage payment timelines; register and record forms; returns and submission authorities; collection of contract-labour statistics; and any other prescribed matter.
sub_structure.3: (3) Every Central Government rule must be laid before each House of Parliament for thirty days, subject to modification or annulment by both Houses.
sub_structure.4: (4) Every State Government rule must similarly be laid before the State Legislature.

plain_english_summary: Empowers the appropriate Government to make detailed implementing rules covering board composition, registration, licensing, welfare facilities, wages, and recordkeeping, subject to parliamentary or state-legislature review.

title: Short title, extent and commencement
text: This Act may be called the Employee's Compensation Act, 1923.

sub_structure.2: It extends to the whole of India.
sub_structure.3: It shall come into force on the first day of July, 1924.

plain_english_summary: Names the Act, applies it across all of India, and fixes its commencement date as 1 July 1924.

title: Definitions
text: In this Act, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context, various terms are defined.

sub_structure.b: "Commissioner" means a Commissioner for Employee's Compensation appointed under section 20.
sub_structure.c: "compensation" means compensation as provided for by this Act.
sub_structure.d: "dependant" means specified relatives of a deceased employee, including a widow, minor children, an unmarried daughter, a widowed mother, and (if wholly or partly dependent) a widower, parent, minor siblings, a widowed daughter-in-law, and certain grandchildren or grandparents.
sub_structure.dd: "employee" means a railway servant not in an administrative/sub-divisional office, a master/seaman/aircraft crew member, a motor-vehicle driver/helper/mechanic/cleaner, a person recruited for work abroad in a capacity specified in Schedule II, or any person employed in a capacity specified in Schedule II; it excludes members of the Armed Forces of the Union, and includes dependants where the employee has died.
sub_structure.e: "employer" includes any body of persons, a managing agent, the legal representative of a deceased employer, and, where an employee's services are lent to another, that other person while the employee works for him.
sub_structure.f: "managing agent" means a person appointed to act as the representative of another for carrying on that other's trade/business, excluding a subordinate individual manager.
sub_structure.ff: "minor" means a person who has not attained the age of eighteen years.
sub_structure.g: "partial disablement" means reduced earning capacity in the employment held at the time of the accident (if temporary) or in every employment the person was capable of undertaking (if permanent); every injury in Part II of Schedule I is deemed permanent partial disablement.
sub_structure.i: "qualified medical practitioner" means a person registered under a relevant medical practitioners' law, or declared qualified by the State Government by notification.
sub_structure.k: "seaman" means a person forming part of a ship's crew, excluding the master.
sub_structure.l: "total disablement" means disablement incapacitating the employee for all work capable of being performed at the time of the accident; permanent total disablement is deemed to result from every injury in Part I of Schedule I, or combinations in Part II totalling 100% or more loss of earning capacity.
sub_structure.m: "wages" includes any money-estimable privilege or benefit, but excludes travelling allowance, travel-concession value, employer pension/provident-fund contributions, and special-expense reimbursements.

plain_english_summary: Defines the Act's key vocabulary: who counts as an 'employee' (covering railway servants, seamen, aircraft crew, motor-vehicle workers and Schedule II occupations, but not the armed forces), who is a 'dependant' entitled to claim after a worker's death, and technical terms like 'partial/total disablement' and 'wages' that determine how much compensation is owed.

title: Employer's liability for compensation
text: If personal injury is caused to an employee by accident arising out of and in the course of his employment, the employer is liable to pay compensation, subject to exceptions.

sub_structure.1_proviso_a: No liability for injury not causing disablement beyond three days.
sub_structure.1_proviso_b: No liability (unless death or permanent total disablement results) where the accident is directly attributable to the employee's intoxication, wilful disobedience of a safety order/rule, or wilful removal/disregard of a safety guard.
sub_structure.2: Contracting a scheduled occupational disease (Schedule III, Parts A/B/C, subject to service-duration conditions for Parts B/C) is deemed an injury by accident arising out of and in the course of employment.
sub_structure.2A: Where an occupational disease under Schedule III Part C arises from service under more than one employer, all such employers share liability as the Commissioner deems just.
sub_structure.3: The appropriate Government may, after three months' notice, add employments to Schedule III and specify the occupational diseases peculiar to them.
sub_structure.4: No compensation is payable for a disease unless it is directly attributable to a specific accidental injury, except as covered by sub-sections (2)/(2A)/(3).
sub_structure.5: An employee who has sued for damages in a Civil Court cannot also claim compensation under this Act, and a compensation claim before a Commissioner (or a compensation agreement) bars a subsequent civil suit for damages.

plain_english_summary: Establishes the core 'no-fault' compensation duty: an employer must pay for accidental workplace injuries, with narrow exceptions for minor injuries, intoxication or wilful safety violations, and extends this duty to scheduled occupational diseases; also bars double recovery through both a court damages suit and a compensation claim.

title: Amount of compensation
text: Sets out the compensation amounts: for death, 50% of monthly wages multiplied by the relevant factor or Rs 1,20,000, whichever is more; for permanent total disablement, 60% of monthly wages multiplied by the relevant factor or Rs 1,20,000, whichever is more (Central Government may enhance these amounts by notification).

sub_structure.1_c: For permanent partial disablement: the Schedule I Part II percentage of the total-disablement compensation for scheduled injuries, or a medically-assessed proportionate percentage for unscheduled injuries (aggregated across multiple injuries from one accident, capped at the total-disablement amount).
sub_structure.1_d: For temporary disablement (total or partial): a half-monthly payment equal to 25% of monthly wages.
sub_structure.1A: For accidents occurring outside India, the Commissioner must offset any compensation already awarded under the foreign country's law.
sub_structure.1B: The Central Government may notify the monthly wages figure to be used for calculating compensation.
sub_structure.2: Half-monthly payments become due on the 16th day (from disablement, if disablement lasts 28+ days, or after a 3-day waiting period if shorter), continuing during disablement or for five years, whichever is shorter; deductions apply for compensation already paid, and no payment can exceed half the pre-accident/post-accident wage difference.
sub_structure.2A: The employee must be reimbursed actual medical expenditure for treatment of employment injuries.
sub_structure.3: On cessation of disablement mid-half-month, a proportionate sum is payable for that half-month.
sub_structure.4: On death, the employer must additionally deposit at least Rs 5,000 with the Commissioner for the funeral expenses of the deceased (Central Government may enhance this amount).

plain_english_summary: Fixes the compensation formulas: death and permanent total disablement pay 50%/60% of wages (times an age-based factor) or a fixed minimum (Rs 1,20,000), whichever is greater; permanent partial disablement is a proportion of that; temporary disablement pays 25% of wages half-monthly; and a separate minimum funeral-expense deposit is required on death, alongside reimbursement of actual medical costs.

title: Compensation to be paid when due and penalty for default
text: Compensation under section 4 shall be paid as soon as it falls due.

sub_structure.2: If the employer disputes the extent of liability, he must still make a provisional payment based on what he accepts, without prejudice to the employee's right to claim more.
sub_structure.3_a: If the employer defaults for over one month from when compensation fell due, the Commissioner shall order payment of the arrears plus simple interest at 12% per annum (or a higher notified rate).
sub_structure.3_b: If the delay is unjustified, the Commissioner may also order a penalty of up to 50% of the arrears, but only after giving the employer a chance to show cause.
sub_structure.3A: Interest and penalty amounts are paid to the employee or dependant.

plain_english_summary: Requires prompt payment of compensation, including a mandatory provisional payment where liability is disputed, and imposes 12%+ annual interest plus up to a 50% penalty (after a hearing) on employers who default for more than a month.

title: Method of calculating wages
text: Defines 'monthly wages' for compensation purposes based on the employee's actual earning history.

sub_structure.a: Where employed continuously for 12+ months before the accident: one-twelfth of total wages earned in the last twelve months.
sub_structure.b: Where the continuous service was less than one month: the average monthly wage of a comparable employee on the same or similar work in the same locality.
sub_structure.c: In other cases: thirty times the total wages earned in the last continuous period of service, divided by the number of days in that period.
sub_structure.explanation: A period of service is 'continuous' unless interrupted by an absence exceeding fourteen days.

plain_english_summary: Sets three formulas for calculating 'monthly wages' depending on how long the employee had worked before the accident, ensuring a fair wage base even for short-tenure or piece-rate workers.

title: Review
text: Any half-monthly payment may be reviewed by the Commissioner on application of the employer or employee, generally supported by a qualified medical practitioner's certificate of changed condition (or without one, per rules).

sub_structure.2: On review, a half-monthly payment may be continued, increased, decreased, ended, or converted to a lump sum (less amounts already paid) if permanent disablement is found.

plain_english_summary: Allows either party to ask the Commissioner to revisit an ongoing half-monthly payment if the worker's medical condition changes, potentially converting it into a final lump sum for permanent disablement.

title: Commutation of half-monthly payments
text: A right to receive half-monthly payments may be redeemed for a lump sum by agreement, or, after six months of continued payments, on application to the Commissioner if the parties cannot agree.
plain_english_summary: Lets an ongoing half-monthly compensation stream be converted into a one-time lump sum, either by mutual agreement or via the Commissioner after six months.

title: Distribution of compensation
text: Death compensation, and any lump sum payable to a woman or person under legal disability, must be paid by deposit with the Commissioner (not directly by the employer, except limited funeral advances).

sub_structure.1_proviso: An employer may advance a deceased employee's dependant up to three months' wages, deductible later from the compensation.
sub_structure.4: On deposit of death compensation, the Commissioner may notify dependants to appear for distribution proceedings; if no dependant is found, the balance is repaid to the employer.
sub_structure.5: Compensation for a deceased employee is apportioned among dependants as the Commissioner thinks fit.
sub_structure.7: Lump sums payable to a woman or person under legal disability may be invested or applied for their benefit as the Commissioner directs.
sub_structure.8: The Commissioner may vary a distribution order for sufficient cause (e.g. parental neglect or changed circumstances), after giving an affected person a chance to be heard.
sub_structure.9: Amounts obtained by fraud, impersonation or other improper means may be recovered under section 31.

plain_english_summary: Protects vulnerable claimants (deceased workers' dependants, women, and persons under legal disability) by routing lump-sum compensation through the Commissioner for supervised distribution, investment or variation, rather than direct employer payment.

title: Compensation not to be assigned, attached or charged
text: No lump sum or half-monthly payment under this Act can be assigned, charged, attached, or passed to anyone other than the employee by operation of law, nor can any claim be set off against it.
plain_english_summary: Shields compensation payments from being seized by creditors, assigned away, or offset against other claims — the money must reach the injured worker or dependant.

title: Notice and claim
text: No compensation claim shall be entertained unless notice of the accident was given as soon as practicable and the claim is preferred within two years of the accident (or of death).

sub_structure.1_proviso1: For occupational diseases, the accident is deemed to occur on the first day of continuous absence from work due to the disease.
sub_structure.1_proviso4: Defects or absence of notice do not bar a claim if the employee died on the employer's premises/place of work, or if the employer had independent knowledge of the accident.
sub_structure.1_proviso5: The Commissioner may still entertain a late claim if satisfied the delay was due to sufficient cause.
sub_structure.2: The notice must state the injured person's name/address, the cause and date of injury, and be served on the employer or a responsible manager.
sub_structure.3: The State Government may require prescribed employers to maintain an accessible notice-book.
sub_structure.4: Notice may be served by delivery, registered post, or entry in a notice-book.

plain_english_summary: Sets a two-year limitation period for compensation claims (with the clock adjusted for occupational diseases), but gives the Commissioner discretion to excuse late or defective notice for good reason or where the employer already knew.

title: Power to require from employers statements regarding fatal accidents
text: On learning of a fatal work accident, the Commissioner may require the employer, by registered notice, to submit within 30 days a statement on the circumstances and whether he accepts liability.

sub_structure.2: If the employer accepts liability, he must deposit the compensation within 30 days.
sub_structure.3: If he disclaims liability, he must state the grounds.
sub_structure.4: Where liability is disclaimed, the Commissioner may inform dependants of their right to claim compensation.

plain_english_summary: Gives the Commissioner power to compel an employer to explain a fatal accident and state his liability position within 30 days, and to then alert the dependants of their right to claim if the employer denies liability.

title: Reports of fatal accidents and serious bodily injuries
text: Where notice of a fatal or serious workplace accident must be given to any authority, that person must also send a report to the Commissioner within seven days.

sub_structure.explanation: 'Serious bodily injury' includes permanent loss/injury to a limb, sight or hearing, fracture of any limb, or enforced absence from work exceeding twenty days.
sub_structure.2: The State Government may extend this reporting duty to other classes of premises and specify who must report.
sub_structure.3: This section does not apply to factories covered by the Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948.

plain_english_summary: Requires employers to report serious or fatal workplace accidents to the Commissioner within seven days, defining exactly what counts as a 'serious bodily injury', while exempting ESI-covered factories.

title: Medical examination
text: An employee who has given accident notice must submit to a free medical examination if the employer offers one within three days, and must periodically re-submit if receiving half-monthly payments.

sub_structure.2: Unreasonable refusal or obstruction of the examination suspends the right to compensation during the refusal.
sub_structure.3: Leaving the vicinity before the examination period expires also suspends the right to compensation until the employee returns and submits.
sub_structure.4: If the employee dies without having submitted to examination, the Commissioner may still direct compensation to dependants.
sub_structure.6: Unreasonable refusal to be treated by, or to follow the instructions of, a free medical practitioner offered by the employer — where this aggravates the injury — means compensation is calculated as if the employee had been properly treated.

plain_english_summary: Requires an injured employee to cooperate with employer-arranged medical examination and treatment, suspending compensation rights during unreasonable refusal, though the Commissioner retains discretion to protect dependants if the worker dies.

title: Contracting
text: Where a principal contracts out work ordinarily part of his own trade/business, he is liable to pay compensation to an employee of the contractor as if directly employed, calculated on that employee's actual wages.

sub_structure.2: A principal who pays such compensation is entitled to be indemnified by the contractor (or further up the chain); disputes over indemnity are settled by the Commissioner.
sub_structure.3: The employee may still choose to recover compensation from the contractor directly instead.
sub_structure.4: This section does not apply where the accident occurred away from the principal's premises or work under his control.

plain_english_summary: Makes a principal employer liable for compensation to a contractor's injured worker doing the principal's core business, while giving the principal a right to be indemnified by the contractor.

title: Remedies of employer against stranger
text: Where an employee recovers compensation for an injury also giving rise to a third party's legal liability for damages, whoever paid the compensation (or indemnity) is entitled to be indemnified by that liable third party.
plain_english_summary: Lets an employer who has paid compensation recover that cost from a third party who was actually legally responsible for causing the injury.

title: Insolvency of employer
text: Where an insured employer becomes insolvent or is wound up, his rights against the insurer transfer to the injured employee, who can then claim directly from the insurer (limited to what the insurer would owe the employer).

sub_structure.2: If the insurer's liability is less than the employer's, the employee may prove for the balance in insolvency/liquidation proceedings.
sub_structure.4: Compensation liabilities accrued before insolvency/winding-up rank among the priority debts under the relevant insolvency/companies laws.
sub_structure.7: This section does not apply where a company is wound up voluntarily merely for reconstruction or amalgamation.

plain_english_summary: Protects injured employees when an employer becomes insolvent by transferring the employer's insurance rights directly to them, and by giving unpaid compensation priority-debt status in insolvency proceedings.

title: Compensation to be first charge on assets transferred by employer
text: Where an employer transfers assets before paying compensation that accrued before the transfer, the unpaid amount becomes a first charge on the transferred immovable property.
plain_english_summary: Prevents employers from evading compensation debts by transferring away property — such debts attach first to any transferred immovable property.

title: Special provisions relating to masters and seamen
text: Applies the Act to masters and seamen with modifications, including notice served on the ship's master, and special claim-timing rules.

sub_structure.2: Death claims must be made within one year of news of death, or within eighteen months if the ship is deemed lost with all hands (subject to the Commissioner's discretion to excuse delay).
sub_structure.3: Depositions taken abroad by judges, magistrates or consular officers are admissible in evidence, subject to authentication and cross-examination safeguards.
sub_structure.4: No half-monthly payment is due while the shipowner is legally liable to maintain the injured seaman under merchant shipping law.
sub_structure.5: No compensation is payable where a gratuity/allowance/pension is provided under specified war pension schemes.

plain_english_summary: Adapts the compensation process to seafaring work — special notice rules, extended claim periods for lost ships, and admissibility of foreign depositions — while avoiding double provision with maritime maintenance or war-pension schemes.

title: Special provisions relating to captains and other members of crew of aircrafts
text: Applies similar modifications as section 15 to aircraft captains and crew: notice via the captain, claim timing tied to news of death or the aircraft being deemed lost, and admissibility of foreign depositions.
plain_english_summary: Extends the same seafarer-style special procedural rules (notice, claim timing, foreign depositions) to aircraft crew members.

title: Special provisions relating to employees abroad of companies and motor vehicles
text: Applies to employees recruited by Indian companies working abroad, and persons sent abroad with registered motor vehicles as drivers/helpers/mechanics, with modified notice, claim-timing, and evidence rules similar to sections 15/15A.
plain_english_summary: Extends the special abroad-work procedural framework (local-agent notice, one-year death-claim window, foreign deposition admissibility) to overseas company employees and motor-vehicle crews.

title: Returns as to compensation
text: The State Government may require employers (or specified classes) to submit periodic returns on the number of injuries compensated and the amounts paid.
plain_english_summary: Allows government to mandate regular compensation-statistics reporting from employers.

title: Contracting out
text: Any contract or agreement by which an employee gives up their right to compensation for a work injury is null and void to the extent it removes or reduces the employer's statutory liability.
plain_english_summary: Prevents employers from using private contracts to make workers waive their statutory compensation rights.

title: Duty to inform employee of rights
text: Every employer shall, immediately upon employing an employee, inform them in writing and electronically of their compensation rights under this Act, in English, Hindi, or the local official language understood by the employee.
plain_english_summary: Requires employers to proactively and accessibly (in writing, electronically, and in an understood language) inform every new employee of their compensation rights.

title: Proof of age (Repealed)
text: This section was repealed by the Workmen's Compensation (Amendment) Act, 1959, with effect from 1 June 1959.
plain_english_summary: A now-repealed provision that previously dealt with proof of age.

title: Penalties
text: Failure to maintain a required notice-book, send a required fatal-accident statement, send a required serious-injury report, make a required return, or inform an employee of rights under section 17A, is punishable with a fine of not less than fifty thousand rupees, extendable to one lakh rupees.

sub_structure.2: Prosecution requires the Commissioner's prior sanction, and a court cannot take cognizance unless a complaint is made within six months of the Commissioner learning of the offence.

plain_english_summary: Sets a substantial fine (Rs 50,000 to 1,00,000) for administrative non-compliance — failing to keep notice-books, file statements/reports/returns, or inform employees of their rights — with a Commissioner-sanction and six-month complaint-window safeguard before prosecution.

title: Reference to Commissioners
text: Any dispute over liability to pay compensation (including whether someone is an 'employee') or over the amount/duration of compensation shall, absent agreement, be settled by a Commissioner.

sub_structure.2: No Civil Court has jurisdiction over matters required to be settled by a Commissioner under this Act, nor to enforce liabilities arising under it.

plain_english_summary: Channels all compensation disputes exclusively to the Commissioner, excluding civil courts from jurisdiction over these matters.

title: Appointment of Commissioners
text: The State Government may appoint, by notification, a qualified person (with judicial, legal, or relevant Gazetted-officer experience) as Commissioner for Employees' Compensation for a specified area.

sub_structure.2: Where multiple Commissioners serve one area, the State Government may regulate distribution of business between them.
sub_structure.3: A Commissioner may co-opt persons with special knowledge to assist in an inquiry.
sub_structure.4: Every Commissioner is deemed a public servant under the Indian Penal Code.

plain_english_summary: Establishes how Commissioners (requiring judicial, legal or senior administrative experience) are appointed for specific areas, with public-servant status and the ability to bring in expert assistance.

title: Venue of proceeding and transfer
text: Matters under this Act are handled by the Commissioner for the area where the accident occurred, where the employee/dependant resides, or where the employer's registered office is.

sub_structure.1_proviso1: Proceeding before a Commissioner other than the one covering the accident location requires notice to that Commissioner and the relevant State Government.
sub_structure.1_proviso2: For accidents abroad involving ships/aircraft/motor vehicles/companies, the matter may be handled where the owner/agent/company is based.
sub_structure.2: A Commissioner satisfied a matter can be more conveniently handled elsewhere may transfer it to another Commissioner, for report or disposal, transmitting relevant documents and funds.
sub_structure.5: The State Government may transfer matters between Commissioners it has appointed.

plain_english_summary: Sets flexible venue rules (accident site, claimant's residence, or employer's office) for compensation proceedings, with mechanisms to transfer cases between Commissioners for convenience, and special rules for accidents occurring abroad.

title: Form of application
text: A compensation claim may be made to the Commissioner following an accident giving rise to liability under the Act.

sub_structure.1A: Except for dependants' claims, an application to the Commissioner can only be made once a dispute has arisen that the parties could not settle by agreement.
sub_structure.2: Applications must be in the prescribed form/fee and include a statement of circumstances and relief sought, notice-service details, party names/addresses, and points of agreement/disagreement.
sub_structure.3: An illiterate or otherwise unable applicant may have the application prepared under the Commissioner's direction.

plain_english_summary: Sets the procedural requirements for filing a compensation claim, requiring a genuine unresolved dispute (except for dependants) and providing assistance for applicants who cannot write their own application.

title: Power of Commissioner to require further deposit in cases of fatal accident
text: If a Commissioner considers a deposited death-compensation sum insufficient, he may require the employer, by written notice, to show cause why a further deposit should not be made.

sub_structure.2: If the employer fails to justify the shortfall, the Commissioner may award the total amount payable and require the deficiency to be deposited.

plain_english_summary: Lets the Commissioner correct an inadequate death-compensation deposit by ordering the employer, after a hearing, to pay the shortfall.

title: Powers and procedure of Commissioners
text: The Commissioner has all the powers of a Civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure for taking evidence on oath, enforcing witness attendance, and compelling production of documents/objects, and is deemed a Civil Court for certain Criminal Procedure Code purposes.
plain_english_summary: Gives Commissioners formal civil-court powers to summon witnesses, take sworn evidence, and demand documents, treating their proceedings as judicial in nature.

title: Appearance of parties
text: Parties may appear before a Commissioner (other than for their own witness examination) through a legal practitioner, an insurance company official, a registered trade union official, a Factories/Mines Act inspector, or another authorised person.
plain_english_summary: Allows represented appearance before the Commissioner via lawyers, insurers, trade unions or authorised inspectors, rather than requiring the party to always appear personally.

title: Method of recording evidence
text: The Commissioner shall record a brief signed memorandum of each witness's evidence as the examination proceeds, forming part of the record.

sub_structure.proviso2: Medical witness evidence must be recorded as nearly as possible word for word.

plain_english_summary: Requires the Commissioner to personally record witness testimony as it is given, with especially precise (near-verbatim) recording for medical witnesses.

title: Time limit for disposal of cases relating to compensation
text: The Commissioner shall dispose of compensation matters within three months from the date of reference and communicate the decision to the employee within that period.
plain_english_summary: Imposes a strict three-month deadline for the Commissioner to decide and communicate compensation cases.

title: Costs
text: All costs incidental to proceedings before a Commissioner are, subject to rules made under the Act, in the Commissioner's discretion.
plain_english_summary: Gives the Commissioner discretion over awarding costs in compensation proceedings.

title: Power to submit cases
text: A Commissioner may submit any question of law to the High Court for decision, and must decide the matter in conformity with that decision.
plain_english_summary: Allows the Commissioner to refer difficult legal questions to the High Court and bind the final decision to the High Court's ruling.

title: Registration of agreements
text: Where a lump sum compensation amount (including for a woman or person under legal disability) is settled by agreement, the employer must send a memorandum to the Commissioner for registration once satisfied of its genuineness.

sub_structure.1_proviso_a: No memorandum can be recorded before seven days after the Commissioner notifies the parties.
sub_structure.1_proviso_c: The Commissioner may rectify the register at any time.
sub_structure.1_proviso_d: The Commissioner may refuse registration (and make consequential orders) if an agreement's amount is inadequate or was obtained by fraud, undue influence, or other improper means.
sub_structure.2: A registered compensation agreement is enforceable under this Act despite anything in the Indian Contract Act, 1872 or other law.

plain_english_summary: Requires lump-sum compensation agreements — especially those involving women or persons under legal disability — to be vetted and registered by the Commissioner, who can refuse registration for inadequate or improperly obtained settlements.

title: Effect of failure to register agreement
text: If a required agreement memorandum is not sent to the Commissioner under section 28, the employer remains liable to pay the full compensation amount and cannot deduct more than half of any amount already paid, unless the Commissioner directs otherwise.
plain_english_summary: Penalises employers who skip the mandatory registration of compensation agreements by denying them the usual right to deduct prior payments beyond 50%.

title: Appeals
text: An appeal lies to the High Court against specified Commissioner orders: lump-sum compensation awards/disallowances, interest/penalty orders under section 4A, refusal of redemption, distribution/disallowance of dependant claims, indemnity claims under section 12(2), and agreement-registration decisions.

sub_structure.1_proviso1: An appeal requires a substantial question of law, and (except for redemption-refusal orders) the amount in dispute must be at least ten thousand rupees or a higher notified amount.
sub_structure.1_proviso2: No appeal lies where parties agreed to abide by the Commissioner's decision or where the order merely records their agreement.
sub_structure.1_proviso3: An employer's appeal against a lump-sum award requires a Commissioner certificate confirming the appellant has deposited the awarded amount.
sub_structure.2: The limitation period for appeal is sixty days.
sub_structure.3: Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963 (condonation of delay) applies to these appeals.

plain_english_summary: Defines a limited right of appeal to the High Court from specific Commissioner orders, gated by a substantial-question-of-law requirement, a minimum disputed amount, a 60-day limitation period, and (for employer appeals) mandatory prior deposit of the awarded sum.

title: Omitted
text: This section was omitted by Act 11 of 2017 (the Employee's Compensation (Amendment) Act, 2017).
plain_english_summary: A provision that no longer has effect, having been removed by the 2017 amendment.

title: Recovery
text: The Commissioner may recover any amount payable under this Act as an arrear of land revenue, and is deemed a public officer under the Revenue Recovery Act, 1890 for this purpose.
plain_english_summary: Gives the Commissioner strong recovery powers, treating unpaid compensation like unpaid land revenue for enforcement purposes.

title: Power of the State Government to make rules
text: The State Government may make rules to carry out the Act's purposes.

sub_structure.2_a_b: Rules may cover conditions for review applications without a medical certificate, and intervals/conditions for required medical examinations.
sub_structure.2_c_d: Rules may prescribe Commissioner procedure and rules for transferring matters/money between Commissioners.
sub_structure.2_i_j: Rules may regulate cost scales and fees payable for proceedings.
sub_structure.2_p_q_r: Rules may prescribe how occupational diseases are diagnosed/certified and how incapacity is assessed.

plain_english_summary: Empowers State Governments to make detailed procedural rules covering everything from medical review conditions to fee scales, disease diagnosis, and incapacity assessment standards.

title: Power of Local Government to make rules (Repealed)
text: This section was repealed by the Adaptation Order, 1937.
plain_english_summary: A historical provision no longer in force.

title: Publication of rules
text: Rules under section 32 are subject to prior publication before being made.

sub_structure.2: A draft rule must be published for at least three months before being finalised, per the General Clauses Act.
sub_structure.3: Rules take effect, once published in the Official Gazette, as if enacted in this Act.

plain_english_summary: Requires State rule-making to go through a minimum three-month public draft/consultation period before rules take legal effect.

title: Rules to give effect to arrangements with other countries for the transfer of money paid as compensation
text: The Central Government may make rules for transferring compensation money deposited with a Commissioner to a foreign country (and vice versa) for persons residing there.

sub_structure.1_proviso: Death-accident deposits cannot be transferred abroad without the employer's consent until distribution/apportionment orders are made.
sub_structure.2: Once transferred under these rules, the Act's usual distribution provisions cease to apply to that money.

plain_english_summary: Enables cross-border transfer of compensation funds for claimants living abroad, with safeguards requiring proper distribution decisions first in fatal-accident cases.

title: Rules made by Central Government to be laid before Parliament
text: Every Central Government rule under this Act shall be laid before each House of Parliament for a total of thirty days; both Houses may modify or annul the rule, without prejudice to anything already done under it.
plain_english_summary: Subjects Central Government rule-making under the Act to a 30-day parliamentary review and possible modification/annulment.

chapter_title: LIST OF INJURIES DEEMED TO RESULT IN PERMANENT DISABLEMENT
title: List of Injuries Deemed to Result in Permanent Total or Partial Disablement (see sections 2(1) and 4)
text: Part I lists injuries deemed to cause 100% loss of earning capacity (permanent total disablement), such as loss of both hands, loss of a hand and a foot, double leg/thigh amputation, sight loss preventing any work, severe facial disfigurement, and absolute deafness. Part II lists injuries deemed to cause permanent partial disablement, each assigned a specific percentage of loss of earning capacity, covering amputations of arms, hands, fingers, legs, feet and toes at various levels, and other injuries such as loss of one eye or partial vision loss.

sub_structure.Part_I: Six listed injuries each rated at 100% loss of earning capacity: loss of both hands or equivalent amputation; loss of a hand and a foot; double leg/thigh amputation or equivalent; sight loss preventing any eyesight-dependent work; very severe facial disfigurement; absolute deafness.
sub_structure.Part_II_upper_limbs: Amputation cases for upper limbs rated 20% to 90% depending on level (shoulder joint down to phalanx), plus specific finger-loss percentages.
sub_structure.Part_II_lower_limbs: Amputation cases for lower limbs rated 20% to 90% depending on level (hip down to toes).
sub_structure.Part_II_other: Other injuries including loss of one eye (40%), loss of vision of one eye (30%), partial vision loss (10%), and detailed finger/toe loss percentages.
sub_structure.note: Complete and permanent loss of use of a limb or member is deemed equivalent to loss of that limb or member.

plain_english_summary: A detailed injury-to-percentage ratings table used to calculate permanent disablement compensation: Part I lists catastrophic injuries treated as 100% total disablement (e.g., loss of both hands, total blindness), while Part II assigns specific loss-of-earning-capacity percentages to particular amputations and injuries (e.g., losing a thumb = 30%, losing one eye = 40%), which are used to compute proportionate compensation under section 4.

chapter_title: LIST OF PERSONS INCLUDED IN THE DEFINITION OF EMPLOYEES
title: List of Persons Who Are Employees Under Section 2(1)(dd)
text: Lists occupations and work categories that qualify a person as an 'employee' under section 2(1)(dd), including railway operation/maintenance workers, factory/manufacturing-process workers, explosives handlers, mine workers, ships' masters/seamen, port/dock workers, construction/demolition workers on tall buildings/dams/roads/bridges, telegraph/telephone/electric line workers, firefighters, postal/railway mail workers, oilfield/gas workers, blasting workers, ferry operators, plantation workers, electricity/gas utility workers, lighthouse workers, film production workers, animal handlers (including wild animals, elephants, snakes), forestry/logging workers, divers, warehouse/market goods handlers, radiation workers, aircraft workers, agricultural/horticultural machinery operators, tube-well workers, circus workers, watchmen, fishing workers, sewer/septic-tank cleaners, and several other hazardous occupations.

sub_structure.i_v: Railway vehicle/lift operation and maintenance; factory manufacturing-process work; making/altering/repairing articles using power; explosives manufacture/handling; mining operations.
sub_structure.vi_vii: Ships' masters and seamen on powered or certain sailing vessels; port/dock cargo handling, ship mooring/docking and related maintenance work.
sub_structure.viii_x: Construction/demolition of tall buildings, dams, roads, bridges, tunnels, canals, marine works; telegraph/telephone/electric line work; aerial ropeway/canal/pipeline/sewer work.
sub_structure.xi_xx: Fire brigade service; railway employment (direct or via contractor); postal/telegraph outdoor work; petroleum/natural gas operations; blasting operations; deep excavation work; ferry operation; plantation work (cardamom, cinchona, coffee, rubber, tea); electricity/gas utility work; lighthouse work.
sub_structure.xxi_xxx: Cinematograph production/exhibition; handling of elephants/wild animals; palm-tapping, tree felling/logging, timber transport, forest-fire control; hunting/catching wild animals; diving; warehouse/market goods handling; radium/X-ray/radioactive work; aircraft-related work; horticulture/forestry/bee-keeping/mechanised farming; tube-well construction/repair.
sub_structure.xxxi_xlviii: Electric-fitting maintenance; circus work; factory/establishment watchmen; sea fishing; venomous-snake/poisonous-animal handling; handling horses/mules/bulls; loading/unloading mechanically propelled vehicles; sewer/septic-tank cleaning; river surveys/hydrological work; land/pond reclamation; cultivation/livestock/forest/fishing operations; water-pump installation/repair; well/borewell construction; pesticide spraying; mechanised harvesting/threshing; bulldozer/tractor/power-tiller work; high-elevation advertisement painting; newspaper-establishment outdoor work.

plain_english_summary: A long, specific list of hazardous or physically demanding occupations (railways, factories, mining, shipping, docks, construction, electrical/telecom lines, firefighting, oilfields, blasting, ferries, plantations, film production, wild-animal handling, forestry, diving, radiation work, aviation, farming machinery, well-digging, circuses, sewer cleaning, fishing, and more) whose workers automatically qualify as 'employees' entitled to compensation under the Act.

title: List of Occupational Diseases (see section 3)
text: Lists occupational diseases deemed to be injury by accident under section 3(2), divided into three parts by qualifying conditions: Part A covers infectious/parasitic diseases and diseases from compressed air, lead, nitrous fumes, and organophosphorus compounds, applicable regardless of length of service. Part B covers diseases from substances such as phosphorus, mercury, benzene, chromium, arsenic, radioactive substances, tar/pitch/mineral oil (skin cancer), carbon disulphide, noise-induced hearing loss, beryllium, cadmium, occupational asthma, and heat/cold extremes, requiring at least six months' continuous service in the relevant employment. Part C covers pneumoconioses (silicosis, asbestosis), bagassosis, byssinosis, extrinsic allergic alveolitis, hard-metal lung disease, and high-altitude pulmonary oedema, subject to a Central-Government-specified minimum service period.

sub_structure.Part_A: Infectious/parasitic disease from health, laboratory, veterinary or contamination-risk work; compressed-air disease; lead poisoning; nitrous fume poisoning; organophosphorus poisoning — no minimum service period required.
sub_structure.Part_B: 27 listed diseases (phosphorus, mercury, benzene, chromium, arsenic, radiation-induced disease and cancer, tar/pitch skin cancer, halogenated hydrocarbon disease, carbon disulphide disease, infra-red cataract, manganese disease, occupational skin disease, noise-induced hearing loss, dinitrophenol poisoning, beryllium/cadmium disease, occupational asthma, fluorine disease, nitroglycerin disease, alcohol/ketone disease, asphyxiant poisoning, asbestos-related lung cancer/mesothelioma, urinary tract neoplasm, snow blindness, heat/cold illness) — requires at least six months' continuous service in the relevant employment.
sub_structure.Part_C: Pneumoconiosis/silico-tuberculosis, bagassosis, byssinosis, extrinsic allergic alveolitis, hard-metal lung disease, acute high-altitude pulmonary oedema — requires a Central-Government-specified continuous service period per employment.

plain_english_summary: Defines which diseases count as job-caused ('occupational diseases') for compensation purposes, grouped into three tiers by how much continuous service is needed to trigger the presumption that the disease arose from the job: Part A diseases (like lead or organophosphorus poisoning) need no minimum service, Part B diseases (like mercury poisoning or noise-induced deafness) need six months' service, and Part C diseases (like silicosis or byssinosis) need a government-specified service period.

chapter_title: FACTORS FOR WORKING OUT LUMP SUM COMPENSATION
title: Factors for Working Out Lump Sum Equivalent of Compensation Amount in Case of Permanent Disablement and Death (see section 4)
text: Provides an age-based multiplier ('relevant factor') table used to convert monthly-wage-based compensation into a lump sum for death or permanent total disablement claims, ranging from a factor of 228.54 for workers aged 16 or under down to 99.37 for workers aged 65 or more, decreasing progressively with each additional year of age.

sub_structure.young: Ages up to 16: factor 228.54, decreasing gradually through the 20s and 30s (e.g., age 25 = 216.91; age 35 = 197.06).
sub_structure.older: Ages 56-65+: factor decreasing from 131.95 (age 56) to 99.37 (age 65 or more).

plain_english_summary: A statutory age-based multiplier table: the younger the worker at the time of the accident, the higher the multiplier applied to their wage-based compensation percentage, reflecting a longer expected working life — ranging from 228.54 for workers 16 or younger down to 99.37 for those 65 and older.

title: Short title, extent, commencement and application
text: (1) This Act may be called the Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948. (2) It extends to the whole of India. (3) It shall come into force on such date or dates as the Central Government may, by notification, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions and for different States or parts thereof. (4) It applies, in the first instance, to all factories (including Government factories) other than seasonal factories.

sub_structure.4_proviso: Sub-section (4) does not apply to a Government-controlled factory or establishment whose employees already receive benefits substantially similar or superior to those under this Act.
sub_structure.5: The appropriate Government, in consultation with the Corporation (and, for a State Government, with Central Government approval), after one month's notice by notification, may extend the Act's provisions to any other establishment, industrial, commercial, agricultural or otherwise.
sub_structure.5_proviso: Where the Act has been brought into force in part of a State, it automatically extends to similar establishments in another part of that State where already applied.
sub_structure.6: A factory or establishment to which the Act applies continues to be governed by it even if employee numbers fall below the specified limit or the manufacturing process ceases to use power.

plain_english_summary: Establishes the Act's name, nationwide extent, and staggered commencement by government notification, and defines its baseline coverage of non-seasonal factories (extendable to other establishments), with continued coverage even if a factory later shrinks below the threshold or stops using power.

title: Definitions
text: In this Act, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context-

sub_structure.1: 'appropriate Government' means the Central Government for establishments under Central Government control, a railway administration, a major port, a mine or oilfield, and the State Government in all other cases.
sub_structure.3: 'confinement' means labour resulting in a living child, or labour after 26 weeks of pregnancy resulting in a child whether alive or dead.
sub_structure.4: 'contribution' means the sum payable to the Corporation by the principal employer for an employee, including any amount payable by or on behalf of the employee.
sub_structure.6: 'Corporation' means the Employees' State Insurance Corporation set up under this Act.
sub_structure.6A: 'dependant' lists the deceased insured person's relatives entitled to dependant's benefit: widow, minor/unmarried children, widowed mother (wholly dependent categories); infirm adult children wholly dependent; and, if wholly or partly dependent, other parents, minor illegitimate children, minor siblings, widowed daughters-in-law, grandchildren of pre-deceased children, and paternal grandparents (in specified circumstances).
sub_structure.8: 'employment injury' means personal injury by accident or occupational disease arising out of and in the course of insurable employment, in or outside India.
sub_structure.9: 'employee' means a person employed for wages in or in connection with a covered factory/establishment's work-whether directly employed, employed through an immediate employer, or lent/let on hire-including administrative, purchase or sales-related staff and certain apprentices, but excluding armed forces members and employees whose wages exceed the Central Government-prescribed ceiling (with a proviso continuing coverage for the rest of a contribution period if wages cross the ceiling mid-period).
sub_structure.10: 'exempted employee' means an employee not liable to pay the employee's contribution.
