sub_structure.11: 'family' means specified relatives of an insured person: spouse, dependent minor children, a dependent child in education until 21 or an unmarried daughter, an infirm dependent child, income-limited dependent parents, and, if the insured person is unmarried and parentless, a dependent minor sibling.
sub_structure.12: 'factory' means premises where ten or more persons are or were employed on any day in the preceding twelve months and where a manufacturing process is carried on, excluding a Mines Act mine or a railway running shed.
sub_structure.13: 'immediate employer' means a person who has undertaken, on the factory/establishment premises or under the principal employer's supervision, execution of work ordinarily part of that factory/establishment's work, including a person lending/hiring out an employee's services, and includes a contractor.
sub_structure.13A: 'insurable employment' means employment in a factory or establishment to which the Act applies.
sub_structure.14: 'insured person' means a person who is or was an employee for whom contributions are or were payable, entitled to benefits by reason thereof.
sub_structure.14A: 'managing agent' means a person appointed to represent another in carrying on that person's trade or business, excluding a subordinate individual manager.
sub_structure.14AA: 'manufacturing process' has the meaning in the Factories Act, 1948.
sub_structure.14B: 'miscarriage' means expulsion of the contents of a pregnant uterus up to or during the 26th week of pregnancy, excluding miscarriage whose causing is a punishable offence under the Indian Penal Code.
sub_structure.15: 'occupier' of a factory has the meaning in the Factories Act, 1948.
sub_structure.15A: 'permanent partial disablement' means permanent disablement reducing earning capacity in every employment the person could undertake at the time of the accident; injuries in Second Schedule Part II are deemed to cause this.
sub_structure.15B: 'permanent total disablement' means permanent disablement incapacitating the person for all work they could perform at the time of the accident; injuries in Second Schedule Part I, or combinations in Part II totalling 100% loss of earning capacity, are deemed to cause this.
sub_structure.16: 'prescribed' means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
sub_structure.17: 'principal employer' means, for a factory, the owner/occupier (including managing agent, legal representative, or named manager); for a Government department establishment, the appointed authority or head of department; for any other establishment, the person responsible for supervision and control.
sub_structure.19A: 'seasonal factory' means a factory exclusively engaged in specified seasonal manufacturing processes (cotton ginning/pressing, groundnut decortication, coffee/indigo/lac/rubber/sugar/tea manufacture, or incidental processes), including tea/coffee blending-packing factories operating up to seven months a year, or other processes the Central Government notifies.
sub_structure.20: 'sickness' means a condition requiring medical treatment and attendance and necessitating abstention from work on medical grounds.
sub_structure.21: 'temporary disablement' means a condition from an employment injury requiring medical treatment and rendering the employee temporarily incapable of doing the work done prior to or at the time of injury.
sub_structure.22: 'wages' means all cash remuneration payable to an employee under the employment contract, including payment for authorised leave, lock-out, legal strike or lay-off, and other additional remuneration paid at intervals not exceeding two months, but excluding employer pension/PF contributions, travelling allowance, special expense reimbursements, and discharge gratuity.
sub_structure.23: 'wage period' means the period for which wages are ordinarily payable to an employee.
sub_structure.24: Undefined words and expressions defined in the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 carry the meanings assigned there.

plain_english_summary: A dense definitions section anchoring the whole scheme: defines who counts as an 'employee' (with a wage ceiling exclusion), 'family' and 'dependant' for benefit purposes, 'factory' (10+ workers), 'wages' for contribution calculation, and the different disablement and occupational-injury concepts used throughout the benefits chapter.

title: Registration of factories and establishments
text: Every factory or establishment to which this Act applies must be registered within such time and in such manner as may be specified in the regulations made in this behalf.
plain_english_summary: Requires every covered factory or establishment to register with the ESI scheme as prescribed by regulations.

chapter_title: CORPORATION, STANDING COMMITTEE AND MEDICAL BENEFIT COUNCIL
title: Establishment of Employees' State Insurance Corporation
text: (1) With effect from a Central Government-notified date, a Corporation called the Employees' State Insurance Corporation is established to administer the ESI scheme. (2) The Corporation is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, able to sue and be sued in that name.
plain_english_summary: Creates the Employees' State Insurance Corporation as a perpetual body corporate to run the ESI scheme.

chapter_title: CORPORATION, STANDING COMMITTEE AND MEDICAL BENEFIT COUNCIL
title: Constitution of Corporation
text: The Corporation consists of: (a) a Chairman appointed by the Central Government; (b) a Vice-Chairman appointed by the Central Government; (c) up to five persons appointed by the Central Government; (d) one representative per State (in which the Act is in force) appointed by the respective State Government; (e) one person appointed by the Central Government representing Union territories; (f) ten persons representing employers, appointed by the Central Government in consultation with recognised employer organisations; (g) ten persons representing employees, similarly appointed in consultation with recognised employee organisations; (h) two persons representing the medical profession, similarly appointed; (i) three Members of Parliament (two Lok Sabha, one Rajya Sabha), elected by their respective Houses; and (j) the Director General of the Corporation, ex officio.
plain_english_summary: Sets out the Corporation's tripartite-plus governance structure, combining Central and State Government appointees, employer/employee/medical-profession representatives, MPs, and the Director General as ex officio member.

chapter_title: CORPORATION, STANDING COMMITTEE AND MEDICAL BENEFIT COUNCIL
title: Term of office of members of the Corporation
text: (1) Save as otherwise provided, the term of office of Corporation members (other than those under section 4(a)-(e) and the ex officio member) is four years from the date their appointment/election is notified, and they continue in office until a successor is notified even after the term expires.

sub_structure.2: Members referred to in section 4(a)-(e) hold office during the pleasure of the appointing Government.

plain_english_summary: Fixes a standard four-year term (with holdover until a successor is notified) for most Corporation members, while Government-appointed members serve at the pleasure of the appointing Government.

chapter_title: CORPORATION, STANDING COMMITTEE AND MEDICAL BENEFIT COUNCIL
title: Eligibility for re-appointment or re-election
text: An outgoing member of the Corporation, Standing Committee, or Medical Benefit Council is eligible for re-appointment or re-election, as the case may be.
plain_english_summary: Confirms outgoing members can be reappointed or re-elected to the same bodies.

chapter_title: CORPORATION, STANDING COMMITTEE AND MEDICAL BENEFIT COUNCIL
title: Authentication of orders, decisions, etc.
text: All orders and decisions of the Corporation must be authenticated by the signature of the Director General, and all other instruments issued by the Corporation must be authenticated by the Director General's signature or that of an officer he authorises.
plain_english_summary: Requires Corporation orders/decisions and instruments to be formally authenticated by the Director General or an officer he authorises.

chapter_title: CORPORATION, STANDING COMMITTEE AND MEDICAL BENEFIT COUNCIL
title: Constitution of Standing Committee
text: The Standing Committee is constituted from Corporation members: (a) a Chairman appointed by the Central Government; (b) three members appointed by the Central Government; (bb) three members representing three State Governments as the Central Government specifies by notification; (c) eight members elected by the Corporation-three representing employers, three representing employees, one representing the medical profession, and one elected by Parliament members of the Corporation; and (d) the Director General, ex officio.
plain_english_summary: Creates a smaller Standing Committee, drawn from the full Corporation, to handle day-to-day administration between full Corporation meetings.

chapter_title: CORPORATION, STANDING COMMITTEE AND MEDICAL BENEFIT COUNCIL
title: Term of office of members of Standing Committee
text: (1) Save as otherwise provided, a Standing Committee member's term (other than under section 8(a), (b) or (bb)) is two years from the date election is notified, with holdover until a successor is notified; a member ceases to hold office on ceasing to be a Corporation member.

sub_structure.2: A member under section 8(a), (b) or (bb) holds office during the pleasure of the Central Government.

plain_english_summary: Sets a two-year term for elected Standing Committee members (tied to continued Corporation membership), while appointed members serve at the Central Government's pleasure.

chapter_title: CORPORATION, STANDING COMMITTEE AND MEDICAL BENEFIT COUNCIL
title: Medical Benefit Council
text: (1) The Central Government constitutes a Medical Benefit Council consisting of: (a) the Director General, ESIC, ex officio Chairman; (b) the Director-General, Health Services, ex officio Co-Chairman; (c) the Corporation's Medical Commissioner, ex officio; (d) one member per State (other than Union territories) in which the Act is in force, appointed by the respective State Government; (e) three members representing employers; (f) three members representing employees; and (g) three members (at least one woman) representing the medical profession-(e), (f) and (g) appointed by the Central Government in consultation with recognised organisations.

sub_structure.2: Save as otherwise provided, a member's term (other than under clauses (a)-(d)) is four years from notification, with holdover until a successor is notified.
sub_structure.3: Members under clauses (b) and (d) hold office during the pleasure of the appointing Government.

plain_english_summary: Establishes a specialist Medical Benefit Council-combining health-service officials, State representatives, and employer/employee/medical-profession nominees-to advise on medical benefit administration.

chapter_title: CORPORATION, STANDING COMMITTEE AND MEDICAL BENEFIT COUNCIL
title: Resignation of membership
text: A member of the Corporation, Standing Committee or Medical Benefit Council may resign by written notice to the Central Government; the seat falls vacant on acceptance of the resignation.
plain_english_summary: Allows members to resign, with the vacancy taking effect once the Central Government accepts the resignation.

chapter_title: CORPORATION, STANDING COMMITTEE AND MEDICAL BENEFIT COUNCIL
title: Cessation of membership
text: (1) A member ceases to be a member of the Corporation, Standing Committee or Medical Benefit Council if he fails to attend three consecutive meetings, subject to possible restoration under Central Government rules.

sub_structure.2: If the Central Government considers that a person appointed/elected to represent employers, employees or the medical profession has ceased to represent them, it may, by notification, declare the person to cease being a member from a specified date.
sub_structure.3: A person referred to in section 4(i) (MP members) ceases to be a member on becoming a Minister, Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Deputy Chairman of the Council of States, or on ceasing to be a member of Parliament.

plain_english_summary: Provides for automatic cessation of membership for persistent non-attendance (with a restoration option), loss of representative character, or (for MP members) taking certain other offices or leaving Parliament.

chapter_title: CORPORATION, STANDING COMMITTEE AND MEDICAL BENEFIT COUNCIL
title: Disqualification
text: A person is disqualified from being chosen as, or being, a member of the Corporation, Standing Committee or Medical Benefit Council if: (a) declared of unsound mind by a competent court; (b) an undischarged insolvent; (c) directly or indirectly interested in a subsisting contract with, or work for, the Corporation (except as a medical practitioner or non-director shareholder); or (d) convicted, before or after the Act's commencement, of an offence involving moral turpitude.
plain_english_summary: Bars persons who are of unsound mind, insolvent, have a conflicting financial interest in Corporation contracts, or have a moral-turpitude conviction from serving on these bodies.

chapter_title: CORPORATION, STANDING COMMITTEE AND MEDICAL BENEFIT COUNCIL
title: Filling of vacancies
text: (1) Vacancies among appointed or elected members of the Corporation, Standing Committee and Medical Benefit Council are filled by appointment or election, as applicable.

sub_structure.2: A member appointed or elected to fill a casual vacancy holds office only for the remainder of the term of the member they replace.

plain_english_summary: Provides that casual vacancies are filled by the same appointment/election process, with the replacement serving only the remainder of the original term.

chapter_title: CORPORATION, STANDING COMMITTEE AND MEDICAL BENEFIT COUNCIL
title: Fees and allowances
text: Members of the Corporation, Standing Committee and Medical Benefit Council receive fees and allowances as prescribed from time to time by the Central Government.
plain_english_summary: Entitles members of these bodies to Central Government-prescribed fees and allowances.

chapter_title: CORPORATION, STANDING COMMITTEE AND MEDICAL BENEFIT COUNCIL
title: Appointment of a Director General and a Financial Commissioner
text: (1) The Central Government, in consultation with the Corporation, may appoint a Director General and a Financial Commissioner. (2) The Director General is the Corporation's Chief Executive Officer.

sub_structure.3: Both are whole-time officers and may not undertake unconnected work without sanction of the Central Government and the Corporation.
sub_structure.4: Each holds office for up to five years as specified in the appointment order, and is eligible for reappointment if otherwise qualified.
sub_structure.5: Their salary and allowances are prescribed by the Central Government.
sub_structure.6: A person subject to a section 13 disqualification cannot be appointed or continue as Director General or Financial Commissioner.
sub_structure.7: The Central Government may remove either from office at any time, and must do so if recommended by a two-thirds majority resolution of the Corporation at a special meeting.

plain_english_summary: Establishes the Corporation's top executive posts-Director General (CEO) and Financial Commissioner-with fixed tenure up to five years, whole-time obligations, and a removal mechanism including mandatory removal on a two-thirds Corporation vote.

chapter_title: CORPORATION, STANDING COMMITTEE AND MEDICAL BENEFIT COUNCIL
title: Staff
text: (1) The Corporation may employ staff necessary for efficient business, but Central Government sanction is required to create any post with maximum monthly salary exceeding the Central Government-prescribed level.

sub_structure.2_a: Recruitment method, salary, discipline and other service conditions of staff are specified in Corporation regulations aligned with corresponding Central Government pay scales, subject to prior Central Government approval for any departure; this does not apply to consultants/specialists engaged on contract.
sub_structure.2_b: In determining corresponding pay scales, the Corporation considers educational qualifications, recruitment method, duties and responsibilities, referring doubtful cases to the Central Government for a final decision.
sub_structure.3: Appointments to posts corresponding to Group A and Group B Central Government posts (other than medical posts) require Union Public Service Commission consultation, except for officiating/temporary appointments up to one year, which confer no claim to regular appointment or seniority credit.
sub_structure.4: Any question whether a post corresponds to a Group A/B Central Government post is referred to, and finally decided by, the Central Government.

plain_english_summary: Governs the Corporation's own staffing-recruitment, pay parity with Central Government scales, UPSC consultation for senior posts, and salary-cap sanctioning-while carving out contract consultants and short-term officiating appointments.

chapter_title: CORPORATION, STANDING COMMITTEE AND MEDICAL BENEFIT COUNCIL
title: Powers of the Standing Committee
text: (1) Subject to the Corporation's general superintendence and control, the Standing Committee administers the Corporation's affairs and may exercise any Corporation power or function.

sub_structure.2: The Standing Committee must submit to the Corporation, for decision, cases and matters specified in regulations.
sub_structure.3: The Standing Committee may, at its discretion, submit any other case or matter for the Corporation's decision.

plain_english_summary: Delegates day-to-day administration of the Corporation to the Standing Committee, subject to overall Corporation control and mandatory referral of certain matters back to the full Corporation.

chapter_title: CORPORATION, STANDING COMMITTEE AND MEDICAL BENEFIT COUNCIL
title: Corporation's power to promote measures for health, etc., of insured persons
text: The Corporation may, in addition to the Act's benefit scheme, promote measures for the health and welfare of insured persons and the rehabilitation/re-employment of disabled or injured insured persons, incurring expenditure from Corporation funds within Central Government-prescribed limits.
plain_english_summary: Allows the Corporation to fund broader health, welfare and rehabilitation initiatives for insured persons beyond the statutory cash/medical benefits, within prescribed spending limits.

chapter_title: CORPORATION, STANDING COMMITTEE AND MEDICAL BENEFIT COUNCIL
title: Meetings of Corporation, Standing Committee and Medical Benefit Council
text: Subject to rules made under the Act, these bodies meet at times and places, and follow procedures for business, as specified in regulations made in this behalf.
plain_english_summary: Leaves meeting logistics and procedure for the Corporation, Standing Committee and Medical Benefit Council to be governed by regulations.

chapter_title: CORPORATION, STANDING COMMITTEE AND MEDICAL BENEFIT COUNCIL
title: Supersession of the Corporation and Standing Committee
text: (1) If the Central Government considers that the Corporation or Standing Committee persistently defaults on its duties or abuses its powers, it may, by notification, supersede the Corporation, or (in consultation with the Corporation) the Standing Committee, after giving a reasonable show-cause opportunity.

sub_structure.2: On publication of a supersession notification, all members of the superseded body are deemed to have vacated office.
sub_structure.3: A superseded Standing Committee is immediately reconstituted under section 8.
sub_structure.4: On superseding the Corporation, the Central Government may appoint new members under section 4 (and constitute a new Standing Committee under section 8), or appoint an agency to exercise the Corporation's powers and functions for a period it thinks fit.
sub_structure.5: A full report of any supersession action, and the circumstances leading to it, must be laid before Parliament within three months of the superseding notification.

plain_english_summary: Empowers the Central Government to dissolve and replace the Corporation or Standing Committee for persistent default or abuse of power, following due process, with mandatory parliamentary reporting.

chapter_title: CORPORATION, STANDING COMMITTEE AND MEDICAL BENEFIT COUNCIL
title: Duties of Medical Benefit Council
text: The Medical Benefit Council must (a) advise the Corporation and Standing Committee on medical benefit administration, certification for benefits, and connected matters; (b) exercise prescribed investigative powers over complaints against medical practitioners regarding treatment/attendance; and (c) perform other regulation-specified duties connected with medical treatment and attendance.
plain_english_summary: Defines the Medical Benefit Council's advisory and investigative role in the medical side of the ESI scheme.

chapter_title: CORPORATION, STANDING COMMITTEE AND MEDICAL BENEFIT COUNCIL
title: Duties of Principal Officers
text: The Director General and the Financial Commissioner exercise such powers and discharge such duties as may be prescribed, and perform other regulation-specified functions.
plain_english_summary: Leaves the detailed powers and duties of the Director General and Financial Commissioner to be fixed by rules and regulations.

chapter_title: CORPORATION, STANDING COMMITTEE AND MEDICAL BENEFIT COUNCIL
title: Acts of Corporation, etc., not invalid by reason of defect in constitution, etc.
text: No act of the Corporation, Standing Committee or Medical Benefit Council is invalid merely because of a defect in the body's constitution, a member's disqualification or irregular appointment/election, or because the act was done during a vacancy in membership.
plain_english_summary: Protects the validity of official acts against technical challenges based on constitutional defects, member disqualification, or vacancies.

chapter_title: CORPORATION, STANDING COMMITTEE AND MEDICAL BENEFIT COUNCIL
title: Regional Boards, Local Committees, Regional and Local Medical Benefit Councils
text: The Corporation may appoint Regional Boards, Local Committees and Regional/Local Medical Benefit Councils in specified areas and manner, delegating to them such powers and functions as provided by regulations.
plain_english_summary: Allows the Corporation to decentralise administration through regional and local bodies with delegated powers.

title: Employees' State Insurance Fund
text: (1) All contributions and other moneys received on the Corporation's behalf are paid into the Employees' State Insurance Fund, held and administered by the Corporation for the Act's purposes.

sub_structure.2: The Corporation may accept grants, donations and gifts from Government, local authorities, or any individual/body for the Act's purposes.
sub_structure.3: Subject to the Act and rules/regulations, all Fund moneys are paid into the Reserve Bank of India or another Central Government-approved bank, to the credit of the Fund's account.
sub_structure.4: That account is operated by officers authorised by the Standing Committee with Corporation approval.

plain_english_summary: Creates the central ESI Fund into which all contributions and donations flow, held in the Reserve Bank of India (or an approved bank) and operated under authorised officers.

title: [Omitted]
text: Omitted by the Employees' State Insurance (Amendment) Act, 1966, with effect from 17-6-1967. (Formerly dealt with grants by the Central Government.)
plain_english_summary: This section, which previously provided for Central Government grants to the Fund, has been omitted.

title: Purposes for which the Fund may be expended
text: Subject to the Act and Central Government rules, the Fund may be expended only for listed purposes.

sub_structure.i: Payment of benefits and provision of medical treatment/attendance to insured persons (and their families where medical benefit is extended), including related charges and costs.
sub_structure.ii: Fees and allowances to members of the Corporation, Standing Committee, Medical Benefit Council, Regional Boards, Local Committees, and Regional/Local Medical Benefit Councils.
sub_structure.iii: Salaries, allowances, gratuities, pensions and benefit-fund contributions for Corporation officers/servants, and expenditure on offices/services implementing the Act.
sub_structure.iv: Establishment and maintenance of hospitals, dispensaries and other institutions and medical/ancillary services for insured persons (and families where extended).
sub_structure.v: Payments to State Governments, local authorities, or private bodies/individuals towards the cost of medical treatment for insured persons (and families), including buildings and equipment, under agreements.
sub_structure.vi: Cost of auditing the Corporation's accounts and valuing its assets and liabilities.
sub_structure.vii: Cost of the Employees' Insurance Courts set up under the Act.
sub_structure.viii: Payments under contracts entered into for the Act's purposes by the Corporation, Standing Committee, or authorised officers.
sub_structure.ix: Payments under court/tribunal decrees, orders or awards, or compromises/settlements, arising from Corporation-related claims.
sub_structure.x: Costs of instituting or defending civil or criminal proceedings arising from action taken under the Act.
sub_structure.xi: Expenditure, within prescribed limits, on health/welfare measures and rehabilitation/re-employment of disabled or injured insured persons.
sub_structure.xii: Other purposes authorised by the Corporation with prior Central Government approval.

plain_english_summary: Provides an exhaustive list of the purposes for which the ESI Fund can be spent-benefits, staff costs, hospitals, litigation, audits, and welfare measures-ensuring the Fund is used strictly for scheme-related expenditure.

title: Administrative expenses
text: The types of expenses termed 'administrative expenses' and the percentage of the Corporation's income that may be spent on them are prescribed by the Central Government, and the Corporation must keep administrative expenses within that limit.
plain_english_summary: Caps how much of the Corporation's income can go toward administrative overhead, as fixed by the Central Government.

title: Holding of property, etc.
text: (1) The Corporation may, subject to Central Government conditions, acquire, hold, sell or transfer movable/immovable property and do all things necessary for its purposes.

sub_structure.2: Subject to Central Government conditions, the Corporation may invest surplus moneys and re-invest or realise such investments.
sub_structure.3: The Corporation may, with prior Central Government sanction and on prescribed terms, raise and discharge loans.
sub_structure.4: The Corporation may constitute provident or other benefit funds for its staff.

plain_english_summary: Gives the Corporation ordinary corporate powers-owning and dealing in property, investing surplus funds, raising loans, and running staff benefit funds-subject to Central Government oversight.

title: Vesting of the property in the Corporation
text: All property acquired before the Corporation's establishment vests in the Corporation, and related income and expenditure are brought into the Corporation's books.
plain_english_summary: Transfers pre-establishment property and associated accounts into the newly formed Corporation.

title: [Omitted]
text: Omitted by the Employees' State Insurance (Amendment) Act, 1966, with effect from 17-6-1967. (Formerly treated Central Government expenditure as a loan.)
plain_english_summary: This section, which previously treated certain Central Government expenditure as a loan to the Corporation, has been omitted.

title: Budget estimates
text: The Corporation must annually frame a budget of probable receipts and proposed expenditure for the following year and submit it for Central Government approval by a fixed date, containing provisions the Central Government considers adequate for liabilities and a working balance.
plain_english_summary: Requires the Corporation to prepare and submit an annual budget for Central Government approval, ensuring adequate provision for liabilities and reserves.

title: Accounts
text: The Corporation must maintain correct accounts of income and expenditure in such form and manner as prescribed by the Central Government.
plain_english_summary: Imposes a basic accounting obligation on the Corporation in the prescribed form.

title: Audit
text: (1) The Corporation's accounts are audited annually by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India, with the Corporation bearing his audit expenses.

sub_structure.2: The CAG and persons appointed by him have the same rights, privileges and authority in this audit as in auditing Government accounts, including demanding production of books/vouchers/documents and inspecting Corporation offices.
sub_structure.3: The certified accounts and audit report are forwarded to the Corporation, which forwards them to the Central Government along with its comments on the CAG's report.

plain_english_summary: Places the Corporation's accounts under statutory CAG audit, with full CAG powers of inspection and document demand, and a requirement for the Corporation to respond formally to the audit report.

title: Annual report
text: The Corporation must submit to the Central Government an annual report of its work and activities.
plain_english_summary: Requires an annual activity report to be submitted to the Central Government.

title: Budget, audited accounts and the annual report to be placed before Parliament
text: The annual report, audited accounts (together with the CAG's report and the Corporation's comments under section 34), and the finally adopted budget are placed before Parliament.
plain_english_summary: Ensures parliamentary oversight by requiring the Corporation's key financial and activity documents to be tabled before Parliament.

title: Valuation of assets and liabilities
text: The Corporation must, at intervals of three years, have its assets and liabilities valued by a Central Government-approved valuer.

sub_structure.proviso: The Central Government may direct a valuation at other times it considers necessary.

plain_english_summary: Mandates periodic (three-yearly) professional valuation of the Corporation's assets and liabilities, with Central Government power to order additional valuations.

title: All employees to be insured
text: Subject to the Act, all employees in factories or establishments to which the Act applies must be insured in the manner provided by the Act.
plain_english_summary: States the basic mandate: every covered employee must be insured under the ESI scheme.

title: Contributions
text: (1) The contribution for an employee comprises the employer's contribution and the employee's contribution, both paid to the Corporation.

sub_structure.2: Contributions are paid at Central Government-prescribed rates, which cannot exceed the rates in force immediately before the 1989 Amendment Act.
sub_structure.3: The wage period is the unit for which all contributions are payable.
sub_structure.4: Contributions for each wage period ordinarily fall due on its last day; for part-period or multi-employer employment, regulations specify the due date.
sub_structure.5_a: If the principal employer fails to pay a contribution by its due date, he is liable for simple interest at 12% per annum (or a higher regulation-specified rate, capped at the scheduled bank lending rate) until actual payment.
sub_structure.5_b: Such interest is recoverable as an arrear of land revenue or under sections 45C-45-I.

plain_english_summary: Establishes the dual (employer + employee) contribution structure, ties contributions to the 'wage period' unit, and imposes interest (minimum 12% p.a.) for late payment by the principal employer.

title: Principal employer to pay contributions in the first instance
text: (1) The principal employer must pay both the employer's and the employee's contribution for every employee, whether directly employed or through an immediate employer.

sub_structure.2: The principal employer may recover the employee's contribution from a directly employed (non-exempted) employee only by deduction from wages, limited to the amount and period the contribution relates to.
sub_structure.3: Neither the principal employer nor immediate employer may deduct or recover the employer's contribution from an employee's wages, despite any contrary contract.
sub_structure.4: Sums deducted from wages are deemed entrusted to the principal employer by the employee for paying the contribution.
sub_structure.5: The principal employer bears the cost of remitting contributions to the Corporation.

plain_english_summary: Places primary responsibility on the principal employer to pay both contribution shares, allowing recovery of only the employee's share via wage deduction (never the employer's share), and treats deducted amounts as held in trust for the Corporation.

title: Recovery of contribution from immediate employees
text: (1) A principal employer who has paid contributions for an employee engaged through an immediate employer may recover the full amount (employer's and employee's contribution) from the immediate employer, by deduction from any amount owed to him or as a debt.

sub_structure.1A: The immediate employer must maintain a prescribed register of employees engaged through him and submit it to the principal employer before settlement of amounts under sub-section (1).
sub_structure.2: The immediate employer may then recover the employee's contribution from the employee by wage deduction only, subject to the section 40(2) proviso conditions.

plain_english_summary: Lets the principal employer pass the full contribution cost down to the immediate employer (contractor), who can in turn recover only the employee's share from the actual worker via wage deduction.

title: General provisions as to payment of contributions
text: (1) No employee's contribution is payable for an employee whose average daily wages during a wage period are below the Central Government-prescribed level.

sub_structure.1_explanation: Average daily wages are calculated in the manner prescribed by the Central Government.
sub_structure.2: Contribution (both shares) is payable by the principal employer for each wage period for which wages are payable to the employee, and not otherwise.

plain_english_summary: Exempts very low-wage employees from the employee-side contribution (while the employer contribution still applies), and ties contribution liability strictly to periods wages are actually payable.

title: Method of payment of contributions
text: Subject to the Act, the Corporation may make regulations on any matter relating to payment and collection of contributions, including the manner and timing of payment, use of adhesive/impressed stamps, deadlines for evidence of payment, entries in books/cards, and issue/custody/replacement of such books or cards.
plain_english_summary: Delegates the operational details of how contributions are physically paid and recorded to Corporation regulations.

title: Employers to furnish returns and maintain registers in certain cases
text: (1) Every principal and immediate employer must submit to the Corporation (or its designated officer) prescribed returns about persons employed and the relevant factory/establishment.

sub_structure.2: If the Corporation has reason to believe a required return was not submitted for a factory/establishment, it may require the person in charge to furnish particulars needed to decide if the Act applies.
sub_structure.3: Every principal and immediate employer must maintain prescribed registers/records for the factory/establishment.

plain_english_summary: Imposes reporting and record-keeping obligations on employers, with a fallback information-demand power where the Corporation suspects non-compliance.

title: Social Security Officers, their functions and duties
text: (1) The Corporation may appoint persons as inspectors (Social Security Officers) with assigned local jurisdiction limits.

sub_structure.2_a: A Social Security Officer may require a principal/immediate employer to furnish necessary information.
sub_structure.2_b: He may enter, at reasonable times, any office/establishment/factory/premises occupied by such an employer to examine and require production of relevant accounts, books and documents, or require information.
sub_structure.2_c: He may examine, on relevant matters, the employer, his agent/servant, or any person found on the premises reasonably believed to be or have been an employee.
sub_structure.2_d: He may copy or extract from any relevant register, account book or document.
sub_structure.2_e: He may exercise such other powers as may be prescribed.
sub_structure.3: A Social Security Officer exercises functions and performs duties authorised by the Corporation or specified in regulations.
sub_structure.4: An authorised Corporation officer may carry out re-inspection or test inspection of records/returns to verify inspection quality.

plain_english_summary: Empowers appointed Social Security Officers (formerly 'Inspectors') with entry, examination, and document-copying powers to verify employer compliance, plus a quality-check mechanism via re-inspection.

title: Determination of contributions in certain cases
text: (1) Where returns/particulars/registers/records are not submitted/maintained under section 44, or a Social Security Officer is prevented from exercising functions under section 45, the Corporation may, on available information, determine by order the contributions payable for that factory/establishment's employees.

sub_structure.1_proviso1: No such order can be passed without giving the principal/immediate employer or person in charge a reasonable hearing.
sub_structure.1_proviso2: No such order can cover a period beyond five years from the date the contribution became payable.
sub_structure.2: An order under sub-section (1) is sufficient proof of the Corporation's claim under section 75, or for recovery as an arrear of land revenue under section 45B or under sections 45C-45-I.

plain_english_summary: Allows the Corporation to assess contributions using best-available information where an employer fails to comply with reporting duties or obstructs inspection, subject to a hearing requirement and a five-year lookback limit.

title: Appellate authority
text: An employer dissatisfied with a section 45A order may appeal, within sixty days, to a regulation-specified appellate authority, after depositing 25% of the ordered contribution or the employer's own calculated contribution, whichever is higher.

sub_structure.proviso: If the employer ultimately succeeds in the appeal, the Corporation must refund the deposit with regulation-specified interest.

plain_english_summary: Creates a statutory appeal route against best-judgment contribution determinations, conditioned on a partial pre-deposit that is refunded with interest if the appeal succeeds.

title: Recovery of contributions
text: Any contribution payable under this Act may be recovered as an arrear of land revenue.
plain_english_summary: Gives contributions the enforcement status of land-revenue arrears for recovery purposes.

title: Issue of certificate to the Recovery Officer
text: (1) Where an amount is in arrear, the authorised officer may issue a certificate to the Recovery Officer specifying the arrears, who then recovers it from the factory/establishment or employer by attachment and sale of property, arrest and detention of the employer, or appointing a receiver.

sub_structure.1_proviso: Attachment and sale is first effected against the factory/establishment's property; only if insufficient does the Recovery Officer proceed against the employer's personal property.
sub_structure.2: The authorised officer may issue a certificate even if recovery by other modes is already underway.

plain_english_summary: Sets up a certificate-based recovery mechanism giving the Recovery Officer strong enforcement tools-property attachment/sale, arrest, or receivership-with employer assets targeted only after establishment assets prove insufficient.

title: Recovery officer to whom certificate is to be forwarded
text: (1) The authorised officer forwards the section 45C certificate to the Recovery Officer with jurisdiction over the employer's business/establishment location, residence, or property location.

sub_structure.2: If property spans multiple Recovery Officer jurisdictions and the current Recovery Officer cannot fully recover the amount or considers it necessary to expedite recovery, he may forward the certificate (or a certified copy for a partial amount) to another Recovery Officer having jurisdiction, who then proceeds as if he had received the original certificate.

plain_english_summary: Determines which Recovery Officer handles a given case based on location of business, property or residence, with a mechanism to involve multiple Recovery Officers when assets are spread across jurisdictions.

title: Validity of certificate and amendment thereof
text: (1) Once a certificate is issued to a Recovery Officer, the employer cannot dispute the correctness of the amount, or raise any other objection, before the Recovery Officer.

sub_structure.2: Despite the certificate's issue, the authorised officer retains power to withdraw it or correct clerical/arithmetical mistakes by intimating the Recovery Officer.
sub_structure.3: The authorised officer must intimate the Recovery Officer of any withdrawal, cancellation, correction, or amendment made under section 45F(4).

plain_english_summary: Prevents the employer from re-litigating the amount before the Recovery Officer while preserving the authorised officer's power to correct or withdraw the certificate.

title: Stay of proceedings under certificate and amendment or withdrawal thereof
text: (1) Despite a certificate's issue, the authorised officer may grant time for payment, requiring the Recovery Officer to stay proceedings until that time expires.

sub_structure.2: The authorised officer must keep the Recovery Officer informed of payments made or time granted after the certificate's issue.
sub_structure.3: If an order giving rise to the certified demand is modified (reducing the demand) in a pending further proceeding, the authorised officer must stay recovery of the reduced portion while that proceeding is pending.
sub_structure.4: Once such a further proceeding becomes final and the demand is reduced, the authorised officer must amend or withdraw the certificate accordingly.

plain_english_summary: Provides flexibility to pause or adjust certificate-based recovery proceedings where payment time is granted or the underlying demand is under appeal or reduced.

title: Other modes of recovery
text: (1) Notwithstanding a certificate's issue under section 45C, the Director General or an authorised officer may recover the amount by other modes provided in this section.

sub_structure.2: If a third party owes money to the defaulting factory/establishment/employer, that third party may be required to deduct and pay over the arrears due, subject to Civil Procedure Code attachment exemptions.
sub_structure.3: The Director General/authorised officer may issue garnishee-type notices to any person holding or owing money to the employer, compelling payment up to the arrears amount, with provisions for joint accounts, notice copies to the employer, mandatory compliance, sworn objections, amendment/revocation of notices, receipts discharging liability, personal liability for non-compliance or false objections, and default enforcement as if it were an arrear.
sub_structure.4: The Director General/authorised officer may apply to a court holding money belonging to the employer for payment of the amount due.
sub_structure.5: If authorised by the Central Government, the Director General or a Corporation officer may recover arrears by distraint and sale of movable property as laid down in the Third Schedule to the Income-tax Act, 1961.

plain_english_summary: Supplements certificate-based recovery with additional tools-garnishee notices on third parties (banks, debtors), court applications, and distraint/sale of movable property-mirroring income-tax recovery machinery.

title: Application of certain provisions of the Income-tax Act
text: The Second and Third Schedules to the Income-tax Act, 1961 and the Income-tax (Certificate Proceedings) Rules, 1962 apply with necessary modifications to arrears of contributions, interest or damages under this Act, as if referring to income-tax, with 'assessee' read as the factory/establishment/employer.
plain_english_summary: Borrows the entire income-tax recovery-certificate machinery (schedules and rules) for enforcing ESI arrears, adapting terminology accordingly.

title: Definitions
text: For sections 45C to 45H: (a) 'authorised officer' means the Director General, Insurance Commissioner, Joint Insurance Commissioner, Regional Director, or another Central Government-notified officer; (b) 'Recovery Officer' means a Central/State Government or Corporation officer notified by the Central Government to exercise Recovery Officer powers.
plain_english_summary: Defines the two key official roles-'authorised officer' and 'Recovery Officer'-used throughout the certificate-recovery chapter.

title: Benefits
text: (1) Subject to the Act, insured persons, their dependants or other specified persons are entitled to: (a) sickness benefit-periodical payments for certified sickness; (b) maternity benefit-periodical payments for confinement, miscarriage, or sickness arising from pregnancy/confinement/premature birth/miscarriage, on certification; (c) disablement benefit-periodical payments for certified disablement from an employment injury; (d) dependants' benefit-periodical payments to dependants of an insured person who dies from an employment injury; (e) medical benefit-medical treatment and attendance; and (f) funeral expenses-a capped payment to the eldest surviving family member (or whoever incurs the expense) for funeral costs, claimed within three months of death (extendable).

sub_structure.2: The Corporation may, at the appropriate Government's request and subject to regulation conditions, extend medical benefits to an insured person's family.

plain_english_summary: Lists the six core benefits of the ESI scheme-sickness, maternity, disablement, dependants', medical, and funeral expenses-forming the heart of what insured persons and their families receive in exchange for contributions.

title: [Omitted]
text: Omitted by the Employees' State Insurance (Amendment) Act, 1966, with effect from 28-1-1968. (Formerly on when a person is eligible for sickness benefit.)
plain_english_summary: This section, formerly setting sickness-benefit eligibility conditions directly in the Act, has been omitted (now governed by prescribed rules under section 49).

title: [Omitted]
text: Omitted by the Employees' State Insurance (Amendment) Act, 1966, with effect from 28-1-1968. (Formerly on when a person is deemed available for employment.)
plain_english_summary: This section, formerly addressing deemed availability for employment, has been omitted.

title: Sickness benefit
text: The qualification of a person to claim sickness benefit, the conditions subject to which it may be given, and its rates and period, are as prescribed by the Central Government.
plain_english_summary: Delegates the detailed eligibility, conditions, rates and duration of sickness benefit entirely to Central Government rules.

title: Maternity benefit
text: The qualification of an insured woman to claim maternity benefit, the conditions subject to which it may be given, and its rates and period, are as prescribed by the Central Government.
plain_english_summary: Delegates the detailed eligibility, conditions, rates and duration of maternity benefit entirely to Central Government rules.

title: Disablement benefit
text: Subject to the Act: (a) a person with temporary disablement of not less than three days (excluding the accident day) is entitled to periodical payment at Central Government-prescribed rates, periods and conditions; (b) a person with permanent disablement (total or partial) is similarly entitled at prescribed rates, periods and conditions.
plain_english_summary: Grants periodical cash payments for both temporary disablement (minimum 3 days) and permanent disablement (total or partial), with the specifics left to Central Government rules.

title: Presumption as to accident arising in course of employment
text: An accident arising in the course of an employee's employment is presumed, absent contrary evidence, to have also arisen out of that employment.
plain_english_summary: Creates a rebuttable presumption favouring the employee: if an accident happened during work, it is presumed work-related unless proven otherwise.

title: Accidents happening while acting in breach of regulations, etc.
text: An accident is deemed to arise out of and in the course of employment even if the employee was, at the time, acting in breach of applicable law or employer instructions, or without instructions, provided (a) the accident would otherwise have been deemed so to arise, and (b) the act was done for the purpose of and in connection with the employer's trade or business.
plain_english_summary: Protects employees from losing coverage merely because they technically violated a rule or acted without specific instructions, as long as they were still acting in furtherance of the employer's business.

title: Accidents happening while travelling in employer's transport
text: (1) An accident while an employee travels as a passenger (with the employer's express or implied permission) in a vehicle to or from work is deemed work-related if the accident would have been so deemed had travel been obligatory, and the vehicle was operated by or for the employer (or arranged by the employer) and not run as ordinary public transport.

sub_structure.2: 'Vehicle' in this section includes a vessel and an aircraft.

plain_english_summary: Extends employment-injury coverage to accidents on employer-arranged transport to/from work, even where using that transport was not compulsory, so long as it wasn't ordinary public transport.

title: Accidents happening while meeting emergency
text: An accident to an employee in or about their workplace premises is deemed work-related if it happens while the employee is responding to an actual or supposed emergency to rescue, help or protect persons who are or may be injured/imperilled, or to avert or minimise serious property damage.
plain_english_summary: Covers employees injured while heroically responding to emergencies at the workplace, even if such rescue action wasn't strictly part of their job duties.

title: Accidents happening while commuting to the place of work and vice versa
text: An accident during an employee's commute from residence to workplace (or back) is deemed to have arisen out of and in the course of employment if a nexus is established between the circumstances, time and place of the accident and the employment.
plain_english_summary: Extends coverage to commuting accidents (not just employer-provided transport) where a genuine connection between the commute and the employment can be shown.

title: Dependant's benefit
text: (1) If an insured person dies from an employment injury (whether or not he was receiving temporary disablement payments for it), dependants' benefit is payable at Central Government-prescribed rates, periods and conditions to dependants under section 2(6A)(i), (ia) and (ii).

sub_structure.2: If the deceased leaves no such dependants, the benefit is paid to other dependants under section 2(6A), at prescribed rates, periods and conditions.

plain_english_summary: Provides periodical payments to the family of an employee who dies from a work-related injury, prioritising the closest dependants and extending to others if none of the primary category survive.

title: Occupational disease
text: (1) An employee in a Part A Third Schedule employment who contracts a disease specified as an occupational disease for that employment, or in a Part B employment for a continuous period of at least six months, or in a Part C employment for a Corporation-specified continuous period, who contracts the corresponding specified disease, is deemed (unless proven otherwise) to have suffered an 'employment injury' arising out of and in the course of employment.

sub_structure.2_i: If the Central/State Government adds an employment description to Schedule III of the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923, that description and its associated occupational diseases are deemed added to the Third Schedule here.
sub_structure.2_ii: The Corporation may also, after three months' notice by notification, add employment descriptions and specify associated occupational diseases to the Third Schedule, applying the Act as if they had been originally declared.
sub_structure.3: Save as provided above, no benefit is payable for a disease unless directly attributable to a specific injury by accident arising out of and in the course of employment.
sub_structure.4: Section 51A's presumption does not apply to cases under this section.

plain_english_summary: Creates a presumption that certain listed diseases contracted in specified employments (after minimum exposure periods for Parts B and C) are work-related 'employment injuries', without requiring proof of a specific accident, while allowing the disease list to be expanded by notification.

title: Bar against receiving or recovery of compensation or damages under any other law
text: An insured person or dependants cannot receive or recover, from the employer or anyone else, compensation or damages under the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 or any other law, for an employment injury covered under this Act.
plain_english_summary: Prevents double recovery by barring parallel compensation claims (e.g., under workmen's compensation law) once ESI covers the same employment injury.

title: Determination of question of disablement
text: Questions on whether an accident resulted in permanent disablement, whether loss of earning capacity can be assessed provisionally or finally, whether an assessment is provisional or final, and (for provisional assessments) the period the assessment holds good, are determined by a medical board constituted under regulations, collectively termed the 'disablement question'.
plain_english_summary: Routes technical medical/disability questions to a specialised medical board rather than ordinary adjudicators.

title: References to medical boards and appeals to medical appeal tribunals and Employees' Insurance Courts
text: (1) A permanent disablement benefit case is referred by the Corporation to a medical board to determine the disablement question; if loss of earning capacity is provisionally assessed, it must be referred again before the provisional period ends.

sub_structure.2: If the insured person or Corporation is dissatisfied with the medical board's decision, either may appeal, within prescribed time and manner, to a medical appeal tribunal (with a further appeal right to the Employees' Insurance Court) or directly to the Employees' Insurance Court.
sub_structure.2_proviso1: No appeal lies for an insured person who has already commuted the disablement benefit based on the medical board's decision and received the commuted value.
sub_structure.2_proviso2: No appeal lies for the Corporation if it has already paid the commuted value based on the medical board's decision.

plain_english_summary: Creates a two-tier appeal structure (medical appeal tribunal, then Employees' Insurance Court, or directly to the Court) for disputing medical board decisions on disablement, subject to a finality bar once commutation has occurred.

title: Review of decisions by medical board or medical appeal tribunal
text: (1) A medical board or medical appeal tribunal decision may be reviewed at any time by that body if satisfied, on fresh evidence, that the decision resulted from non-disclosure or misrepresentation of a material fact (fraudulent or not).

sub_structure.2: An assessment of disablement extent may also be reviewed by a medical board if satisfied there has been substantial, unforeseen aggravation since the assessment, provided review is needed to avoid substantial injustice given the assessment period and probable aggravation duration.
sub_structure.3: Except with medical appeal tribunal leave, an assessment cannot be reviewed under sub-section (2) on an application made less than five years (or six months for a provisional assessment) after the assessment; a revised assessment excludes any period before the application date.
sub_structure.4: A medical board handling a review may deal with it as it would an original reference, including making a provisional assessment even if the reviewed assessment was final, with section 54A applying to review applications and decisions as it applies to original disablement-benefit cases.

plain_english_summary: Allows correction of medical board/tribunal decisions where fraud or misrepresentation is later discovered, and permits reopening of disablement assessments where the injury has substantially worsened, subject to timing safeguards.

title: Review of dependants' benefit
text: (1) Any decision awarding dependants' benefit may be reviewed at any time by the Corporation if satisfied, on fresh evidence, that it resulted from non-disclosure/misrepresentation, or that it is no longer in accordance with the Act due to a birth, death, marriage, re-marriage, cesser of infirmity, or a claimant turning eighteen.

sub_structure.2: On such review, the Corporation may direct that the benefit be continued, increased, reduced or discontinued.

plain_english_summary: Allows dependants' benefit awards to be revisited when family circumstances change (birth, death, marriage, coming of age) or when the original decision was based on false information.

title: Medical benefit
text: (1) An insured person (or, where extended, a family member) whose condition requires medical treatment and attendance is entitled to medical benefit.

sub_structure.2: Medical benefit may be given as out-patient treatment, home visits, or in-patient treatment in a hospital or institution.
sub_structure.3: A person is entitled to medical benefit during any period contributions are payable, or during which he is qualified for sickness/maternity benefit, or is receiving disablement benefit that does not disentitle him under regulations.
sub_structure.3_proviso1: A person for whom contributions cease to be payable may still be allowed medical benefit for a regulation-specified period and nature.
sub_structure.3_proviso2: An insured person who leaves insurable employment due to permanent disablement continues (on payment of contribution and prescribed conditions) to receive medical benefit until the date he would have reached superannuation age.
sub_structure.3_proviso3: An insured person who has attained superannuation age, and their spouse, remain eligible for medical benefit on payment of contribution and prescribed conditions.
sub_structure.explanation: 'Superannuation' means the age fixed in the person's service contract/conditions for vacating insurable employment, or age 60 if no such age is fixed and the person is no longer in insurable employment.

plain_english_summary: Defines entitlement to medical treatment-covering active contributors, sickness/maternity-eligible persons, and extending continued medical benefit (with contribution) to those permanently disabled out of employment, and to superannuated insured persons and their spouses.

title: Scale of medical benefit
text: (1) An insured person and (where extended) their family are entitled only to medical benefit of the kind and scale provided by the State Government or Corporation, with no right to treatment beyond what the allotted dispensary/hospital/clinic provides or regulations allow.

sub_structure.2: Nothing in the Act entitles an insured person or their family to reimbursement from the Corporation for medical expenses, except as regulations provide.

plain_english_summary: Limits medical benefit to what is actually provided through allotted facilities or regulations, with no general right to reimbursement for self-funded treatment.

title: Provision of medical treatment by State Government
text: (1) The State Government must provide reasonable medical, surgical and obstetric treatment for insured persons (and, where extended, their families) in the State.

sub_structure.1_proviso: With Corporation approval, the State Government may arrange treatment at medical practitioners' clinics on agreed scale and terms.
sub_structure.2: If sickness benefit payments in a State exceed the all-India average, the excess cost is shared between the Corporation and State Government as agreed, though the Corporation may waive the State's share.
sub_structure.3: The Corporation may agree with a State Government on the nature/scale of treatment (including buildings, equipment, medicines, staff) and cost-sharing, including sharing of excess sickness incidence costs.
sub_structure.4: In default of agreement, an arbitrator (a sitting or former High Court Judge appointed by the Chief Justice of India) determines the treatment extent and cost-sharing proportion, binding on both parties.
sub_structure.5: With prior Central Government approval, a State Government may establish its own organisation (in addition to the Corporation) to provide sickness/maternity/employment-injury benefits, with Act references to 'State Government' then including that organisation.
sub_structure.6: That organisation's structure, functions, powers and activities are as prescribed.

plain_english_summary: Establishes State Governments as the primary medical-care providers under the ESI scheme (with Corporation cost-sharing for excess sickness incidence), including an arbitration mechanism for disputes and provision for States to set up dedicated ESI-medical organisations.

title: Establishment and maintenance of hospitals, etc., by Corporation
text: (1) The Corporation, with State Government approval, may establish and maintain hospitals, dispensaries and other medical/surgical services in a State for insured persons (and families, where extended).

sub_structure.2: The Corporation may agree with local authorities, private bodies or individuals on providing medical treatment in any area and sharing costs.
sub_structure.3: The Corporation may also agree with local authorities/bodies for commissioning and running ESI hospitals through third-party participation.

plain_english_summary: Allows the Corporation to directly run its own medical infrastructure (with State approval) or partner with local authorities and private/third parties to deliver medical benefit.

title: Provision of medical benefit by the Corporation in lieu of State Government
text: (1) Notwithstanding other provisions, the Corporation may, in consultation with the State Government, take over responsibility for providing medical benefit (including to families, where extended) in a State, with the State sharing the cost as agreed.

sub_structure.2: Where the Corporation exercises this power, medical-benefit provisions apply as if references to the State Government were references to the Corporation.

plain_english_summary: Allows the Corporation to step into the State Government's shoes for delivering medical benefit directly, by mutual agreement on cost-sharing.

title: Medical and para-medical education
text: The Corporation may establish medical colleges, nursing colleges and training institutes for its para-medical staff and other employees, to improve the quality of ESI scheme services.
plain_english_summary: Lets the Corporation build its own educational institutions to train medical and para-medical staff for the ESI system.

title: Benefit not assignable or attachable
text: (1) The right to receive any benefit payment under the Act is not transferable or assignable. (2) No cash benefit under the Act is liable to attachment or sale in execution of any court decree or order.
plain_english_summary: Protects ESI benefits from being sold, transferred, or seized to satisfy the beneficiary's debts.

title: Bar of benefits under other enactments
text: A person entitled to any Act benefit cannot also receive any similar benefit admissible under any other enactment.
plain_english_summary: Prevents claiming duplicate similar benefits under other laws once entitled under this Act.

title: Persons not to commute cash benefits
text: Save as regulations may provide, no person is entitled to commute for a lump sum any disablement benefit admissible under the Act.
plain_english_summary: Generally prevents converting periodical disablement benefit into a one-time lump sum, except as regulations specifically allow.

title: Persons not entitled to receive benefit in certain cases
text: Save as regulations may provide, no person is entitled to sickness benefit or temporary disablement benefit for any day on which he works, is on leave/holiday for which he receives wages, or is on strike.
plain_english_summary: Blocks sickness/temporary-disablement benefit for days when the person is actually working, receiving paid leave/holiday wages, or on strike, avoiding double compensation.

title: Recipients of sickness or disablement benefit to observe conditions
text: A person receiving sickness benefit or (non-permanent) disablement benefit must (a) remain under prescribed medical treatment and follow the treating officer's instructions; (b) not do anything while under treatment that might retard recovery; (c) not leave the treatment area without permission; and (d) submit to examination by an authorised medical officer or other authorised person.
plain_english_summary: Imposes behavioural conditions on benefit recipients-cooperating with treatment, not undermining recovery, staying within the treatment area, and submitting to check-ups-to maintain entitlement.

title: Benefits not to be combined
text: (1) An insured person cannot receive, for the same period, both sickness and maternity benefit, both sickness and temporary disablement benefit, or both maternity and temporary disablement benefit.

sub_structure.2: Where entitled to more than one such benefit, the person may choose which to receive.

plain_english_summary: Prevents stacking of overlapping cash benefits for the same period, letting the claimant choose the applicable one.

title: [Omitted]
text: Omitted by the Employees' State Insurance (Amendment) Act, 1966, with effect from 17-6-1967. (Formerly on the Corporation's right to recover damages from employer in certain cases.)
plain_english_summary: This section, which previously allowed the Corporation to recover damages from an employer in certain circumstances, has been omitted.

title: [Omitted]
text: Omitted by the Employees' State Insurance (Amendment) Act, 1966, with effect from 17-6-1967. (Formerly on the Corporation's right to be indemnified in certain cases.)
plain_english_summary: This section, which previously gave the Corporation an indemnity right in certain cases, has been omitted.

title: Corporation's rights where a principal employer fails or neglects to pay any contribution
text: (1) If a principal employer fails/neglects to pay a due contribution, causing an employee to lose or receive a lower benefit, the Corporation may pay the person the full benefit they would otherwise have received, and recover from the employer either (i) the difference between what was actually paid and what the actual contributions justified, or (ii) twice the unpaid contribution, whichever is greater.

sub_structure.2: The recoverable amount may be recovered as an arrear of land revenue or under sections 45C-45-I.

plain_english_summary: Protects employees from losing benefits due to their employer's contribution default, while penalising the defaulting employer by recovering the shortfall (or double the unpaid amount, whichever is more).

title: Liability of owner or occupier of factories, etc., for excessive sickness benefit
text: (1) Where the Corporation considers sickness incidence excessive due to insanitary factory/establishment conditions (or employer neglect of health regulations) or insanitary tenements/lodgings occupied by insured persons (due to owner neglect), it may claim the extra sickness-benefit expenditure from the owner/occupier, referring unresolved claims to the appropriate Government.

sub_structure.2: If the Government finds a prima facie case, it appoints a person or persons to hold an inquiry.
sub_structure.3: If the inquiry proves the excess sickness is due to the owner's/occupier's default or neglect, the inquiry officer(s) determine the extra expenditure amount and who must pay it to the Corporation.
sub_structure.4: Such a determination is enforceable as a civil court money decree.
sub_structure.5: 'Owner' of tenements/lodgings includes the owner's agent and any person entitled to collect rent as the owner's lessee.

plain_english_summary: Lets the Corporation recover extra sickness-benefit costs traceable to an employer's or landlord's neglect of health regulations, through a formal inquiry process culminating in a civilly enforceable determination.

title: Repayment of benefit improperly received
text: (1) A person who receives any benefit or payment without lawful entitlement must repay its value/amount to the Corporation; on death, the representative must repay from the deceased's assets, if any.

sub_structure.2: The value of non-cash benefits received is determined by a regulation-specified authority, whose decision is final.
sub_structure.3: The recoverable amount may be recovered as an arrear of land revenue or under sections 45C-45-I.

plain_english_summary: Requires repayment of wrongly received benefits, with enforcement as land-revenue arrears, including from a deceased recipient's estate.

title: Benefit payable up to and including day of death
text: Except as provided in the section 50 proviso, if a person dies during a period for which they are entitled to a cash benefit, the amount up to and including the day of death is paid to the person nominated in writing (as regulations specify), or, absent nomination, to the heir or legal representative.
plain_english_summary: Ensures cash benefit accrued up to the date of death is paid to a nominee or legal heir rather than being forfeited.

title: Employer not to reduce wages, etc.
text: No employer may, merely because of liability for Act contributions, directly or indirectly reduce an employee's wages, or (except as regulations provide) discontinue or reduce service-condition benefits similar to those conferred by this Act.
plain_english_summary: Prevents employers from offsetting their ESI contribution liability by cutting wages or withdrawing comparable existing benefits.

title: Employer not to dismiss or punish employee during period of sickness, etc.
text: (1) No employer may dismiss, discharge, reduce, or otherwise punish an employee while receiving sickness or maternity benefit; nor (except as regulations provide) while receiving temporary disablement benefit, under medical treatment for sickness, or absent due to certified pregnancy/confinement-related illness rendering them unfit for work.

sub_structure.2: Any dismissal/discharge/reduction notice given during the protected period is invalid and inoperative.

plain_english_summary: Protects employees from adverse employment action while they are on ESI-covered sickness, maternity, or disablement-related leave, voiding any notice of dismissal given during that protected window.

title: Definitions
text: In this Chapter: (a) 'other beneficiaries' means persons other than those insured under the Act; (b) 'Scheme' means a Central Government scheme under section 73B for medical facility to other beneficiaries; (c) 'underutilised hospital' means a hospital not fully utilised by insured persons; (d) 'user charges' means the amount chargeable to other beneficiaries for medical facilities, as notified by the Corporation in consultation with the Central Government.
plain_english_summary: Defines the key terms used to extend ESI hospital facilities, on a paid basis, to people outside the insured-person scheme.

title: Power to frame Scheme
text: Notwithstanding anything else in the Act, the Central Government may, by notification, frame a Scheme for other beneficiaries and their families to receive medical facilities at any underutilised Corporation-established hospital, on payment of user charges.
plain_english_summary: Empowers the Central Government to open up spare capacity at ESI hospitals to non-insured persons for a fee.

title: Collection of user charges
text: User charges collected from other beneficiaries are deemed to be contributions and form part of the Employees' State Insurance Fund.
plain_english_summary: Folds the user-charge revenue from non-insured patients into the main ESI Fund, treating it like a contribution.

title: Scheme for other beneficiaries
text: The Scheme may provide for which other beneficiaries are covered, the time and manner of availing medical facilities, the form for furnishing personal/family particulars, and any other matter necessary for implementing the Scheme.
plain_english_summary: Sets out the range of operational matters the Central Government's Scheme for other beneficiaries may address.

title: Power to amend Scheme
text: The Central Government may, by notification, add to, amend, vary or rescind the Scheme.
plain_english_summary: Gives the Central Government ongoing flexibility to modify or cancel the other-beneficiaries Scheme.

title: Laying of Scheme framed under this Chapter
text: Every Scheme framed under this Chapter must be laid before each House of Parliament for a total of thirty days (in one or more sessions); if both Houses agree to modify or annul it before the following session ends, the Scheme has effect only as modified, or ceases to have effect, without prejudice to anything previously done under it.
plain_english_summary: Subjects the other-beneficiaries Scheme to the same parliamentary laying and modification/annulment procedure used for delegated legislation elsewhere in the Act.

title: Constitution of Employees' Insurance Court
text: (1) The State Government, by notification, constitutes an Employees' Insurance Court for a specified local area.

sub_structure.2: The Court consists of as many Judges as the State Government thinks fit.
sub_structure.3: A person who is or has been a judicial officer, or a legal practitioner of five years' standing, is qualified to be a Judge.
sub_structure.4: The State Government may appoint the same Court for multiple local areas, or multiple Courts for the same area.
sub_structure.5: Where multiple Courts serve the same area, the State Government may regulate business distribution between them by order.

plain_english_summary: Establishes specialised Employees' Insurance Courts, staffed by judicial officers or experienced legal practitioners, to adjudicate ESI disputes at the local level.

title: Matters to be decided by Employees' Insurance Court
text: (1) Disputes on whether a person is an 'employee' or liable for the employee's contribution, wage/average-daily-wage rate, contribution rate, identity of the principal employer, a person's right to benefit (amount/duration), a section 55A dependants'-benefit review direction, or other disputes between principal employer and Corporation, principal and immediate employer, or a person/employee and the Corporation/employer over contributions, benefits or dues, are decided by the Employees' Insurance Court.

sub_structure.2: The Court also decides claims for recovery of contributions from the principal employer, claims by a principal employer against an immediate employer, claims against a principal employer under section 68, claims under section 70 for improperly received benefits, and any claim for recovery of an admissible benefit.
sub_structure.2A: If a 'disablement question' arises in Court proceedings without a medical board/tribunal decision, the Court directs the Corporation to obtain that decision and then proceeds in accordance with it, except where a section 54A(2) appeal is already before the Court, in which case the Court may itself decide all issues.
sub_structure.2B: A principal employer cannot raise a contribution/dues dispute with the Corporation before the Court unless he has deposited 50% of the amount claimed, though the Court may waive or reduce this for recorded reasons.
sub_structure.3: No Civil Court has jurisdiction over matters that the Act assigns to a medical board, medical appeal tribunal, or the Employees' Insurance Court.

plain_english_summary: Defines the Employees' Insurance Court's broad jurisdiction over the full range of ESI disputes-status, wages, contribution rates, benefit entitlement, and recovery claims-excluding ordinary civil courts, and imposing a 50% pre-deposit condition on employer-side contribution disputes.

title: Institution of proceedings, etc.
text: (1) Subject to the Act and State Government rules, proceedings before the Employees' Insurance Court are instituted in the Court for the local area where the insured person was working when the dispute arose.

sub_structure.2: If the Court finds a matter can be more conveniently handled by another Employees' Insurance Court in the same State, it may transfer it, forwarding the relevant records.
sub_structure.3: The State Government may transfer a pending matter to a Court in another State, with that State's consent.
sub_structure.4: A Court receiving a transferred matter continues proceedings as if originally instituted there.

plain_english_summary: Fixes venue rules for ESI Court proceedings and allows for both intra-State and inter-State transfer of cases for convenience.

title: Commencement of proceedings
text: (1) Proceedings before an Employees' Insurance Court commence by application.

sub_structure.1A: Every application must be made within three years from when the cause of action arose. For a benefit claim, the cause of action arises only when the claim is made in accordance with regulations, within twelve months of it becoming due (or a further period the Court allows on reasonable grounds); for the Corporation's contribution-recovery claim against a principal employer, the cause of action arises when the Corporation first makes the claim, but no claim can be made more than five years after the relevant period; for a principal employer's claim against an immediate employer, the cause of action arises only when evidence of contribution payment is due to be received by the Corporation under regulations.
sub_structure.2: Every application must be in the prescribed form, contain prescribed particulars, and be accompanied by any prescribed fee, per State Government rules made in consultation with the Corporation.

plain_english_summary: Sets a three-year limitation period for ESI Court applications, with specific rules on when the 'cause of action' is deemed to arise for benefit claims, Corporation recovery claims (capped at five years back), and employer-to-employer claims.
