sub_structure.5: (5) If a worker does not in any one calendar year take the whole of the leave allowed to him under sub-section (1) or sub-section (2), as the case may be, any leave not taken by him shall be added to the leave to be allowed to him in the succeeding calendar year: Provided that the total number of days of leave that may be carried forward to a succeeding year shall not exceed thirty in the case of an adult or forty in the case of a child: Provided further that a worker, who has applied for leave with wages but has not been given such leave in accordance with any scheme laid down in sub-sections (8) and (9) or in contravention of sub-section (10) shall be entitled to carry forward the leave refused without any limit.
sub_structure.6: (6) A worker may at any time apply in writing to the manager of a factory not less than fifteen days before the date on which he wishes his leave to begin, to take all the leave or any portion thereof allowable to him during the calendar year: Provided that the application shall be made not less than thirty days before the date on which the worker wishes his leave to begin, if he is employed in a public utility service as defined in clause (ii) of section 2 of the Industrial Disputes Act. 1947 (14 of 1947): Provided further that the number of times in which leave may be taken during any year shall not exceed three.
sub_structure.7: (7) If a worker wants to avail himself of the leave with wages due to him to cover a period of illness, he shall be granted such leave even if the application for leave is not made within the time specified in sub-section (6); and in such a case wages as admissible under section 81 shall be paid not later than fifteen days, or in the case of a public utility service not later than thirty days from the date of the application for leave.
sub_structure.8: (8) For the purpose of ensuring the continuity of work, the occupier or manager of the factory, in agreement with the Works Committee of the factory constituted under section 3 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (14 of 1947), or a similar Committee constituted under any other Act or if there is no such Works Committee or a similar Committee in the factory, in agreement with the representatives of the workers therein chosen in the prescribed manner, may lodge with the Chief Inspector a scheme in writing whereby the grant of leave allowable under this section may be regulated.
sub_structure.9: (9) A scheme lodged under sub-section (8) shall be displayed at some conspicuous and convenient places in the factory and shall be in force for a period of twelve months from the date on which it comes into force, and may thereafter be renewed with or without modification for a further period of twelve months at a time, by the manager in agreement with the Works Committee or a similar Committee, or as the case may be, in agreement with the representatives of the workers as specified in sub-section (8), and a notice of renewal shall be sent to the Chief Inspector before it is renewed.
sub_structure.10: (10) An application for leave which does not contravene the provisions of sub-section (6) shall not be refused, unless refusal is in accordance with the scheme for the time being in operation under sub-sections (8) and (9).
sub_structure.11: (11) If the employment of a worker who is entitled to leave under sub-section (1) or sub-section (2), as the case may be, is terminated by the occupier before he has taken the entire leave to which he is entitled, or if having applied for and having not been granted such leave, the worker quits his employment, before he has taken the leave, the occupier of the factory shall pay him the amount payable under section 80 in respect of the leave not taken, and such payment shall be made, where the employment of the worker is terminated by the occupier, before the expiry of the second working day after such termination, and where a worker who quits his employment, on or before the next pay day.
sub_structure.12: (12) The unavailed leave of a worker shall not be taken into consideration in computing the period of any notice required to be given before discharge or dismissal.

plain_english_summary: Entitles a worker who has worked 240+ days in a calendar year to earned annual leave (roughly 1 day per 20 days worked for adults, per 15 days for children), with detailed rules on accrual, carry-forward, and encashment on termination.

title: Wages during leave period
text: (1) For the leave allowed to him under section 78 or section 79, as the case may be, a worker shall be entitled to wages at a rate equal to the daily average of his total full time earnings for the days on which he actually worked during the month immediately preceding his leave, exclusive of any overtime and bonus but inclusive of dearness allowance and the cash equivalent of the advantage accruing through the concessional sale to the worker of food grains and other articles: Provided that in the case of a worker who has not worked on any day during the calendar month immediately preceding his leave, he shall be paid at a rate equal to the daily average of his total full time earnings for the days on which he actually worked during the last calendar month preceding his leave, in which he actually worked, exclusive of any overtime and bonus but inclusive of dearness allowance and the cash equivalent of the advantage accruing through the concessional sale to the workers of food grains and other articles.

sub_structure.2: (2) The cash equivalent of the advantage accruing through the concessional sale to the worker of food grains and other articles shall be computed as often as may be prescribed, on the basis of the maximum quantity of food grains and other articles admissible to a standard family. Explanation 1.—“Standard family” means a family consisting of a worker, his or her spouse and two children below the age of fourteen years requiring in all three adult consumption units. Explanation 2.—“Adult consumption unit” means the consumption unit of a male above the age of fourteen years; and the consumption unit of a female above the age of fourteen years and that of a child below the age of fourteen years shall be calculated at the rates of 8 and 6 respectively of one adult consumption unit.
sub_structure.3: (3) The State Government may make rules prescribing— (a) the manner in which the cash equivalent of the advantage accruing through the concessional sale to a worker of food grains and other articles shall be computed; and (b) the registers that shall be maintained in a factory for the purpose of securing compliance with the provisions of this section.

plain_english_summary: Sets the wage rate payable during annual leave, generally the worker's average daily earnings, including dearness allowance and cash equivalents of concessions, but excluding overtime.

title: Payment in advance in certain cases
text: A worker who has been allowed leave for not less than four days, in the case of an adult, and five days, in the case of a child, shall, before his leave begins be paid the wages due for the period of the leave allowed.
plain_english_summary: Requires advance payment of leave wages before leave begins, where the leave taken is at least four days (adult) or five days (child).

title: Mode of recovery of unpaid wages
text: Any sum required to be paid by an employer, under his Chapter but not paid by him shall be recoverable as delayed wages under the provisions of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 (4 of 1936).
plain_english_summary: Provides that unpaid leave wages are recoverable as delayed wages under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936.

title: Power to make rules
text: The State Government may make rules directing managers of factories to keep registers containing such particulars as may be prescribed and requiring the registers to be made available for examination by Inspectors.
plain_english_summary: Allows the State Government to require factories to keep prescribed leave registers available for Inspector examination.

title: Power to exempt factories
text: Where the State Government is satisfied that the leave rules applicable to workers in a factory provide benefits which in its opinion are not less favourable than those for which this Chapter makes provision it may, by written order; exempt the factory from all or any of the provisions of this Chapter subject to such conditions as may be specified in the order. Explanation.—For the purposes of this section, in deciding whether the benefits which are provided for by any leave rules are less favourable than those for which this Chapter makes provision, or not, the totality of the benefits shall be taken into account.
plain_english_summary: Lets the State Government exempt a factory from this Chapter where its own leave rules are at least as favourable to workers.

title: Power to apply the act to certain premises
text: (1) The State Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, declare that all or any of the provisions of this Act shall apply to any place wherein a manufacturing process is carried on with or without the aid of power or is so ordinarily carried on, notwithstanding that— (i) the number of persons employed therein is less than ten, if working with the aid of power and less than twenty if working without the aid of power, or (ii) the persons working therein are not employed by the owner thereof but are working with the permission of, or under agreement with, such owner: Provided that the manufacturing process is not being carried on by the owner only with the aid of his family.

sub_structure.2: (2) After a place is so declared, it shall be deemed to be a factory for the purposes of this Act, and the owner shall be deemed to be the occupier, and any person working therein, a worker. Explanation.—For the purposes of this section, “owner” shall include a lessee or mortgage with possession of the premises.

plain_english_summary: Allows the State Government to extend some or all provisions of the Act to smaller manufacturing premises not otherwise meeting the statutory definition of a factory.

title: Power to exempt public institutions
text: The State Government may exempt, subject to such conditions as it may consider necessary, any workshop or workplace where a manufacturing process is carried on and which is attached to a public institution maintained for the purposes of education, training, research or reformation, from all or any of the provisions of this Act: Provided that no exemption shall be granted from the provisions relating to hours of work and holidays, unless the persons having the control of the institution submit, for the approval of the State Government, a scheme for the regulation of the hours of employment, intervals for meals, and holidays of the persons employed in or attending the institution or who are inmates of the institution, and the State Government is satisfied that the provisions of the scheme are not less favourable than the corresponding provisions of this Act.
plain_english_summary: Allows the State Government to exempt workshops attached to certain public institutions (for technical training, not for private profit) from the Act.

title: Dangerous operations
text: Where the State Government is of opinion that any manufacturing process or operation carried on in a factory exposes any persons employed in it to a serious risk of bodily injury, poisoning or disease, it may make rules applicable to any factory or class or description of factories in which the manufacturing process or operation is carried on— (a) specifying the manufacturing process or operation and declaring it to be dangerous; (b) prohibiting or restricting the employment of women, adolescents or children in the manufacturing process or operation; (c) providing for the periodical medical examination of persons employed, or seeking to be employed, in the manufacturing process or operation, and prohibiting the employment or persons not certified as fit for such employment and requiring the payment by the occupier of the factory of fees for such medical examination; (d) providing for the protection of all persons employed in the manufacturing process or operation or in the vicinity of the places where it is carried on; (e) prohibiting, restricting or controlling the use of any specified materials or processes in connection with the manufacturing process or operation; (f) requiring the provision of additional welfare amenities and sanitary facilities and the supply of protective equipment and clothing, and laying down the standards thereof, having regard to the dangerous nature of the manufacturing process or operation. * * * * *
plain_english_summary: Lets the State Government make special rules for factories carrying on processes that pose a serious risk of injury, poisoning or disease, including restricting who may work there.

title: Power to prohibit employment on account of serious hazard
text: (1) Where it appears to the Inspector that conditions in a factory or part thereof are such that they may cause serious hazard by way of injury or death to the persons employed therein or to the general public in the vicinity, he may, by order in writing to the occupier of the factory, state the particulars in respect of which he considers the factory or part thereof to be the cause of such serious hazard and prohibit such occupier from employing any person in the factory or any part thereof other than the minimum number of persons necessary to attend to the minimum tasks till the hazard is removed.

sub_structure.2: (2) Any order issued by the Inspector under sub-section (1) shall have effect for a period of three days until extended by the Chief Inspector by a subsequent order.
sub_structure.3: (3) Any person aggrieved by an order of the Inspector under sub-section (1), and the Chief Inspector under sub-section (2), shall have the right to appeal to the High Court.
sub_structure.4: (4) Any person whose employment has been affected by an order issued under sub-section (1), shall be entitled to wages and other benefits and it shall be the duty of the occupier to provide alternative employment to him wherever possible and in the manner prescribed.
sub_structure.5: (5) The provisions of sub-section (4) shall be without prejudice to the rights of the parties under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (14 of 1947).

plain_english_summary: Allows an Inspector to prohibit employment in a factory area where conditions create a serious hazard of injury or death to workers or the public, until remedied.

title: Notice of certain accidents
text: 1 (1) Where in any factory an accident occurs which causes death, or which causes any bodily injury by reason of which the person injured is prevented from working for a period of forty-eight hours or more immediately following the accident, or which is of such nature as may be prescribed in this behalf, the manager of the factory shall send notice thereof to such authorities, and in such form and within such time, as may be prescribed. (2) Where a notice given under sub-section (1) relates to an accident causing death, the authority to whom the notice is sent shall make an inquiry into the occurrence within one month of the receipt of the notice or, if such authority is not the Inspector, cause the Inspector to make an inquiry within the said period. (3) The State Government may make rules for regulating the procedure at inquiries under this section.
plain_english_summary: Requires the manager to notify authorities of accidents causing death or disabling injury of 48+ hours, and dangerous occurrences, in the prescribed form and timeframe.

title: Notice of certain dangerous occurrences
text: Where in a factory any dangerous occurrence of such nature as may be prescribed occurs, whether causing any bodily injury or disability or not, the manager of the factory shall send notice thereof to such authorities, and in such form and within such time, as may be prescribed.
plain_english_summary: Requires notice to be sent to prescribed authorities of any dangerous occurrence of a specified kind, whether or not it causes injury.

title: Notice of certain diseases
text: (1) Where any worker in a factory contracts any disease specified in the Third Schedule, the manager of the factory shall send notice thereof to such authorities, and in such form and within such time, as may be prescribed.

sub_structure.2: (2) If any medical practitioner attends on a person who is or has been employed in a factory, and who is, or is believed by the medical practitioner to be, suffering from any disease specified in the Third Schedule, the medical practitioner shall without delay send a report in writing to the office of the Chief Inspector stating— (a) the name and full postal address of the patient, (b) the disease from which he believes the patient to be suffering, and (c) the name and address of the factory in which the patient is, or was last, employed.
sub_structure.3: (3) Where the report under sub-section (2) is confirmed to the satisfaction of the Chief Inspector, by the certificate of a certifying surgeon or otherwise, that the person is suffering from a disease specified in the Third Schedule, he shall pay to the medical practitioner such fee as may be prescribed, and the fee so paid shall be recoverable as an arrear of land-revenue from the occupier of the factory in which the person contracted the disease.
sub_structure.4: (4) If any medical practitioner fails to comply with the provisions of sub-section (2), he shall be punishable with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees.
sub_structure.5: (5) The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, add to or alter the Third Schedule and any such addition or alteration shall have effect as if it had been made by this Act.

plain_english_summary: Requires the manager to notify prescribed authorities when a worker contracts a disease listed in the Third Schedule, and a medical practitioner treating such a case must also report it.

title: Power to direct enquiry into cases of accident or disease
text: (1) The State Government may, if it considers it expedient so to do, appoint a competent person to inquire into the causes of any accident occurring in a factory or into any case where a disease specified in the Third Schedule has been, or is suspected to have been contracted in a factory, and may also appoint one or more persons possessing legal or special knowledge to act as assessors in such inquiry.

sub_structure.2: (2) The person appointed to hold an inquiry under this section shall have all the powers of a Civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (5 of 1908), for the purposes of enforcing the attendance of witnesses and compelling the production of documents and material objects, and may also, so far as may be necessary for the purposes of the inquiry, exercise any of the powers of an Inspector under this Act; and every person required by the person making the inquiry to furnish any information shall be deemed to be legally bound so to do within the meaning of section 176 of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860).
sub_structure.3: (3) The person holding an inquiry under this section shall make a report to the State Government stating the causes of the accident, or as the case may be, disease, and any attendant circumstances, and addition any observations which he or any of the assessors may think fit to make.
sub_structure.4: (4) The State Government may, if it thinks fit, cause to be published any report made under this section or any extracts therefrom.
sub_structure.5: (5) The State Government may make rules for regulating the procedure at inquiries under this section.

plain_english_summary: Allows the State Government to order an inquiry into the causes of a factory accident or notified disease and to hold a public hearing, with costs recoverable from a person found responsible.

title: Power to take samples
text: (1) An Inspector may at any time during the normal working hours of a factory, after informing the occupier or manager of the factory or other person for the time being purporting to be in charge of the factory, take in the manner hereinafter provided a sufficient sample of any substances used or intended to be used in the factory, such use being— (a) in the belief of the Inspector in contravention of any of the provisions of this Act or the rules made thereunder, or (b) in the opinion of the Inspector likely to cause bodily injury to, or injury to the health of, workers in the factory.

sub_structure.2: (2) Where the Inspector takes a sample under sub-section (1), he shall, in the presence of the person informed under that sub-section unless such person wilfully absents himself, divide the sample into three portions and effectively seal and suitably mark them, and shall permit such person to add his own seal and mark thereto.
sub_structure.3: (3) The person informed as aforesaid shall, if the Inspector so requires, provide the appliances for dividing, sealing and marking the sample taken under this section.
sub_structure.4: (4) The Inspector shall— (a) forthwith give one portion of the sample to the person informed under sub-section (1); (b) forthwith send the second portion to a Government Analyst for analysis and report thereon; (c) retain the third portion for production to the Court before which proceedings, if any, are instituted in respect of the substance.
sub_structure.5: (5) Any document purporting to be a report under the hand of any Government Analyst upon any substance submitted to him for analysis and report under this section, may be used as evidence in any proceedings instituted in respect of the substance.

plain_english_summary: Allows an Inspector to take samples of substances used or handled in a factory for analysis, following a set procedure for notice, sealing, and sharing results with the occupier.

title: Safety and occupational health surveys
text: (1) The Chief Inspector, or the Director General of Factory Advice Service and Labour Institutes, or the Director General of Health Services, to the Government of India, or such other officer as may be authorised in this behalf by the State Government or the Chief Inspector or the Director General of Factory Advice Service and Labour Institutes or the Director General of Health Services may, at any time during the normal working hours of a factory, or at any other time as is found by him to be necessary, after giving notice in writing to the occupier or manager of the factory or any other person who for the time being purports to be in charge of the factory, undertake safety and occupational health surveys, and such occupier or manager or other person shall afford all facilities for such survey, including facilities for the examination and testing of plant and machinery and collection of samples and other data relevant to the survey.

sub_structure.2: (2) For the purpose of facilitating surveys under sub-section (1) every worker shall, if so required by the person conducting the survey, present himself to undergo such medical examination as may be considered necessary by such person and furnish all information in his possession and relevant to the survey.
sub_structure.3: (3) Any time spent by a worker for undergoing medical examination or furnishing information under sub-section (2) shall, for the purpose of calculating wages and extra wages for overtime work, be deemed to be time during which such worker worked in the factory. Explanation.—For the purposes of this section, the report, if any, submitted to the State Government by the person conducting the survey under sub-section (1) shall be deemed to be a report submitted by an Inspector under this Act.

plain_english_summary: Empowers designated officers to conduct occupational safety and health surveys, with occupiers required to provide facilities and information.

title: General penalty for offences
text: Save as is otherwise expressly provided in this Act and subject to the provisions of section 93, if in, or in respect of, any factory there is any contravention of any of the provisions of this Act or of any rules made thereunder or of any order in writing given thereunder, the occupier and manager of the factory shall each be guilty of an offence and punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years or with fine which may extend to one lakh rupees or with both, and if the contravention is continued after conviction, with a further fine which may extend to one thousand rupees for each day on which the contravention is so continued: Provided that where contravention of any of the provisions of Chapter IV or any rule made thereunder or under section 87 has resulted in an accident causing death or serious bodily injury, the fine shall not be less than twenty-five thousand rupees in the case of an accident causing death, and five thousand rupees in the case of an accident causing serious bodily injury. Explanation.—In this section and in section 94 “serious bodily injury” means an injury which involves, or in all probability will involve, the permanent loss of the use of, or permanent injury to, any limb or the permanent loss of, or injury to, sight or hearing, or the fracture of any bone, but shall not include, the fracture of bone or joint (not being fracture of more than one bone or joint) of any phalanges of the hand or foot.
plain_english_summary: Sets the general penalty for breaching the Act or rules: up to two years' imprisonment or a fine up to one lakh rupees (or both), with continuing fines for ongoing breaches and higher minimum fines where a safety breach causes death or serious injury.

title: Liability of owner of premises in certain circumstances
text: (1) Where in any premises separate buildings are leased to different occupiers for use as separate factories, the owner of the premises shall be responsible for the provision and maintenance of common facilities and services, such as approach roads, drainage, water supply, lighting and sanitation.

sub_structure.2: (2) The Chief Inspector shall have, subject to the control of the State Government, power to issue orders to the owner of the premises in respect of the carrying out of the provisions of sub-section (1).
sub_structure.3: (3) Where is any premises, independent or self-containted, floors or flats are leased to different occupiers for use as separate factories, the owner of the premises shall be liable as if he were the occupier or manager of a factory, for any contravention of the provisions of this Act in respect of— (i) latrines, urinals and washing facilities in so far as the maintenance of the common supply of water for these purposes is concerned; (ii) fencing of machinery and plant belonging to the owner and not specifically entrusted to the custody or use of an occupier; (iii) safe means of access to the floors or flats and maintenance and cleanliness of staircases and common passages; (iv) precautions in case of fire; (v) maintenance of hoists and lifts; and (vi) maintenance of any other common facilities provided in the premises.
sub_structure.4: (4) The Chief Inspector shall have, subject to the control of the State Government, power to issue orders to the owner of the premises in respect of the carrying out the provisions of sub-section (3).
sub_structure.5: (5) The provisions of sub-section (3) relating to the liability of the owner shall apply where in any premises independent rooms with common latrines, urinals and washing facilities are leased to different occupiers for use as separate factories: Provided that the owner shall be responsible also for complying with the requirements relating to the provision and maintenance of latrines, urinals and washing facilities.
sub_structure.6: (6) The Chief Inspector shall have, subject to the control of the State Government, the power to issue orders to the owner of the premises referred to in sub-section (5) in respect of the carrying out of the provisions of section 46 or section 48.
sub_structure.7: (7) Where in any premises portions of a room or a shed are leased to different occupiers for use as separate factories, the owner of the premises shall be liable for any contravention of the provisions of— (i) Chapter III, except sections 14 and 15; (ii) Chapter IV, except sections 22, 23, 27, 34, 35 and 36: Provided that in respect of the provisions of sections 21, 24 and 32 the owner's liability shall be only in so far as such provisions relate to things under his control: Provided further that the occupier shall be responsible for complying with the provisions of Chapter IV in respect of plant and machinery belonging to or supplied by him; (iii) section 42.
sub_structure.8: (8) The Chief Inspector shall have, subject to the control of the State Government, power to issue orders to the owner of the premises in respect of the carrying out the provisions of sub-section (7).
sub_structure.9: (9) In respect of sub-sections (5) and (7), while computing for the purposes of any of the provisions of this Act the total number of workers employed, the whole of the premises shall be deemed to be a single factory.

plain_english_summary: Where a building housing separate factories is leased out, makes the building owner (not each occupier) responsible for shared facilities like sanitation and drainage, with liability for breach.

title: Enhanced penalty after previous conviction
text: 1 (1) If any person who has been convicted of any offence punishable under section 92 is again guilty of an offence involving a contravention of the same provision, he shall be punishable on a subsequent conviction with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine which shall not be less than ten thousand rupees but which may extend to two lakh rupees or with both: Provided that the court may, for any adequate and special reasons to be mentioned in the judgment, impose a fine of less than ten thousand rupees: Provided further that where contravention of any of the provisions of Chapter IV or any rule made thereunder or under section 87 has resulted in an accident causing death or serious bodily injury, the fine shall not be less than thirty-five thousand rupees in the case of an accident causing death and ten thousand rupees in the case of an accident causing serious bodily injury. (2) For the purposes of sub-section (1), no cognizance shall be taken of any conviction made more than two years before the commission or the offence for which the person is subsequently being convicted.
plain_english_summary: Increases the penalty (up to 3 years' imprisonment or fine up to Rs 2 lakh, with a minimum fine in most cases) for a repeat conviction of the same offence within two years.

title: Penalty for obstructing Inspector
text: Whoever wilfully obstructs an Inspector in the exercise of any power conferred on him by or under this Act, or fails to produce on demand by an Inspector any registers or other documents in his custody kept in pursuance of this Act or of any rules made thereunder, or conceals or prevents any worker in a factory from appearing before, or being examined by, an Inspector, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees or with both.
plain_english_summary: Penalises anyone who wilfully obstructs an Inspector or refuses to produce required registers/documents, with imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to Rs 10,000.

title: Penalty for wrongfully disclosing results of analysis under section 91
text: Whoever, except in so far as it may be necessary for the purposes of a prosecution for any offence punishable under this Act, publishes or discloses to any person the results of an analysis made under section 91, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees or with both.
plain_english_summary: Penalises unauthorised disclosure of the results of a sample analysis under section 91, with imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to Rs 10,000.

title: Penalty for contravention of the provisions of sections 41B, 41 C and 41 H
text: (1) Whoever Whoever fails to comply with or contravenes any of the provisions of section 41B, 41 C or 41 H or the rules made thereunder, shall, in respect of such failure or contravention, be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years and with fine which may extend to two lakh rupees, and in case the failure or contravention continues, with additional fine which may extend to five thousand rupees for every day during which such failure or contravention continues after the conviction for the first such failure or contravention.

sub_structure.2: (2) If the failure or contravention referred to in sub-section (1) continues beyond a period of one year after the date of conviction, the offender shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years.

plain_english_summary: Sets a stiff penalty (2 to 7 years' imprisonment and fine up to Rs 2 lakh, higher on repeat offence) for breaching the hazardous-process disclosure, responsibility or right-to-warn provisions (sections 41B, 41C, 41H).

title: Offences by workers
text: (1) Subject to the provisions of section 111, if any worker employed in a factory contravenes any provision of this Act or any rules or orders made thereunder, imposing any duty or liability on workers, he shall be punishable with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees.

sub_structure.2: (2) Where a worker is convicted of an offence punishable under sub-section (1) the occupier or manager of the factory shall not be deemed to be guilty of an offence in respect of that contravention, unless it is proved that he failed to take all reasonable measures for its prevention.

plain_english_summary: Makes workers who breach duties or rules imposed on them personally liable to a fine up to Rs 500, subject to the employer's-liability defence in section 111.

title: Penalty for using false certificate of fitness
text: Whoever knowingly uses or attempts to use, as a certificate of fitness granted to himself under section 70, a certificate granted to another person under that section, or who, having procured such a certificate, knowingly allows it to be used, or an attempt to use it to be made, by another person, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two months or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees or with both.
plain_english_summary: Penalises misuse of another person's certificate of fitness, or knowingly making a false statement to obtain one, with imprisonment up to 3 months or fine up to Rs 1,000, or both.

title: Penalty for permitting double employment of child
text: If a child works in a factory on any day on which he has already been working in another factory, the parent or guardian of the child or the person having custody of or control over him or obtaining any direct benefit from his wages, shall be punishable with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, unless it appears to the Court that the child so worked without the consent or connivance of such parent, guardian or person.
plain_english_summary: Makes a parent, guardian or person benefiting from a child's wages liable to a fine up to Rs 50 if the child works in two factories on the same day.

title: Determination of occupier in certain cases
text: Rep. by the Factories (Amendment) Act, 1987 (20 of 1987), s. 38 (w.e.f. 1-12-1987).
plain_english_summary: A former provision on determining the occupier in certain cases; it was repealed by the Factories (Amendment) Act, 1987, with effect from 1 December 1987.

title: Exemption of occupier or manager from liability in certain cases
text: Where the occupier or manager of a factory is charged with an offence punishable under this Act, he shall be entitled, upon complaint duly made by him and on giving to the prosecutor not less than three clear days' notice in writing of his intention so to do, to have any other person whom he charges as the actual offender brought before the Court at time appointed for hearing the charge; and if, after the commission of the offence has been proved, the occupier or manager of the factory, as the case may be, proves to the satisfaction of the Court— (a) that he has used due diligence to enforce the execution of this Act, and (b) that the said other person committed the offence in question without his knowledge, consent or connivance, that other person shall be convicted of the offence and shall be liable to the like punishment as if he were the occupier or manager of the factory, and the occupier or manager, as the case may be, shall be discharged from any liability under this Act in respect of such offence: Provided that in seeking to prove as aforesaid, the occupier or manager of the factory, as the case may be, may be examined on oath, and his evidence and that of any witness whom he calls in his support shall be subject to cross-examination on behalf of the person he charges as the actual offender and by the prosecutor: Provided further that, if the person charged as the actual offender by the occupier or manager cannot be brought before the Court at the time appointed for hearing the charge, the Court shall adjourn the hearing from time to time for a period not exceeding three months and if by the end of the said period the person charged as the actual offenders cannot still be brought before the Court, the Court shall proceed to hear the charge against the occupier or manager and shall, if the offence be proved, convict the occupier or manager.
plain_english_summary: Lets an occupier or manager charged with an offence shift liability to the person actually at fault, if they give timely notice and prove the offence occurred without their knowledge or default.

title: Power of Court to make orders
text: (1) Where the occupier or manager of a factory is convicted of an offence punishable under this Act the Court may, in addition to awarding any punishment, by order in writing require him, within a period specified in the order (which the court may, if it thinks fit and on application in such behalf, from time to time extend) to take such measures as may be so specified for remedying the matters in respect of which the offence was committed.

sub_structure.2: (2) Where an order is made under sub-section (1) the occupier or manager of the factory, as the case may be, shall not be liable under this Act in respect of the continuation of the offence during the period, or extended period, if any, allowed by the Court, but if, on the expiry of such period or extended period, as the case may be, the order or the Court has not been fully complied with, the occupier or manager, as the case may be, shall be deemed to have committed a further offence, and may be sentenced therefore by the Court to undergo imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months or to pay a fine which may extend to one hundred rupees for every day after such expiry on which the order has not been complied with, or both to undergo such imprisonment and to pay such fine, as aforesaid.

plain_english_summary: Allows a convicting court to additionally order the occupier/manager to fix the default within a set time, on pain of a daily fine for continued non-compliance.

title: Presumption as to employment
text: If a person is found in a factory at any time, except during intervals for meals or rest, when work is going on or the machinery is in motion, he shall until the contrary is proved, be deemed for the purposes of this Act and the rules made thereunder to have been at that time employed in the factory.
plain_english_summary: Creates a presumption that anyone found in a factory during working hours, other than meal/rest breaks, is employed there unless proven otherwise.

title: Onus as to age
text: (1) When any act or omission would, if a person were under a certain age, be an offence punishable under this Act, and such person is in the opinion of the Court prima facie under such age, the burden shall be on the accused to prove that such person is no under such age.

sub_structure.2: (2) A declaration in writing by a certifying surgeon relating to a worker that he has personally examined him and believes him to be under the age stated is such declaration shall, for the purposes of this Act and the rules made thereunder, be admissible as evidence of the age of that worker.

plain_english_summary: Where an offence depends on a person being under a certain age, and the court thinks they appear to be under that age, the burden shifts to the accused to prove otherwise.

title: Onus of proving limits of what is practicable, etc
text: In any proceeding for an offence for the contravention of any provision of this Act or rules made thereunder consisting of a failure to comply with a duty or requirement to do something, it shall be for the person who is alleged to have failed to comply with such duty or requirement, to prove that it was not reasonably practicable or, as the case may be, all practicable measures were taken to satisfy the duty or requirement.
plain_english_summary: In prosecutions for failing to do something 'so far as practicable' or similar, puts the burden on the accused to show they did all that was practicable.

title: Cognizance of offences
text: (1) No Court shall take cognizance of any offence under this Act except on complaint by, or with the previous sanction in writing of, an Inspector.

sub_structure.2: (2) No Court below that of a Presidency Magistrate or of a Magistrate of the first class shall try any offence punishable under this Act.

plain_english_summary: Bars courts from taking up a case under the Act except on a complaint made, or sanctioned in writing, by an Inspector (with special rules for worker-caused deaths).

title: Limitation of prosecutions
text: No Court shall take cognizance of any offence punishable under this Act unless complaint thereof is made within three months of the date on which the alleged commission of the offence came to the knowledge of an Inspector: Provided that where the offence consists of disobeying a written order made by an Inspector, complaint thereof may be made within six months of the date on which the offence is alleged to have been committed. Explanation.—For the purposes of this section,— (a) in the case of a continuing offence, the period of limitation shall be computed with reference to every point of time during which the offence continues; (b) where for the performance of any act time is granted or extended on an application made by the occupier or manager of a factory, the period of limitation shall be computed from the date on which the time so granted or extended expired.
plain_english_summary: Sets a three-month limitation period for prosecutions, running from when the Inspector became aware of the alleged offence, subject to special rules for continuing/repeat offences.

title: Jurisdiction of a court for entertaining proceedings, etc., for offence
text: For the purposes of conferring jurisdiction on any court in relation to an offence under this Act or the rules made thereunder in connection with the operation of any plant, the place where the plant is for the time being situate shall be deemed to be the place where such offence has been committed.
plain_english_summary: Fixes jurisdiction for offences connected with the operation of a plant at the place where the plant is located, for cases under this Act or its rules.

title: Appeals
text: (1) The manager of a factory on whom an order in writing by an Inspector has been served under the provisions of this Act or the occupier of the factory may, within thirty days of the service of the order, appeal against it to the prescribed authority, and such authority may, subject to rules made in this behalf by the State Government, confirm, modify or reverse the order.

sub_structure.2: (2) Subject to rules made in this behalf by the State Government (which may prescribe classes of appeals which shall not be heard with the aid of assessors), the appellate authority may, or if so required in the petition of appeal shall, hear the appeal with the aid of assessors, one of whom shall be appointed by the appellate authority and the other by such body representing the industry concerned as may be prescribed: Provided that if no assessor is appointed by such body before the time fixed for hearing the appeal, or if the assessor so appointed fails to attend the hearing at such time, the appellate authority may, unless satisfied that the failure to attend is due to sufficient cause, proceed to hear the appeal without the aid of such assessor or, if it thinks fit, without the aid of any assessor.
sub_structure.3: (3) Subject to such rules as the Stale Government may make in this behalf and subject to such conditions as to partial compliance or the adoption of temporary measures as the appellate authority may in any case think fit to impose, the appellate authority may, if it thinks fit, suspend the order appealed against pending the decision of the appeal.

plain_english_summary: Gives a manager or occupier a right to appeal, within 30 days, to prescribed authorities against certain written orders made by an Inspector.

title: Display of notices
text: (1) In addition to the notices required to be displayed in any factory by or under this Act, there shall be displayed in every factory a notice containing such abstracts of this Act and of the rules made thereunder as may be prescribed and also the name and address of the Inspector and the certifying surgeon.

sub_structure.2: (2) All notices required by or under this Act to be displayed in a factory shall be in English and in a language understood by the majority of the workers in the factory, and shall be displayed at some conspicuous and convenient place at or near the main entrance to the factory, and shall be maintained in a clean and legible condition.
sub_structure.3: (3) The Chief Inspector may, by order in writing served on the manager of any factory, require that there shall be displayed in the factory any other notice or poster relating to the health, safety or welfare of the workers in the factory.

plain_english_summary: Requires display of a notice in the factory containing prescribed abstracts of the Act and rules, along with the name and address of the Inspector and certifying surgeon, in English and a locally understood language.

title: Service of notices
text: The State Government may make rules prescribing the manner of the service of orders under this Act on owners, occupiers or managers of factories.
plain_english_summary: Lets the State Government make rules on how notices and orders under the Act are to be formally served on owners, occupiers or managers.

title: Returns
text: The State Government may make rules requiring owners, occupiers or managers of factories to submit such returns, occasional or periodical, as may in its opinion be required for the purposes of this Act.
plain_english_summary: Lets the State Government require factories to submit occasional or periodical returns needed for administering the Act.

title: Obligations of workers
text: (1) No worker in a factory— (a) shall wilfully interfere with or misuse any appliance, convenience or other thing provided in a factory for the purposes of securing the health, safety or welfare of the workers therein; (b) shall wilfully and without reasonable cause do anything likely to endanger himself or others; and (c) shall wilfully neglect to make use of any appliance or other thing provided in the factory for the purposes of securing the health or safety of the workers therein.

sub_structure.2: (2) If any worker employed in a factory contravenes any of the provisions of this section or of any rule or order made thereunder, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to one hundred rupees, or with both.

plain_english_summary: Prohibits workers from misusing safety equipment, wilfully endangering themselves or others, or refusing to use provided safety appliances; also protects a worker who refuses to work if their right to warn under section 41H is unaddressed.

title: Right of workers, etc
text: Every worker shall have the right to— (i) obtain from the occupier, information relating to workers' health and safety at work, (ii) get trained within the factory wherever possible, or, to get himself sponsored by the occupier for getting trained at a training center or institute, duly approved by the Chief Inspector, where training is imparted for workers' health and safety at work, (iii) represent to the Inspector directly or through his representative in the matter of inadequate provision for protection of his health or safety in the factory.
plain_english_summary: Grants workers rights to safety information, on-site training, prompt notice of hazards, and to raise safety concerns with the occupier, Inspector or Safety Committee.

title: General power to make rules
text: The State Government may make rules providing for any matter which, under any of the provisions of this Act, is to be or may be prescribed or which may be considered expedient in order to give effect to the purposes of this Act.
plain_english_summary: Gives the State Government a broad, general power to make rules on any matter the Act says may or must be prescribed, or that is expedient to carry out the Act's purposes.

title: Powers of Centre to give directions
text: The Central Government may give directions to a State Government to the carrying into execution of the provisions of this Act.
plain_english_summary: Allows the Central Government to direct a State Government on how to carry the Act's provisions into execution.

title: No charge for facilities and conveniences
text: Subject to the provisions of section 46 no fee or charge shall be realised from any worker in respect of any arrangements or facilities to be provided, or any equipments or appliances to be supplied by the occupier under the provisions of this Act.
plain_english_summary: Prohibits charging workers any fee for facilities, equipment or arrangements the occupier is required to provide, other than under the canteen provisions of section 46.

title: Publication of rules
text: 1 (1) All rules made under this Act shall be published in the Official Gazette, and shall be subject to the condition of previous publication; and the date to be specified under clause (3) of section 23 of the General Clauses Act, 1897 (10 of 1897), shall be not less than forty-five days from the date on which the draft of the proposed rules was published. (2) Every rule made by the State Government under this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made, before the State Legislature.
plain_english_summary: Requires rules made under the Act to be published in the Official Gazette, subject to prior-publication requirements, with commencement dates fixed as specified.

title: Application of Act to Government factories
text: Unless otherwise provided this Act shall apply to factories belonging to the Central or any State Government.
plain_english_summary: Applies the Act to factories owned by the Central or State Government unless the Act itself provides otherwise.

title: Protection to persons acting under this Act
text: No suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against any person for anything which is in good faith done or intended to be done under this Act.
plain_english_summary: Protects anyone from suit, prosecution or other legal proceedings for actions done in good faith under the Act.

title: Restrictions on disclosure of information
text: (1) No Inspector shall, while in service or after leaving the service, disclose otherwise than in connection with the execution, or for the purposes, of this Act any information relating to any manufacturing or commercial business or any working process which may come to his knowledge in the course of his official duties.

sub_structure.2: (2) Nothing in sub-section (1) shall apply to any disclosure of information made with the previous consent in writing of the owner of such business or process or for the purposes of any legal proceeding (including arbitration) pursuant to this Act or of any criminal proceeding which may be taken, whether pursuant to this Act or otherwise, or for the purposes of any report of such proceedings as aforesaid.
sub_structure.3: (3) If any Inspector contravenes the provisions of sub-section (1) he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

plain_english_summary: Bars an Inspector, during or after service, from disclosing confidential manufacturing/commercial information they learn in the course of duty, except for enforcing the Act, with limited exceptions.

title: Restriction on disclosure of information
text: (1) Every Inspector shall treat as confidential the source of any complaint brought to his notice on the breach of any provision of this Act.

sub_structure.2: (2) No inspector shall, while making an inspection under this Act, disclose to the occupier, manager or his representative that the inspection is made in pursuance of the receipt of a complaint: Provided that nothing in this sub-section shall apply to any case in which the person who has made the complaint has consented to disclose his name.

plain_english_summary: Requires every Inspector to keep confidential the identity of anyone who complains about a breach of the Act.

title: Act to have effect notwithstanding anything contained in Act 37 of 1970
text: The provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970 or any other law for the time being in force.
plain_english_summary: States that this Act prevails over anything inconsistent in the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970, or any other law.

title: Repeal and savings
text: The enactments set out in the Table appended to this section are hereby repealed: Provided that anything done under the said enactments which could have been done under this Act if it had then been in force shall be deemed to have been done under this Act. TABLE.—Enactments repealed. Rep. by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1950 (35 of 1950), s. 2 and the First Schedule (w.e.f. 10-4-1950.)
plain_english_summary: Repeals the earlier factories enactments listed in the appended Table, while preserving the validity of things already done under them.

title: Short title, extent and commencement
text: This Act may be called the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947. It extends to the whole of India. It shall come into force on the first day of April, 1947.
plain_english_summary: Names the Act, confirms it applies pan-India, and fixes its commencement date as 1 April 1947.

title: Definitions
text: In this Act, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context, the following terms are defined.

sub_structure.a: "appropriate Government" means, in relation to industrial disputes concerning industries carried on by or under the authority of the Central Government, railways, banking or insurance companies, mines, oilfields, major ports, controlled industries, certain public sector corporations or companies in which the Central Government holds not less than 51% of paid-up share capital, the Central Government; and in relation to any other industrial dispute, the State Government.
sub_structure.j: "industry" means any business, trade, undertaking, manufacture or calling of employers and includes any calling, service, employment, handicraft, or industrial occupation or avocation of workmen.
sub_structure.k: "industrial dispute" means any dispute or difference between employers and employers, employers and workmen, or workmen and workmen, connected with employment, non-employment, terms of employment, or conditions of labour of any person.
sub_structure.l: "lock-out" means the temporary closing of a place of employment, or the suspension of work, or the refusal by an employer to continue to employ any number of persons employed by him.
sub_structure.oo: "retrenchment" means the termination by the employer of the service of a workman for any reason whatsoever, otherwise than as a punishment by way of disciplinary action, but does not include voluntary retirement, retirement on superannuation, non-renewal of a fixed-term contract on its expiry, or termination on ground of continued ill-health.
sub_structure.q: "strike" means a cessation of work by a body of persons employed in any industry acting in combination, or a concerted refusal, or a refusal under a common understanding, of any number of persons who are or have been so employed to continue to work or to accept employment.
sub_structure.rr: "wages" means all remuneration capable of being expressed in terms of money payable to a workman in respect of employment, including allowances, value of house accommodation or concessional supplies, and travelling concession, but excluding bonus, employer's PF/pension contributions, and gratuity.
sub_structure.s: "workman" means any person (including an apprentice) employed to do manual, unskilled, skilled, technical, operational, clerical or supervisory work for hire or reward; it excludes persons employed mainly in a managerial or administrative capacity, and supervisory employees drawing wages exceeding ten thousand rupees per month or exercising mainly managerial functions.

plain_english_summary: Defines the Act's core vocabulary. Critically for a startup, 'workman' excludes people in a genuinely managerial/administrative role and excludes supervisors earning over Rs. 10,000/month who mainly perform managerial functions -- so many salaried tech employees may fall outside the Act's protections, while others (e.g., support staff, ops executants) may be covered as 'workmen'. 'Retrenchment' notably does not cover a fixed-term contract simply expiring.

title: Dismissal, etc., of an individual workman to be deemed to be an industrial dispute
text: Where an employer discharges, dismisses, retrenches, or otherwise terminates the services of an individual workman, any dispute connected with or arising out of such action is deemed to be an industrial dispute even though no other workman or union is a party to it. Such a workman may apply directly to the Labour Court or Tribunal for adjudication after 45 days from filing a conciliation application, and the application must be made within three years of the date of discharge, dismissal, retrenchment or termination.

sub_structure.2: A workman may make a direct application to the Labour Court or Tribunal after 45 days from the date the conciliation application was made, without waiting for a government reference.
sub_structure.3: The application under sub-section (2) must be made before the expiry of three years from the date of discharge, dismissal, retrenchment or termination.

plain_english_summary: Even a single employee's dismissal dispute counts as an 'industrial dispute' -- a startup does not need a union or group of employees involved for this Act to apply. The employee can go straight to a Labour Court after a short waiting period, within a 3-year limitation window.

title: Works Committee
text: In any industrial establishment employing 100 or more workmen in the preceding 12 months, the appropriate Government may require the employer to constitute a Works Committee of employer and workmen representatives (workmen representatives not fewer than employer representatives), chosen in consultation with the registered trade union if any. Its duty is to promote amity between employer and workmen and address matters of common interest.
plain_english_summary: Applies only to larger establishments (100+ workmen). It is a joint consultative body for smoothing employer-employee relations, not an adjudicatory body.

title: Conciliation officers
text: The appropriate Government may appoint conciliation officers, charged with mediating in and promoting settlement of industrial disputes, for a specified area, industries, or period.
plain_english_summary: Government-appointed officials who try to mediate and settle disputes before they escalate to litigation.

title: Board of Conciliation
text: The appropriate Government may constitute a Board of Conciliation (an independent chairman plus 2 or 4 members representing the parties) to promote settlement of an industrial dispute.
plain_english_summary: A tripartite conciliation panel that can be set up for a specific dispute.

title: Courts of Inquiry
text: The appropriate Government may constitute a Court of Inquiry (one or more independent persons) to inquire into any matter connected with or relevant to an industrial dispute.
plain_english_summary: A fact-finding body, distinct from adjudicatory Labour Courts/Tribunals.

title: Labour Courts
text: The appropriate Government may constitute one or more Labour Courts for adjudicating industrial disputes relating to matters in the Second Schedule (e.g., legality of an order under standing orders, discharge/dismissal, illegality of strikes/lock-outs). A Labour Court has a single presiding officer meeting prescribed judicial/legal-service qualifications.
plain_english_summary: The primary forum for individual dismissal/discharge disputes and standing-orders disputes that a startup is most likely to face.

title: Tribunals
text: The appropriate Government may constitute one or more Industrial Tribunals for adjudicating disputes relating to any matter in the Second or Third Schedule (e.g., wages, bonus, retrenchment, closure). A Tribunal has one presiding officer meeting prescribed qualifications, and the Government may appoint assessors to advise it.
plain_english_summary: Handles broader/more complex disputes than a Labour Court, including wage structures, bonus, and retrenchment/closure matters.

title: National Tribunals
text: The Central Government may constitute National Industrial Tribunals for disputes of national importance or affecting establishments in more than one State. A National Tribunal has a single presiding officer who must be, or have been, a High Court Judge.
plain_english_summary: Reserved for large, multi-state or nationally significant disputes -- unlikely to be relevant for most single-state startups.

title: Disqualifications for presiding officers
text: No person shall be appointed to, or continue in, the office of presiding officer of a Labour Court, Tribunal or National Tribunal if he is not an independent person or has attained the age of 65 years.
plain_english_summary: Ensures neutrality and an age cap for judges of these labour forums.

title: Qualifications, terms and conditions of service of Presiding Officer
text: After commencement of Part XIV of Chapter VI of the Finance Act, 2017, the qualifications, appointment, tenure, salary and removal of the Presiding Officer of the Industrial Tribunal appointed by the Central Government are governed by section 184 of the Finance Act, 2017, subject to a saving for officers appointed earlier.
plain_english_summary: Administrative/tribunal-reform provision aligning appointment terms with the 2017 tribunal rationalisation reform.

title: Filling of vacancies
text: If a vacancy (other than temporary absence) occurs in the office of a presiding officer, chairman or member of a Board/Court, the Central or appropriate Government shall appoint a replacement, and proceedings continue from the stage at which the vacancy arose.
plain_english_summary: Ensures continuity of pending cases despite a change of judge/member.

title: Finality of orders constituting Boards, etc.
text: Orders appointing the chairman/members of a Board, Court, Labour Court, Tribunal or National Tribunal cannot be challenged merely on the ground of a vacancy or constitutional defect; settlements are not invalidated merely because they were reached after the prescribed reporting period, or because of casual absence of a Board member when the report is signed by the chairman and other members.
plain_english_summary: Protects the validity of settlements and appointments from technical challenges.

title: Notice of change
text: No employer proposing to change conditions of service specified in the Fourth Schedule (e.g., wages, allowances, hours of work, leave, shift working, rules of discipline) may effect the change without giving 21 days' prior notice in the prescribed manner to affected workmen, except where the change follows a settlement/award or applies to civil-service-rules-governed employees.
plain_english_summary: Before a startup can change core terms like wages, hours, or shift patterns for its 'workman'-category employees, it generally must give 21 days' written notice, unless the change flows from an existing settlement/award.

title: Power of Government to exempt
text: Where applying section 9A to a class of establishments/workmen would prejudicially affect employers so as to cause serious repercussion on the industry, and public interest requires it, the appropriate Government may, by notification, exempt that class from section 9A, conditionally or unconditionally.
plain_english_summary: A safety-valve allowing the government to exempt certain industries/employers from the 21-day notice requirement.

title: Setting up of Grievance Redressal Machinery
text: Every industrial establishment employing 20 or more workmen must have one or more Grievance Redressal Committees, with equal employer and workmen representation (up to 6 members total, with proportionate representation for women), to resolve individual grievances within 30 days of a written application. An aggrieved workman may appeal to the employer, who must decide within one month. This does not affect the workman's right to separately raise an industrial dispute, and does not apply where an established grievance mechanism already exists.
plain_english_summary: Any startup with 20+ workmen-category employees must set up an internal grievance committee with joint employer-employee representation, and resolve individual grievances within 30 days -- but employees keep the right to escalate to a full industrial dispute regardless.

chapter_title: REFERENCE OF DISPUTES TO BOARDS, COURTS OR TRIBUNALS
title: Reference of disputes to Boards, Courts or Tribunals
text: Where the appropriate Government is of the opinion that an industrial dispute exists or is apprehended, it may refer the dispute to a Board (for settlement), a Court (for inquiry), a Labour Court (for Second Schedule matters), or a Tribunal (for Second or Third Schedule matters). Where a dispute relates to a public utility service and a strike/lock-out notice has been given, the Government generally must make a reference. The order of reference must specify a time limit for the award (generally 3 months for individual-workman disputes), extendable on application.
plain_english_summary: Disputes generally reach adjudication through a government reference (not the employer or employee directly filing in a labour court, except for individual dismissal disputes under section 2A/10). The reference order sets a deadline for the award.

chapter_title: REFERENCE OF DISPUTES TO BOARDS, COURTS OR TRIBUNALS
title: Voluntary reference of disputes to arbitration
text: Where an industrial dispute exists or is apprehended and the employer and workmen agree, they may, by written agreement (before any reference under section 10), refer the dispute to one or more arbitrators of their choosing, including a sitting Labour Court/Tribunal presiding officer. The agreement must be forwarded to the Government and published in the Official Gazette; the Arbitration Act, 1940 does not apply to such arbitration.
plain_english_summary: Gives a startup and its employees an alternative, mutually agreed private-arbitration route instead of waiting for a government reference -- useful for faster, negotiated dispute resolution.

chapter_title: PROCEDURE, POWERS AND DUTIES OF AUTHORITIES
title: Procedure and powers of conciliation officers, Boards, Courts and Tribunals
text: Conciliation officers, Boards, Courts, Labour Courts, Tribunals and National Tribunals may follow such procedure as they think fit, subject to rules. They have Civil Court-like powers (summoning witnesses, compelling document production, issuing commissions), and their proceedings are deemed judicial proceedings under the Indian Penal Code. Awards/orders are executable like a civil court decree.
plain_english_summary: These bodies are given real teeth -- civil court powers for evidence and enforcement, and their awards are directly executable like a court decree.

chapter_title: PROCEDURE, POWERS AND DUTIES OF AUTHORITIES
title: Power to give appropriate relief in discharge/dismissal cases
text: Where a discharge/dismissal dispute is referred for adjudication and the Labour Court/Tribunal/National Tribunal finds the order unjustified, it may set aside the discharge/dismissal and direct reinstatement on such terms as it thinks fit, or award any lesser punishment or other relief, relying only on the material on record (no fresh evidence).
plain_english_summary: This is a very important provision for startups: if a Labour Court finds a dismissal unjustified, it can order reinstatement of the employee (not just compensation), or impose a lesser penalty instead of the dismissal.

chapter_title: PROCEDURE, POWERS AND DUTIES OF AUTHORITIES
title: Duties of conciliation officers
text: The conciliation officer must investigate the dispute without delay and try to bring about a fair settlement; if settled, a report and signed settlement memorandum go to the Government; if not, a full report on the failure goes to the Government within 14 days (extendable). Based on the report, the Government decides whether to refer the dispute onward.
plain_english_summary: Sets the conciliation timeline (14 days to report) that precedes escalation to adjudication.

chapter_title: PROCEDURE, POWERS AND DUTIES OF AUTHORITIES
title: Duties of Board
text: A Board must investigate the dispute and endeavour to bring about a settlement, reporting to the Government within two months (extendable by up to two months at a time) whether or not settlement was reached.
plain_english_summary: Parallel conciliation duty for the Board of Conciliation, with a longer (2-month) reporting timeline than a conciliation officer.

chapter_title: PROCEDURE, POWERS AND DUTIES OF AUTHORITIES
title: Duties of Courts
text: A Court of Inquiry must inquire into the matters referred to it and report to the appropriate Government, ordinarily within six months of commencing its inquiry.
plain_english_summary: Sets a roughly six-month timeline for fact-finding inquiries.

chapter_title: PROCEDURE, POWERS AND DUTIES OF AUTHORITIES
title: Duties of Labour Courts, Tribunals and National Tribunals
text: Where a dispute is referred for adjudication, the Labour Court/Tribunal/National Tribunal must hold proceedings expeditiously and submit its award to the appropriate Government within the period specified in the referral order (or any extension).
plain_english_summary: Adjudicating bodies must decide and deliver awards within the time frame the government sets in the reference order.

chapter_title: PROCEDURE, POWERS AND DUTIES OF AUTHORITIES
title: Form of report or award
text: A Board/Court report must be in writing and signed by all members (dissenting members may record a minute of dissent). A Labour Court/Tribunal/National Tribunal award must be in writing, signed by the presiding officer.
plain_english_summary: Formal requirements for how reports and awards must be documented.

chapter_title: PROCEDURE, POWERS AND DUTIES OF AUTHORITIES
title: Publication of reports and awards
text: Every Board/Court report, arbitration award, and Labour Court/Tribunal/National Tribunal award must be published by the appropriate Government within 30 days of receipt, in a manner the Government thinks fit. Once published (subject to section 17A), the award is final and cannot be questioned by any Court.
plain_english_summary: Awards only take legal effect once officially published, and thereafter cannot be challenged in ordinary courts (subject to the enforceability rules in section 17A).

chapter_title: PROCEDURE, POWERS AND DUTIES OF AUTHORITIES
title: Commencement of the award
text: An award becomes enforceable 30 days after publication, unless the Government declares (on grounds of national economy or social justice) that it will not become enforceable, in which case the Government may reject or modify it within 90 days and must lay it before the legislature; the award then becomes enforceable per the timelines set out.
plain_english_summary: Gives the government a limited override power to reject or modify an award on macro-economic/public-interest grounds before it takes legal effect -- rarely used but exists as a check.

chapter_title: PROCEDURE, POWERS AND DUTIES OF AUTHORITIES
title: Payment of full wages to workman pending proceedings in higher courts
text: Where an award directs reinstatement and the employer challenges it in the High Court or Supreme Court, the employer must pay the workman full last-drawn wages (inclusive of any admissible allowance) during the pendency of that challenge, provided the workman was not employed elsewhere and files an affidavit to that effect; if the workman was in fact adequately employed elsewhere, the court may deny wages for that period.
plain_english_summary: If a startup appeals a reinstatement order to a higher court, it must generally keep paying the dismissed employee's full wages while the appeal is pending, unless the employee found equivalent work elsewhere.

chapter_title: PROCEDURE, POWERS AND DUTIES OF AUTHORITIES
title: Persons on whom settlements and awards are binding
text: A private settlement (outside conciliation) binds only the signing parties. A settlement reached during conciliation, an enforceable arbitration award (under a notified section 10A(3A) reference), or an enforceable Labour Court/Tribunal/National Tribunal award binds all parties to the dispute, all other parties properly summoned, the employer's heirs/successors/assigns, and -- where the workmen side was a party -- all persons employed in the establishment at the time of dispute and those subsequently employed there.
plain_english_summary: A key point for startups: an award or conciliation settlement can bind not just the specific employees involved but the whole workforce category at the establishment, including future hires, and survives a change in ownership (successors/assigns).

chapter_title: PROCEDURE, POWERS AND DUTIES OF AUTHORITIES
title: Period of operation of settlements and awards
text: A settlement operates from the agreed date (or signing date) and binds parties for the agreed period, or six months by default, continuing until two months' notice of termination is given. An award normally operates for one year from enforceability (extendable up to three years total), unless it imposes no continuing obligation, and continues to bind parties until two months after a termination notice; the Government may refer an award back to the Labour Court/Tribunal to assess if changed circumstances justify shortening it.
plain_english_summary: Settlements and awards are not necessarily permanent -- they have default validity periods and formal termination-notice requirements, which matters for how long a startup remains bound by a wage settlement or award.

chapter_title: PROCEDURE, POWERS AND DUTIES OF AUTHORITIES
title: Commencement and conclusion of proceedings
text: Conciliation proceedings commence when a strike/lock-out notice is received or a Board reference order is made, and conclude on settlement, on report to Government, or on reference to a Court/Labour Court/Tribunal. Arbitration/adjudication proceedings commence on the date of reference and conclude when the award becomes enforceable.
plain_english_summary: Defines the exact start and end points of each stage of the dispute-resolution process, which matters for calculating notice periods and strike/lock-out restrictions.

chapter_title: PROCEDURE, POWERS AND DUTIES OF AUTHORITIES
title: Certain matters to be kept confidential
text: Information about a trade union or an individual business obtained during investigation/inquiry, and requested in writing to be kept confidential, must not be included in any report/award nor disclosed by the officer/members without the written consent of the union secretary or business concerned, except for a prosecution under IPC section 193.
plain_english_summary: Protects sensitive business or union information disclosed during a dispute investigation from being made public without consent.

title: Prohibition of strikes and lock-outs
text: In a public utility service, no workman may strike, and no employer may lock out, without 6 weeks' notice, within 14 days of such notice, before the notified strike/lock-out date, or during conciliation proceedings and 7 days after their conclusion. Notice is not needed if a strike/lock-out already exists, but the employer must intimate the authority. Notices must follow prescribed form and manner, and the employer must report received/given notices within 5 days.
plain_english_summary: If a startup's operations are classified as a 'public utility service' (per the First Schedule), strict 6-week notice and cooling-off requirements apply before either side can strike or lock out.

title: General prohibition of strikes and lock-outs
text: No workman in any industrial establishment may strike, and no employer may lock out, during pendency of Board conciliation proceedings and 7 days after; during pendency of Labour Court/Tribunal/National Tribunal proceedings and 2 months after; during pendency of notified arbitration proceedings and 2 months after; or during the operation of a settlement/award on matters it covers.
plain_english_summary: A general (not just public-utility) ban on strikes/lock-outs while a dispute is actively before conciliation, arbitration, or adjudication, and while a settlement/award is in force on the same matters.

title: Illegal strikes and lock-outs
text: A strike/lock-out is illegal if commenced in contravention of sections 22 or 23, or continued in contravention of a prohibition order under section 10(3) or 10A(4A). A strike/lock-out already in existence when a dispute is referred does not become illegal merely because of the reference, provided it was lawful at commencement and its continuance was not prohibited. A lock-out in response to an illegal strike, or a strike in response to an illegal lock-out, is not itself illegal.
plain_english_summary: Clarifies exactly when a strike or lock-out crosses the line into being 'illegal' -- important because illegal strikes/lock-outs attract criminal penalties under Chapter VI.

title: Prohibition of financial aid to illegal strikes and lock-outs
text: No person may knowingly expend or apply any money in direct furtherance or support of an illegal strike or lock-out.
plain_english_summary: Bans funding illegal strikes/lock-outs, whether by a union, employer body, or third party.

title: Application of sections 25C to 25E
