sub_structure.2: If pregnant, the notice must state the date from which she will be absent, not earlier than six weeks before her expected delivery date.
sub_structure.3: A woman who did not give notice while pregnant may give it as soon as possible after delivery.
sub_structure.4: On receiving the notice, the employer must permit the woman to be absent during the period she receives maternity benefit.
sub_structure.5: The benefit for the pre-delivery period is paid in advance on proof of pregnancy; the amount for the subsequent period is paid within forty-eight hours of proof of delivery.
sub_structure.6: Failure to give notice does not disentitle a woman to maternity benefit if she is otherwise entitled; an Inspector may, suo motu or on her application, order payment within a specified time.

plain_english_summary: Sets out the notice procedure for claiming maternity benefit-when and how a woman must inform her employer-and the payment timeline: advance payment before delivery on proof of pregnancy, and the balance within 48 hours of proof of delivery, with a safety net if the notice formality was missed.

title: Payment of maternity benefit in case of death of a woman
text: If a woman entitled to maternity benefit or any other amount dies before receiving it, or where the employer is liable under the second proviso to section 5(3), the employer must pay the benefit or amount to the person nominated in her section 6 notice, or, if none, to her legal representative.
plain_english_summary: Ensures maternity benefit due to a deceased woman is paid to her nominee, or her legal representative if she named no nominee.

title: Payment of medical bonus
text: (1) Every woman entitled to maternity benefit is also entitled to a medical bonus of one thousand rupees from her employer, if pre-natal confinement and post-natal care is not provided free of charge.

sub_structure.2: The Central Government may, by notification every three years, increase the medical bonus amount, subject to a maximum of twenty thousand rupees.

plain_english_summary: Provides a flat medical bonus (currently Rs 1,000, revisable up to Rs 20,000 by the Central Government) to cover medical care costs, unless the employer already provides free pre- and post-natal care.

title: Leave for miscarriage, etc.
text: In case of miscarriage or medical termination of pregnancy, a woman is entitled, on prescribed proof, to six weeks' leave with wages at the maternity-benefit rate, immediately following the day of the miscarriage or termination.
plain_english_summary: Grants six weeks of paid leave (at the maternity benefit rate) after a miscarriage or medical termination of pregnancy.

title: Leave with wages for tubectomy operation
text: In case of a tubectomy operation, a woman is entitled, on prescribed proof, to two weeks' leave with wages at the maternity-benefit rate, immediately following the day of the operation.
plain_english_summary: Provides two weeks of paid leave following a tubectomy (female sterilisation) operation.

title: Leave for illness arising out of pregnancy, delivery, premature birth, miscarriage, medical termination of pregnancy or tubectomy operation
text: A woman suffering illness arising out of pregnancy, delivery, premature birth of child, miscarriage, medical termination of pregnancy or tubectomy operation is entitled, on prescribed proof, in addition to leave under section 6 or section 9, to leave with wages at the maternity-benefit rate for a maximum period of one month.
plain_english_summary: Adds up to one extra month of paid leave for illness connected to pregnancy, childbirth, miscarriage, medical termination, or tubectomy, on top of the standard maternity or miscarriage leave.

title: Nursing breaks
text: Every woman delivered of a child who returns to duty after delivery is allowed, in addition to her rest interval, two breaks of prescribed duration each day for nursing the child, until the child turns fifteen months old.
plain_english_summary: Guarantees two daily nursing breaks (on top of normal rest breaks) for a returning mother until her child reaches 15 months of age.

title: Crèche facility
text: (1) Every establishment with fifty or more employees must provide a crèche facility within a prescribed distance, either separately or as part of common facilities.

sub_structure.1_proviso: The employer must allow the woman four visits a day to the crèche, which includes her allowed rest interval.
sub_structure.2: Every establishment must intimate every woman in writing and electronically, at the time of her initial appointment, about every benefit available under the Act.

plain_english_summary: Requires larger establishments (50+ employees) to provide an on-site or nearby crèche with guaranteed daily visits for nursing mothers, and mandates that all women be informed in writing and electronically about their Act benefits when hired.

title: Dismissal during absence of pregnancy
text: (1) It is unlawful for an employer to discharge or dismiss a woman during or on account of her absence under this Act, to give notice of discharge/dismissal expiring during such absence, or to vary her service conditions to her disadvantage because of such absence.

sub_structure.2_a: Discharge or dismissal of a pregnant woman at any time during pregnancy does not deprive her of maternity benefit or medical bonus she would otherwise have been entitled to, except that where dismissal is for prescribed gross misconduct, the employer may, by written order, deprive her of the maternity benefit or medical bonus or both.
sub_structure.2_b: A woman deprived of maternity benefit/medical bonus, or discharged/dismissed during or on account of her Act-protected absence, may appeal to the prescribed authority within sixty days of communication of the order, and that authority's decision is final.

plain_english_summary: Protects pregnant and new mothers from being dismissed or having their service conditions worsened because of maternity-related absence, while allowing an employer to withhold benefits (but only via a formal written order, subject to appeal) if the woman was dismissed for gross misconduct as defined by rules.

title: No deduction of wages in certain cases
text: No deduction from the normal and usual daily wages of a woman entitled to maternity benefit may be made merely because of (a) the lighter nature of work assigned to her under section 4(3), or (b) nursing breaks allowed to her under section 11.
plain_english_summary: Prevents employers from cutting a woman's wages simply because she was given lighter duties during pregnancy or takes her allowed nursing breaks.

title: Appointment of Inspectors
text: The appropriate Government may, by notification, appoint officers it thinks fit as Inspectors for the purposes of this Act, and may define the local limits of their jurisdiction.
plain_english_summary: Allows the Government to appoint Inspectors with defined territorial jurisdiction to enforce the Act.

title: Powers and duties of Inspectors
text: An Inspector may, subject to prescribed restrictions or conditions, exercise the following powers:

sub_structure.a: Enter, at reasonable times with assistants from Government or local/public authority service, any premises where women are employed, to examine required registers, records and notices and require their production.
sub_structure.b: Examine any person found on the premises reasonably believed to be employed there, though no one can be compelled to answer self-incriminating questions.
sub_structure.c: Require the employer to furnish information on names/addresses of women employed, payments made, and applications/notices received under the Act.
sub_structure.d: Take copies of registers, records, notices or portions thereof.

plain_english_summary: Gives Inspectors entry, examination, information-gathering and document-copying powers to check employer compliance, with a built-in protection against self-incrimination for examined persons.

title: Inspectors to be public servants
text: Every Inspector appointed under this Act is deemed to be a public servant within the meaning of section 21 of the Indian Penal Code.
plain_english_summary: Confers public-servant status on Inspectors, attracting the corresponding legal protections and obligations under the Indian Penal Code.

title: Power of Inspector to direct payments to be made
text: (1) A woman claiming that maternity benefit or any other amount due to her (or a person claiming a section 7 payment) has been improperly withheld, or that she has been discharged/dismissed during or on account of Act-protected absence, may complain to the Inspector.

sub_structure.2_a: On inquiry, if satisfied payment has been wrongfully withheld, the Inspector may direct payment.
sub_structure.2_b: On inquiry, if satisfied the woman was wrongfully discharged/dismissed, the Inspector may pass just and proper orders.
sub_structure.3: A person aggrieved by the Inspector's decision may appeal to the prescribed authority within thirty days of communication.
sub_structure.4: The decision of the prescribed authority (on appeal) or of the Inspector (if no appeal) is final.
sub_structure.5: Any amount payable under this section is recoverable by the Collector, on a certificate issued by the Inspector, as an arrear of land revenue.

plain_english_summary: Establishes a complaint-and-inquiry mechanism before Inspectors for withheld maternity payments or unlawful dismissal, with a right of appeal to a prescribed authority and enforcement of unpaid amounts as land-revenue arrears.

title: Forfeiture of maternity benefit
text: If a woman works in any establishment during a period of authorised absence granted by her employer under section 6, she forfeits her claim to maternity benefit for that period.
plain_english_summary: A woman who works elsewhere during her sanctioned maternity leave loses her entitlement to maternity benefit for that period.

title: Abstract of Act and rules thereunder to be exhibited
text: An abstract of the Act's provisions and rules made under it, in the local language(s), must be exhibited by the employer in a conspicuous place in every part of the establishment where women are employed.
plain_english_summary: Requires employers to publicly display a summary of the Act and its rules, in local languages, where women employees can see it.

title: Registers, etc.
text: Every employer must prepare and maintain such registers, records and muster-rolls, and in such manner, as may be prescribed.
plain_english_summary: Imposes a general record-keeping obligation on employers regarding registers, records and muster-rolls.

title: Penalty for contravention of Act by employer
text: (1) If an employer fails to pay maternity benefit due to a woman under this Act, or discharges/dismisses her during or on account of Act-protected absence, he is punishable with imprisonment of not less than three months (extendable to one year) and fine of not less than two thousand rupees (extendable to five thousand rupees).

sub_structure.1_proviso: For sufficient reasons recorded in writing, the court may impose a lesser term of imprisonment, or fine only in lieu of imprisonment.
sub_structure.2: For any other contravention of the Act or rules for which no other penalty is provided, the employer is punishable with imprisonment up to one year, or fine up to five thousand rupees, or both; where the contravention concerns unpaid maternity benefit or other amount, the court must additionally recover that amount as if it were a fine and pay it to the person entitled.

plain_english_summary: Sets criminal penalties for employers who deny maternity benefit or unlawfully dismiss a protected woman (minimum 3 months' imprisonment and Rs 2,000 fine, up to 1 year/Rs 5,000), and a residual penalty for other violations, with courts empowered to recover unpaid amounts directly for the woman.

title: Penalty for obstructing Inspector
text: Whoever fails to produce, on an Inspector's demand, any register or document in their custody kept under this Act or its rules, or conceals or prevents any person from appearing before or being examined by an Inspector, is punishable with imprisonment up to one year, or fine up to five thousand rupees, or both.
plain_english_summary: Penalises obstruction of Inspectors-refusing to produce records or preventing witnesses from being examined-with imprisonment up to a year and/or a fine up to Rs 5,000.

title: Cognizance of offences
text: (1) An aggrieved woman, an office-bearer of a registered trade union of which she is a member, a registered voluntary organisation, or an Inspector, may file a complaint regarding an offence under this Act in a court of competent jurisdiction; no complaint may be filed after one year from the date the offence is alleged to have been committed.

sub_structure.2: No court inferior to a Metropolitan Magistrate or Magistrate of the first class may try an offence under this Act.

plain_english_summary: Widens who can initiate prosecution under the Act-beyond the woman herself, her union representative, a registered voluntary organisation, or an Inspector can complain-subject to a one-year limitation period, and fixes a minimum seniority for the trial court.

title: Protection of action taken in good faith
text: No suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding lies against any person for anything done or intended to be done in good faith under this Act or any rule or order made thereunder.
plain_english_summary: Shields officials and others from legal liability for good-faith acts done while implementing the Act.

title: Power of Central Government to give directions
text: The Central Government may give directions it deems necessary to a State Government regarding the execution of this Act's provisions, and the State Government must comply.
plain_english_summary: Lets the Central Government issue binding directions to State Governments on implementing the Act.

title: Power to exempt establishments
text: If satisfied that an establishment or class of establishments provides benefits not less favourable than those under this Act, the appropriate Government may, by notification, exempt it, subject to specified conditions and restrictions, from all or any of the Act's provisions or rules.
plain_english_summary: Allows exemption of employers who already offer equal-or-better maternity benefits, so they need not duplicate compliance with the Act's specific provisions.

title: Effect of laws and agreements inconsistent with this Act
text: (1) This Act has effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent in any other law or in the terms of any award, agreement or contract of service, made before or after the Act's commencement.

sub_structure.1_proviso: Where an award, agreement, contract of service or otherwise gives a woman more favourable benefits on a matter than this Act, she continues to be entitled to those more favourable benefits for that matter, even while receiving Act benefits on other matters.
sub_structure.2: Nothing in the Act precludes a woman from agreeing with her employer for rights or privileges more favourable than those under the Act.

plain_english_summary: The Act overrides inconsistent laws, awards, agreements or contracts, but a woman keeps any more-favourable benefit she already has on a specific matter, and can still negotiate better terms directly with her employer.

title: Power to make rules
text: (1) The appropriate Government may, subject to previous publication, by notification, make rules to carry out the purposes of this Act.

sub_structure.2_a: Rules may provide for preparation and maintenance of registers, records and muster-rolls.
sub_structure.2_b: Rules may provide for the exercise of powers, including inspection of establishments and Inspectors' duties.
sub_structure.2_c: Rules may provide for the method of payment of maternity benefit and other benefits not otherwise provided for in the Act.
sub_structure.2_d: Rules may provide for the form of notices under section 6.
sub_structure.2_e: Rules may provide for the nature of proof required under the Act.
sub_structure.2_f: Rules may provide for the duration of nursing breaks under section 11.
sub_structure.2_g: Rules may provide for acts constituting gross misconduct for section 12 purposes.
sub_structure.2_h: Rules may provide for the appellate authority, form, manner and procedure for appeals under section 12(2)(b).
sub_structure.2_i: Rules may provide for the appellate authority, form, manner and procedure for appeals against Inspector decisions under section 17.
sub_structure.2_j: Rules may provide for the form and manner of complaints to Inspectors under section 17(1) and the inquiry procedure under section 17(2).
sub_structure.2_k: Rules may provide for any other matter to be, or which may be, prescribed.
sub_structure.3: Every Central Government rule must be laid before each House of Parliament for a total of thirty days (in one or more sessions); if both Houses agree to modify or annul it before the next session ends, the rule has effect only as modified, or ceases to have effect, without prejudice to anything previously done under it.

plain_english_summary: Authorises the appropriate Government to make detailed implementing rules-covering records, inspection, payment methods, notice forms, proof requirements, gross misconduct, and appeal procedures-with Central Government rules subject to a parliamentary laying and modification/annulment process.

title: Amendment of Act 69 of 1951
text: Amends section 32 of the Plantations Labour Act, 1951: (a) in sub-section (1), removes the '(a)' before 'in the case of sickness', the word 'and' after 'sickness allowance', and omits clause (b); (b) in sub-section (2), removes the words 'or maternity'.
plain_english_summary: Makes consequential amendments to the Plantations Labour Act, 1951 to remove its now-redundant maternity-related provisions, since maternity benefit for plantation workers is now governed by this Act.

title: Repeal
text: On the application of this Act (i) to mines, the Mines Maternity Benefit Act, 1941 stands repealed; and (ii) to factories in the Union territory of Delhi, the Bombay Maternity Benefit Act, 1929 (as in force in that territory) stands repealed.
plain_english_summary: Repeals the two earlier maternity-benefit laws-covering mines and Delhi factories respectively-once this Act starts applying to those establishments.

title: Short title, extent and application
text: (1) This Act may be called the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965. (2) It extends to the whole of India. (3) Save as otherwise provided in this Act, it shall apply to every factory, and every other establishment in which twenty or more persons are employed on any day during an accounting year.

sub_structure.3_proviso: The appropriate Government may, after two months' notice by notification, apply the Act from a specified accounting year to establishments employing fewer than twenty persons, but not less than ten.
sub_structure.4: Save as otherwise provided, the Act has effect for the accounting year commencing on any day in 1964 and every subsequent accounting year.
sub_structure.4_proviso1: For Jammu and Kashmir, the reference to the 1964 accounting year is read as the accounting year commencing in 1968.
sub_structure.4_proviso2: Where the Act is extended to an establishment by notification under the proviso to sub-section (3), '1964' (or '1968') is read as the accounting year specified in that notification.
sub_structure.5: An establishment to which the Act applies continues to be governed by it even if the number of persons employed later falls below twenty (or the notified lower number).

plain_english_summary: Sets out the Act's name, its application across the whole of India, and that it covers factories and establishments with 20 or more employees (extendable down to 10 by government notification). Once covered, an establishment stays covered even if headcount later drops below the threshold.

title: Definitions
text: In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires-

sub_structure.1: 'accounting year' means: for a corporation, the year its books are closed and balanced; for a company, the period for which its profit and loss account is made up; in any other case, the year from 1 April, or, if the employer's accounts are closed on a different date, the year ending on that date (option, once exercised, not changeable without permission).
sub_structure.4: 'allocable surplus' means 67% of available surplus for a company (other than a banking company) that has not made arrangements under the Income-tax Act for declaring dividends within India, and 60% of available surplus in any other case.
sub_structure.5: 'appropriate Government' means the Central Government for establishments for which it is the appropriate Government under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, and the State Government for any other establishment.
sub_structure.6: 'available surplus' means the available surplus computed under section 5.
sub_structure.8: 'banking company' has the meaning given in the Banking Companies Act, 1949, and includes the State Bank of India, its subsidiary banks, corresponding new banks, co-operative banks, and any banking institution notified by the Central Government.
sub_structure.9: 'company' means a company as defined in section 3 of the Companies Act, 1956, and includes a foreign company.
sub_structure.11: 'corporation' means a body corporate established by a Central, Provincial or State Act, but not a company or co-operative society.
sub_structure.12: 'direct tax' means tax chargeable under the Income-tax Act, the Super Profits Tax Act 1963, the Companies (Profits) Surtax Act 1964, agricultural income-tax law, and any other tax the Central Government notifies as a direct tax for the purposes of this Act.
sub_structure.13: 'employee' means a person (other than an apprentice) employed on a salary or wage not exceeding twenty-one thousand rupees per mensem to do skilled or unskilled manual, supervisory, managerial, administrative, technical or clerical work, whether the terms of employment are express or implied.
sub_structure.14: 'employer' includes, for a factory, the owner or occupier (or agent/legal representative/named manager), and for any other establishment, the person or authority with ultimate control, or the manager/managing director/managing agent to whom such affairs are entrusted.
sub_structure.15: 'establishment in private sector' means any establishment other than an establishment in public sector.
sub_structure.16: 'establishment in public sector' means an establishment owned, controlled or managed by a Government company, or a corporation in which not less than 40% of capital is held by Government, Reserve Bank of India, or a corporation owned by them.
sub_structure.17: 'factory' has the meaning assigned in section 2(m) of the Factories Act, 1948.
sub_structure.21: 'salary or wage' means all remuneration (excluding overtime pay) expressed in money terms payable to an employee, including dearness allowance, but excluding other allowances, house/light/water/medical amenities, travelling concession, any bonus, employer's pension/provident fund contributions, retrenchment compensation/gratuity/ex gratia payments, and commission.
sub_structure.22: Words and expressions not defined here but defined in the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 have the meanings assigned there.

plain_english_summary: Defines key terms used throughout the Act. Most importantly, it caps 'employee' status at a monthly salary/wage of Rs 21,000, defines what counts as 'salary or wage' for bonus computation (excluding allowances, gratuity, commission, etc.), and fixes allocable surplus at 60% (or 67% for certain companies) of available surplus.

title: Establishments to include departments, undertakings and branches
text: Where an establishment consists of different departments or undertakings or has branches, whether in the same place or different places, all such departments, undertakings or branches are treated as parts of the same establishment for computing bonus under this Act.

sub_structure.proviso: Where a separate balance-sheet and profit and loss account are prepared for any such department, undertaking or branch for an accounting year, it is treated as a separate establishment for that year's bonus computation, unless it was already treated as part of the establishment immediately before that accounting year.

plain_english_summary: Branches and departments of one establishment are normally clubbed together for bonus purposes, unless a unit keeps its own separate accounts, in which case it is treated as a distinct establishment for that year.

title: Computation of gross profits
text: The gross profits derived by an employer from an establishment for an accounting year are calculated in the manner specified in the First Schedule for a banking company, and in the manner specified in the Second Schedule in any other case.
plain_english_summary: Directs that gross profits be worked out using the prescribed schedule format, with a distinct formula for banking companies (First Schedule) and all other employers (Second Schedule).

title: Computation of available surplus
text: The available surplus for an accounting year is the gross profits for that year after deducting the sums referred to in section 6.

sub_structure.proviso: From the accounting year commencing in 1968 onward, available surplus equals (a) gross profits after deducting section 6 sums, plus (b) the difference between the direct tax on the previous year's gross profits and the direct tax on the previous year's gross profits after deducting bonus paid/payable for that year.

plain_english_summary: Explains how 'available surplus'-the pool from which bonus is paid-is calculated: gross profits minus prior charges under section 6, plus (from 1968) a tax-adjustment add-back reflecting the tax saved by paying bonus in the preceding year.

title: Sums deductible from gross profits
text: The following sums are deducted from the gross profits as prior charges:

sub_structure.a: Depreciation admissible under section 32(1) of the Income-tax Act or agricultural income-tax law (with a proviso allowing continuation of notional normal depreciation for certain pre-29 May 1965 settlements/awards, at the employer's one-time option).
sub_structure.b: Any development rebate, investment allowance or development allowance the employer may deduct under the Income-tax Act.
sub_structure.c: Any direct tax the employer is liable to pay for the accounting year on income, profits and gains, subject to section 7.
sub_structure.d: Such further sums as are specified for the employer in the Third Schedule.

plain_english_summary: Lists the prior charges-depreciation, investment/development allowances, direct tax, and Third-Schedule items (like dividend and reserve requirements)-that must be subtracted from gross profits before arriving at available surplus.

title: Calculation of direct tax payable by the employer
text: Direct tax payable by the employer for an accounting year is calculated at the rates applicable to the employer's income for that year, subject to the following provisions:

sub_structure.a_i: No account is taken of any loss carried forward from a previous accounting year under direct tax law.
sub_structure.a_ii: No account is taken of arrears of depreciation addable to a following year's allowance under section 32(2) of the Income-tax Act.
sub_structure.a_iii: No account is taken of exemptions/deductions under sections 84 or 101(1) of the Income-tax Act (as they stood before the Finance Act, 1965).
sub_structure.b: A religious/charitable institution not covered by section 32, whose income is tax-exempt, is treated for that exempted income as a company in which the public are substantially interested.
sub_structure.c: For an individual or Hindu undivided family employer, tax is calculated as if the establishment's income were the employer's only income.
sub_structure.d: Any export rebate under direct tax law is disregarded.
sub_structure.e: No account is taken of any other rebate, credit, relief or deduction (besides development rebate/investment allowance/development allowance) allowed under direct tax law or the annual Finance Act for industrial development.

plain_english_summary: Provides detailed rules for computing the notional direct tax figure used in the bonus formula, stripping out carried-forward losses, certain exemptions and most rebates so the tax figure reflects a standardised calculation rather than the employer's actual tax bill.

title: Eligibility for bonus
text: Every employee is entitled to be paid bonus by his employer in an accounting year, in accordance with this Act, provided he has worked in the establishment for not less than thirty working days in that year.
plain_english_summary: The basic eligibility rule: an employee qualifies for bonus once they have worked at least 30 days in the establishment during the accounting year.

title: Disqualification for bonus
text: Notwithstanding anything in this Act, an employee is disqualified from receiving bonus if dismissed from service for:

sub_structure.a: fraud; or
sub_structure.b: riotous or violent behaviour while on the premises of the establishment; or
sub_structure.c: theft, misappropriation or sabotage of any property of the establishment.

plain_english_summary: An employee otherwise eligible loses their right to bonus if they were dismissed for fraud, violent conduct at the workplace, or theft/misappropriation/sabotage of company property.

title: Payment of minimum bonus
text: Subject to the other provisions of this Act, every employer must pay every employee, for the accounting year commencing in 1979 and every subsequent accounting year, a minimum bonus of 8.33% of the salary or wage earned by the employee during the accounting year or one hundred rupees, whichever is higher, whether or not the employer has any allocable surplus in that year.

sub_structure.proviso: Where the employee had not completed fifteen years of age at the start of the accounting year, 'sixty rupees' is substituted for 'one hundred rupees'.

plain_english_summary: Guarantees every eligible employee a minimum bonus of 8.33% of annual salary/wage or Rs 100 (Rs 60 for employees under 15), payable regardless of whether the employer actually made a surplus that year.

title: Payment of maximum bonus
text: (1) Where the allocable surplus for an accounting year exceeds the minimum bonus payable under section 10, the employer must instead pay every employee a bonus proportionate to the salary or wage earned during the year, subject to a maximum of twenty per cent of such salary or wage.

sub_structure.2: In computing allocable surplus under this section, amounts set on or set off under section 15 are taken into account.

plain_english_summary: Caps bonus at 20% of annual salary/wage: if the allocable surplus is large enough, employees get more than the statutory minimum, proportionate to their earnings, but never above this 20% ceiling.

title: Calculation of bonus with respect to certain employees
text: Where the salary or wage of an employee exceeds seven thousand rupees, or the minimum wage for the scheduled employment fixed by the appropriate Government (whichever is higher), per mensem, the bonus payable to that employee under section 10 or section 11 is calculated as if his salary or wage were seven thousand rupees (or that higher minimum wage figure), per mensem.

sub_structure.explanation: 'Scheduled employment' has the same meaning as in section 2(g) of the Minimum Wages Act, 1948.

plain_english_summary: For higher-paid employees (above the Rs 7,000/month bonus-calculation ceiling, or the relevant scheduled minimum wage if higher), bonus is calculated as if they earned only that ceiling amount, capping the payable bonus in rupee terms even though eligibility itself is based on the Rs 21,000 salary limit under section 2(13).

title: Proportionate reduction in bonus in certain cases
text: Where an employee has not worked all the working days in an accounting year, the minimum bonus of one hundred rupees (or sixty rupees, as applicable), if higher than 8.33% of the salary or wage for the days actually worked, is proportionately reduced.
plain_english_summary: If an employee worked only part of the year, the flat Rs 100/Rs 60 minimum bonus figure is scaled down proportionately to the days actually worked, rather than being paid in full.

title: Computation of number of working days
text: For the purposes of section 13, an employee is deemed to have worked in an establishment during an accounting year also on days when:

sub_structure.a: he was laid off under an agreement, standing orders, the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, or other applicable law;
sub_structure.b: he was on leave with salary or wage;
sub_structure.c: he was absent due to temporary disablement caused by an accident arising out of and in the course of employment; and
sub_structure.d: she was on maternity leave with salary or wage.

plain_english_summary: Certain days on which an employee did not physically work-lay-off, paid leave, work-related temporary disablement, and paid maternity leave-still count as 'working days' for the proportionate-reduction calculation.

title: Set on and set off of allocable surplus
text: (1) Where the allocable surplus for an accounting year exceeds the maximum bonus payable under section 11, the excess (up to 20% of the total salary or wage of employees for that year) is carried forward as a 'set on' for up to the next four accounting years, to be used for bonus payment as illustrated in the Fourth Schedule.

sub_structure.2: Where there is no available surplus, or the allocable surplus falls short of the minimum bonus payable under section 10, and there is insufficient set-on carried forward to cover it, the shortfall is carried forward as a 'set off' for up to the next four accounting years, as illustrated in the Fourth Schedule.
sub_structure.3: The set on/set off principle illustrated in the Fourth Schedule applies to all other cases not covered by sub-sections (1) or (2).
sub_structure.4: Where amounts have been carried forward and set on or set off, in calculating bonus for a succeeding year, the amount from the earliest accounting year is taken into account first.

plain_english_summary: Creates a smoothing mechanism: surplus beyond the 20% maximum bonus is banked ('set on') for up to four future years to fund bonus in leaner years, while shortfalls below the minimum bonus are similarly carried forward as a 'set off' debt against future surplus, following the worked example in the Fourth Schedule.

title: Special provisions with respect to certain establishments
text: (1) Where an establishment is newly set up, whether before or after the commencement of this Act, its employees are entitled to bonus in accordance with sub-sections (1A), (1B) and (1C).

sub_structure.1A: In the first five accounting years following the year the employer first sells goods/renders services from the new establishment, bonus is payable only for a year in which the employer derives profit from it, calculated under the Act for that year without applying section 15.
sub_structure.1B: For the sixth and seventh such accounting years, section 15 applies with modified set-on/set-off calculations taking into account only the fifth and sixth years (for the sixth year) or fifth, sixth and seventh years (for the seventh year).
sub_structure.1C: From the eighth such accounting year onward, section 15 applies to the establishment exactly as it applies to any other establishment.
sub_structure.explanation_1: An establishment is not deemed 'newly set up' merely because of a change in location, management, name or ownership.
sub_structure.explanation_2: For sub-section (1A), an employer is not deemed to have derived profit in a year unless depreciation provision has been made and arrears of depreciation/losses from earlier years have been fully set off against profits.
sub_structure.explanation_3: Sales during trial running of a factory, or the prospecting stage of a mine/oil field, are disregarded for sub-sections (1A)-(1C); disputes on this point are decided finally by the appropriate Government after hearing the parties.
sub_structure.2: Sub-sections (1), (1A), (1B) and (1C) apply, so far as may be, to new departments, undertakings or branches set up by existing establishments, subject to a proviso preserving pre-29 May 1965 consolidated-profit bonus practices for multi-branch employers.

plain_english_summary: Gives newly set-up establishments a phased-in bonus regime: profit-only bonus (no set on/set off) for the first five years, a partial set-on/set-off window for years six and seven, and full application of the normal section 15 rules from year eight onward.

title: Adjustment of customary or interim bonus against bonus payable under the Act
text: Where in an accounting year an employer has paid any puja bonus or other customary bonus to an employee, or has paid part of the statutory bonus before it became due, the employer may deduct the amount so paid from the bonus payable under this Act for that year, and the employee is entitled to receive only the balance.
plain_english_summary: Customary bonuses (like puja bonus) or early part-payments of statutory bonus can be offset against the bonus legally due, so employees don't receive both in full.

title: Deduction of certain amounts from bonus payable under the Act
text: Where in an accounting year an employee is found guilty of misconduct causing financial loss to the employer, the employer may deduct the amount of that loss from the bonus payable to the employee for that accounting year only, and the employee is entitled to receive the balance, if any.
plain_english_summary: An employer can offset financial losses caused by an employee's proven misconduct against that employee's bonus for the same year only, not against future years.

title: Time-limit for payment of bonus
text: All amounts payable to an employee by way of bonus under this Act must be paid in cash by the employer:

sub_structure.a: where a bonus dispute is pending before an authority under section 22, within one month from the date the award becomes enforceable or the settlement comes into operation;
sub_structure.b: in any other case, within eight months from the close of the accounting year.
sub_structure.proviso: The appropriate Government or specified authority may, on the employer's application and for sufficient reasons, extend the eight-month period, but the total extension cannot exceed two years.

plain_english_summary: Bonus must be paid in cash, generally within eight months of the close of the accounting year (or within a month of a dispute award/settlement), with a possible government-approved extension capped at two years in total.

title: Application of Act to establishments in public sector in certain cases
text: (1) If in any accounting year a public-sector establishment sells goods or renders services in competition with a private-sector establishment, and income from such sale/services is not less than twenty per cent of its gross income for that year, the Act applies to it as it applies to a like private-sector establishment.

sub_structure.2: Save as provided in sub-section (1), nothing in this Act applies to employees of any public-sector establishment.

plain_english_summary: Public-sector undertakings are generally outside the Act, except where they compete commercially with private industry and derive at least 20% of gross income from that competitive activity-in which case the Act applies to them just like a private employer.

title: Recovery of bonus due from an employer
text: Where money is due to an employee by way of bonus under a settlement, award or agreement, the employee (or an authorised person, or heirs/assignee on death) may apply to the appropriate Government for recovery; if satisfied, the Government issues a recovery certificate to the Collector, who recovers it as an arrear of land revenue.

sub_structure.proviso_1: Such application must be made within one year from the date the money became due.
sub_structure.proviso_2: A late application may still be entertained if the appropriate Government is satisfied there was sufficient cause for the delay.
sub_structure.explanation: In this section and sections 22-25, 'employee' includes a person entitled to bonus under the Act who is no longer employed.

plain_english_summary: Provides a government-backed recovery mechanism-akin to recovering land revenue arrears-for employees owed bonus, with a normal one-year limitation period that can be relaxed for sufficient cause.

title: Reference of disputes under the Act
text: Any dispute between an employer and employees regarding bonus payable under this Act, or regarding the Act's application to a public-sector establishment, is deemed an industrial dispute under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (or corresponding state law), and that Act's provisions apply accordingly.
plain_english_summary: Bonus disputes are routed through the ordinary industrial-dispute machinery (Labour Courts, Tribunals, etc.) under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.

title: Presumption about accuracy of balance-sheet and profit and loss account of corporations and companies
text: (1) Where, in proceedings before an authority under the Industrial Disputes Act (or corresponding law) on a bonus dispute, the duly audited balance-sheet and profit and loss account of a corporation or company (other than a banking company) are produced, the authority may presume the statements accurate without the corporation/company needing to prove accuracy by affidavit or other mode.

sub_structure.1_proviso: If the authority is satisfied the statements are not accurate, it may take steps it considers necessary to verify them.
sub_structure.2: On application by a trade union or, absent one, the employees, requiring clarification of any balance-sheet/P&L item, the authority may direct the corporation or company to furnish the clarification within a specified time, and it must comply.

plain_english_summary: Audited balance sheets and profit and loss accounts of corporations/companies are presumed accurate in bonus disputes, saving the employer the burden of separately proving them, though the tribunal can still probe accuracy or order clarifications for the union/employees.

title: Audited accounts of banking companies not to be questioned
text: (1) Where a bonus dispute involving a banking company is before an authority and its duly audited accounts are produced, the authority must not permit any trade union or employees to question the accounts' correctness, though they may be permitted to obtain information necessary to verify the amount of bonus due.

sub_structure.2: This does not entitle the trade union or employees to any information the banking company is not compelled to furnish under section 34A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

plain_english_summary: Banking companies' audited accounts get extra protection in bonus disputes-their correctness cannot be challenged-though employees can still seek limited information needed to verify the bonus amount, subject to banking-secrecy provisions.

title: Audit of accounts of employers, not being corporations or companies
text: (1) Where a bonus dispute involves an employer who is not a corporation or company, and duly qualified auditor-audited accounts are produced before the authority, section 23 applies to those accounts as far as may be.

sub_structure.2: If the authority finds the employer's accounts have not been so audited and considers an audit necessary, it may direct the employer to get them audited within a specified time.
sub_structure.3: If the employer fails to get the accounts audited, the authority may itself get them audited by an auditor of its choice, without prejudice to section 28 (penalty).
sub_structure.4: Accounts audited under sub-section (2) or (3) are then treated under section 23 as well.
sub_structure.5: Expenses of an audit under sub-section (3), including auditor remuneration, are determined (finally) by the authority and paid by the employer, recoverable as under section 21 in default.

plain_english_summary: For individual/firm employers (not corporations or companies), the authority can order accounts to be audited if not already properly audited, and even arrange the audit itself at the employer's expense if the employer fails to comply.

title: Maintenance of registers, records, etc.
text: Every employer must prepare and maintain such registers, records and other documents in such form and manner as may be prescribed.
plain_english_summary: Employers have an ongoing statutory obligation to keep prescribed bonus-related registers and records.

title: Inspectors
text: (1) The appropriate Government may, by notification, appoint Inspectors for the purposes of this Act and define their jurisdiction.

sub_structure.2_a: An Inspector may require an employer to furnish necessary information.
sub_structure.2_b: An Inspector may enter any establishment or connected premises at a reasonable time (with assistance if needed) and require production of accounts, books, registers and other documents relating to employment, salary/wage or bonus payment.
sub_structure.2_c: An Inspector may examine the employer, agent, servant, or any person in charge of the establishment, or any person reasonably believed to be or have been an employee, on relevant matters.
sub_structure.2_d: An Inspector may make copies of or take extracts from any relevant book, register or document.
sub_structure.2_e: An Inspector may exercise such other powers as may be prescribed.
sub_structure.3: Every Inspector is deemed a public servant within the meaning of the Indian Penal Code.
sub_structure.4: Any person required to produce documents or give information to an Inspector is legally bound to do so.
sub_structure.5: An Inspector cannot require a banking company to furnish or disclose anything it is not compelled to furnish under section 34A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

plain_english_summary: Empowers appointed Inspectors to enter establishments, inspect and copy records, question relevant persons, and compel information from employers to check compliance-subject to banking-secrecy limits for banking companies.

title: Penalty
text: If any person contravenes any provision of this Act or any rule made thereunder, or fails to comply with a direction or requisition given under the Act, he is punishable with imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both.
plain_english_summary: General penalty provision for violations of the Act or its rules, or non-compliance with lawful directions: up to six months' imprisonment and/or a fine up to Rs 1,000.

title: Offences by companies
text: (1) Where a company commits an offence under this Act, every person in charge of and responsible to the company for its business conduct at the time, as well as the company, is deemed guilty and liable to be proceeded against, unless he proves the offence occurred without his knowledge or that he exercised due diligence to prevent it.

sub_structure.2: Notwithstanding sub-section (1), where the offence is proved to have been committed with the consent, connivance, or attributable neglect of any director, manager, secretary or other officer, that person is also deemed guilty and liable.
sub_structure.explanation_a: 'Company' means any body corporate and includes a firm or other association of individuals.
sub_structure.explanation_b: 'Director', for a firm, means a partner.

plain_english_summary: Extends criminal liability for a company's offence under the Act to persons in charge of its business, and separately to directors/officers whose consent, connivance or neglect contributed to the offence-subject to a due-diligence defence.

title: Cognizance of offences
text: (1) No court can take cognizance of any offence under this Act except on a complaint by or under the authority of the appropriate Government, or an authorised officer of that Government (not below Regional Labour Commissioner for the Centre, or Labour Commissioner for a State).

sub_structure.2: No court inferior to a presidency magistrate or magistrate of the first class can try an offence under this Act.

plain_english_summary: Restricts prosecution under the Act to government-sanctioned complaints and requires trial before a sufficiently senior magistrate.

title: Protection of action taken under the Act
text: No suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding lies against the Government or any Government officer for anything done or intended to be done in good faith under this Act or any rule made thereunder.
plain_english_summary: Shields the Government and its officers from legal proceedings for good-faith actions taken in implementing the Act.

title: Special provision with respect to payment of bonus linked with production or productivity
text: Notwithstanding anything in this Act, where employees enter into an agreement or settlement with their employer (before or after the commencement of the Payment of Bonus (Amendment) Act, 1976) for payment of an annual bonus linked with production or productivity in lieu of profit-based bonus under this Act, they are entitled to receive the bonus due under such agreement or settlement.

sub_structure.proviso_1: Any such agreement or settlement by which employees relinquish their right to the minimum bonus under section 10 is null and void to that extent.
sub_structure.proviso_2: Such employees cannot be paid bonus exceeding twenty per cent of the salary or wage earned during the relevant accounting year.

plain_english_summary: Allows employers and employees to agree on a productivity-linked bonus instead of the standard profit-linked formula, but the statutory minimum bonus can never be bargained away and the 20% overall cap still applies.

title: Act not to apply to certain classes of employees
text: Nothing in this Act applies to the classes of employees listed below.

sub_structure.i: Employees of any insurer carrying on general insurance business, and employees of the Life Insurance Corporation of India.
sub_structure.ii: Seamen as defined in the Merchant Shipping Act, 1958.
sub_structure.iii: Employees registered/listed under a scheme made under the Dock Workers (Regulation of Employment) Act, 1948, employed by registered/listed employers.
sub_structure.iv: Employees of an establishment in an industry carried on by or under the authority of a Central/State Government department or a local authority.
sub_structure.v: Employees of the Indian Red Cross Society or similar institutions, universities and educational institutions, and non-profit institutions (including hospitals, chambers of commerce, social welfare institutions).
sub_structure.viii: Employees of the Reserve Bank of India.
sub_structure.ix: Employees of specified financial institutions, including the Industrial Finance Corporation of India, State/Joint Financial Corporations, the Deposit Insurance Corporation, NABARD, the Unit Trust of India, the Industrial Development Bank of India, SIDBI, the National Housing Bank, and any other public-sector financial institution the Central Government notifies having regard to its capital structure, objectives, Government assistance and other relevant factors.
sub_structure.xi: Employees of inland water transport establishments operating on routes passing through any other country.

plain_english_summary: Carves out a list of employee categories-insurance and LIC staff, seamen, dock workers, government-department industry employees, charitable/educational institution staff, RBI staff, specified development finance institution staff, and certain inland water-transport employees-who fall entirely outside the Act.

title: [Repealed]
text: Repealed by the Payment of Bonus (Amendment) Act, 1976 (23 of 1976), s. 23, with effect from 25-9-1975. (Formerly dealt with application of the Act to certain pending disputes regarding payment of bonus.)
plain_english_summary: This section, which originally addressed pending bonus disputes at the time of enactment, has been repealed and no longer has effect.

title: Effect of laws and agreements inconsistent with the Act
text: Subject to section 31A, this Act has effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent in any other law for the time being in force, or in the terms of any award, agreement, settlement or contract of service.
plain_english_summary: The Act overrides any inconsistent law, award, agreement, settlement or employment contract, except where section 31A's productivity-linked bonus arrangements apply.

title: Saving
text: Nothing in this Act affects the provisions of the Coal Mines Provident Fund and Bonus Schemes Act, 1948, or any scheme made under it.
plain_english_summary: Preserves the separate bonus scheme under the Coal Mines Provident Fund and Bonus Schemes Act, 1948, which continues to operate independently of this Act.

title: Power of exemption
text: If the appropriate Government, considering the financial position and other relevant circumstances of an establishment or class of establishments, is of the opinion that applying all or any provisions of this Act would not be in the public interest, it may, by notification, exempt such establishment(s) from all or any provisions for a specified period, subject to conditions it may impose.
plain_english_summary: Gives Government a discretionary power to exempt financially struggling establishments from some or all of the Act's requirements, for a defined period and subject to conditions.

title: [Repealed]
text: Repealed by the Payment of Bonus (Amendment) Act, 1976 (23 of 1976), s. 23, with effect from 25-9-1975. (Formerly the power to remove difficulties.)
plain_english_summary: This section, which originally gave a power to remove difficulties in implementing the Act, has been repealed and no longer has effect.

title: Power to make rules
text: (1) The Central Government may, subject to previous publication, by notification, make rules to carry out the provisions of this Act.

sub_structure.2_a: Rules may provide for the authority granting permission under the proviso to section 2(1)(iii).
sub_structure.2_b: Rules may provide for the form and manner of preparing and maintaining registers, records and documents under section 26.
sub_structure.2_c: Rules may provide for powers exercisable by an Inspector under section 27(2)(e).
sub_structure.2_d: Rules may provide for any other matter to be, or which may be, prescribed.
sub_structure.3: Every rule must be laid before each House of Parliament for a total of thirty days (in one session or successive sessions); if both Houses agree to modify or annul it before the following session ends, the rule has effect only as modified, or ceases to have effect, without prejudice to anything previously done under it.

plain_english_summary: Authorises the Central Government to frame rules implementing the Act (covering registers, Inspector powers, permissions, etc.), subject to a parliamentary laying and modification/annulment procedure.

title: Application of certain law not barred
text: Save as otherwise expressly provided, the provisions of this Act are in addition to, and not in derogation of, the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, or any corresponding state law relating to investigation and settlement of industrial disputes.
plain_english_summary: Clarifies that this Act supplements, rather than replaces, the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 and equivalent state laws.

title: Repeal and saving
text: (1) The Payment of Bonus Ordinance, 1965 (3 of 1965), is repealed.

sub_structure.2: Notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or action taken under the Ordinance is deemed to have been done or taken under this Act, as if this Act had commenced on 29th May, 1965.

plain_english_summary: Repeals the earlier Ordinance that this Act replaced, while preserving everything already done under it as if this Act itself had commenced on 29 May 1965.

title: Computation of Gross Profits (Banking Companies)
text: Prescribes the format under section 4(a) for computing the gross profits of a banking company for bonus purposes: starting from net profit per the profit and loss account, adding back provisions for bonus, depreciation, development rebate reserve and other reserves, adding back bonus paid for previous years, excess gratuity provision, excess donations, certain capital expenditure/losses, RBI-certified amounts, and losses relating to business outside India, adding income credited directly to reserves (subject to exclusions), and then deducting capital receipts/profits, income/receipts relating to business outside India, expenditure/losses debited directly to reserves, allocable head-office overheads for foreign banking companies, refunds of excess direct tax or written-back provisions, and specified cash subsidies, to arrive at gross profits for bonus purposes.
plain_english_summary: A detailed accounting worksheet specifically for banking companies, starting from net profit and making a series of standardised add-backs and deductions (depreciation, reserves, capital items, foreign-business items, subsidies, etc.) to arrive at a uniform 'gross profits' figure used for the bonus calculation.

title: Computation of Gross Profits (Other Employers)
text: Prescribes the format under section 4(b) for computing gross profits for employers other than banking companies: starting from net profit per the profit and loss account, adding back provisions for bonus, depreciation, direct taxes, development rebate/investment allowance/development allowance reserve and other reserves, adding back bonus paid for previous years, excess gratuity provision, excess donations, certain annuity payments under section 280D of the Income-tax Act, certain capital expenditure/losses, and losses relating to business outside India, adding income credited directly to reserves (subject to exclusions), and then deducting capital receipts/profits, income/receipts relating to business outside India, expenditure/losses debited directly to reserves, allocable head-office overheads for foreign concerns, refunds of excess tax or written-back provisions, and specified cash subsidies, to arrive at gross profits for bonus purposes.
plain_english_summary: The equivalent gross-profits worksheet used by all non-banking employers, following the same add-back/deduction logic as the First Schedule but tailored to non-banking accounts (e.g., including direct taxes and annuity deposits in the add-backs).

title: Further Sums Deductible from Gross Profits (Prior Charges)
text: Prescribes, under section 6(d), further sums deductible from gross profits depending on the category of employer: for a company (other than a banking company), preference dividends, 8.5% of paid-up equity capital, and 6% of reserves; for a banking company, preference dividends, 7.5% of paid-up equity capital, 5% of reserves, and certain statutory reserve transfers (whichever is higher), with special proportional rules for foreign companies/banks; for a corporation, 8.5% of paid-up capital and 6% of reserves; for a co-operative society, 8.5% of invested capital and statutory reserve-fund transfers; for any other employer, 8.5% of invested capital (with provisions for annuity deposits, and partner/proprietor remuneration deductions for firms, individuals and Hindu undivided families capped at 25% of gross profits or forty-eight thousand rupees per partner/proprietor, whichever is less); and, for licensees under the Electricity (Supply) Act, 1948, amounts required to be appropriated to a reserve under its Sixth Schedule, in addition to the above.

sub_structure.explanation: 'Reserves' in Items 1(iii), 2(iii) and 3(ii) excludes amounts set apart for payable direct tax, section 6(a) depreciation, and declared dividends, but includes amounts set apart beyond those for direct tax reserves and excess depreciation provisions.

plain_english_summary: Sets out category-specific prior charges-return on capital/reserves for companies, corporations, co-operatives, and other employers, plus special rules for firms/individuals' partner remuneration and electricity licensees-that must be deducted from gross profits before the available surplus is computed.

title: Illustration of Set On and Set Off of Allocable Surplus
text: Illustrates, under sections 15 and 16, the working of set on and set off of allocable surplus over a ten-year example where the total 8.33% minimum bonus for all employees is assumed to be Rs 1,04,167 and the 20% maximum bonus is assumed to be Rs 2,50,000. The table shows, year by year, the allocable surplus, the amount actually paid as bonus (subject to the minimum/maximum), the set on or set off arising for that year, and the cumulative set on/set off carried forward, including a lapse of a 4th-year-old set-on balance after the permitted carry-forward period.
plain_english_summary: A worked numerical example spanning ten years showing exactly how surplus above the maximum bonus is banked forward ('set on') and deficits below the minimum bonus are carried as debts ('set off'), including how a set-on balance can lapse if not used within four years.

title: Short title, extent, application and commencement
text: This Act may be called the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972. It extends to the whole of India, except that provisions relating to plantations or ports do not extend to the State of Jammu and Kashmir.

sub_structure.3: (3) It shall apply to - (a) every factory, mine, oilfield, plantation, port and railway company; (b) every shop or establishment in which ten or more persons are employed, or were employed, on any day of the preceding twelve months; (c) such other establishments as the Central Government may notify.
sub_structure.3A: (3A) A shop or establishment to which this Act has become applicable shall continue to be governed by this Act even if the number of persons employed later falls below ten.
sub_structure.4: (4) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification, appoint.

plain_english_summary: Sets out the Act's name, its nationwide reach (with a Jammu & Kashmir carve-out for plantations/ports), and that it covers factories, mines, ports, railways and any shop/establishment with 10+ employees, which stays covered even if staff numbers later drop.

title: Definitions
text: Defines the key terms used throughout the Act.

sub_structure.a: "appropriate Government" - the Central Government for establishments it controls, major ports, mines, oilfields, railways, or multi-state establishments; the State Government in all other cases.
sub_structure.e: "employee" - any person (other than an apprentice) employed on wages to do skilled, semi-skilled, unskilled, manual, supervisory, technical, clerical, managerial or administrative work, but excludes Central/State Government post-holders governed by their own gratuity rules.
sub_structure.f: "employer" - the person or authority with ultimate control over the establishment's affairs, including a government-appointed supervisor for government-controlled establishments.
sub_structure.h: "family" - for a male employee: himself, wife, children, dependent parents (and wife's dependent parents) and predeceased son's widow/children. For a female employee: the equivalent list with her husband in place of wife.
sub_structure.s: "wages" - all emoluments earned while on duty or leave, paid or payable in cash, including dearness allowance, but excluding bonus, commission, house rent allowance, overtime wages and other allowances.

plain_english_summary: Defines the Act's core vocabulary - who counts as an 'employee' and 'employer', what 'wages' and 'family' mean, and which government (Central or State) is the 'appropriate Government' for a given establishment.

title: Continuous service
text: Defines when an employee is treated as being in 'continuous service' for gratuity eligibility purposes, including deemed continuous service based on minimum days actually worked.

sub_structure.1: (1) An employee is in continuous service if uninterrupted, or if interrupted only by sickness, accident, leave, authorised absence, lay-off, strike, lock-out, or a work stoppage not the employee's fault.
sub_structure.2a: (2)(a) Deemed continuous service for one year if the employee actually worked at least 190 days (below-ground mine/less-than-6-day week establishments) or 240 days (other cases) in the preceding 12 months.
sub_structure.2b: (2)(b) Deemed continuous service for six months if the employee actually worked at least 95 days or 120 days (as above) in the preceding six months.
sub_structure.3: (3) For seasonal establishments, deemed continuous service applies if the employee worked at least 75% of the days the establishment was in operation during the period.

plain_english_summary: Explains the minimum attendance thresholds (e.g. 240 days in a year, or 120 days in six months) an employee must actually work to be treated as having rendered 'continuous service', which determines gratuity eligibility.

title: Controlling authority
text: The appropriate Government may, by notification, appoint any officer to be a controlling authority responsible for administering this Act; different controlling authorities may be appointed for different areas.
plain_english_summary: Allows the government to appoint officers as 'controlling authorities' to administer the Act, with different officers covering different areas.

title: Payment of gratuity
text: Gratuity is payable to an employee on termination of employment after at least five years of continuous service, on superannuation, retirement, resignation, death or disablement (the five-year requirement is waived for death or disablement).

sub_structure.2: (2) Gratuity is paid at fifteen days' wages (last drawn) for every completed year of service or part thereof exceeding six months; for monthly-rated employees, fifteen days' wages = (monthly wage / 26) x 15; seasonal establishment employees get seven days' wages per season.
sub_structure.3: (3) The amount of gratuity payable to an employee shall not exceed three lakh fifty thousand rupees.
sub_structure.6a: (6)(a) Gratuity is forfeited to the extent of damage/loss where an employee's services are terminated for wilful damage to the employer's property.
sub_structure.6b: (6)(b) Gratuity may be wholly or partially forfeited if the employee's services are terminated for riotous/disorderly/violent conduct, or for an offence involving moral turpitude committed during employment.

plain_english_summary: Establishes the core gratuity entitlement: employees get 15 days' wages per completed year of service after 5 years of continuous service (waived on death/disablement), capped at Rs. 3,50,000, and lays out when an employer can forfeit gratuity for employee misconduct.

title: Compulsory insurance
text: Every employer (other than Central/State Government establishments) must obtain insurance for their gratuity liability from LIC or another prescribed insurer, unless exempted for having an approved gratuity fund.

sub_structure.2: (2) The appropriate Government may exempt employers who already have an approved gratuity fund, or who employ 500+ persons and establish such a fund, from the compulsory insurance requirement.
sub_structure.3: (3) Every employer must register their establishment with the controlling authority; registration requires proof of insurance or an approved gratuity fund.
sub_structure.6: (6) Failure to pay insurance premiums or fund contributions is punishable with a fine up to ten thousand rupees, plus one thousand rupees per day for a continuing offence.

plain_english_summary: Requires employers to insure their gratuity liability (typically with LIC) or maintain an approved gratuity fund, and register with the controlling authority; non-payment of premiums/contributions attracts fines.

title: Power to exempt
text: The appropriate Government may, by notification, exempt any establishment or any employee/class of employees from the Act if they already receive gratuity or pensionary benefits at least as favourable as under this Act.

sub_structure.3: (3) Such an exemption notification may be issued retrospectively, but not before the Act's commencement date, and not so as to prejudicially affect anyone's interests.

plain_english_summary: Lets the government exempt an establishment or employees from the Act where they already get equal or better gratuity/pension benefits elsewhere.

title: Nomination
text: Every employee who completes one year of service must file a nomination, in the prescribed form, for gratuity payable in case of death.

sub_structure.2: (2) An employee may split the gratuity amount among more than one nominee.
sub_structure.3: (3) If the employee has a family, the nomination must be in favour of one or more family members; a nomination in favour of a non-family member is void.
sub_structure.4: (4) If the employee has no family when nominating, they may nominate anyone; but if they later acquire a family, that nomination becomes invalid and a fresh family nomination is required.
sub_structure.6: (6) If a nominee predeceases the employee, the employee must make a fresh nomination for that interest.

plain_english_summary: Requires employees with one year of service to file a gratuity nomination, generally in favour of family members, which must be updated if family circumstances or a nominee's death change.

title: Determination of the amount of gratuity
text: The employer must determine the gratuity amount as soon as it becomes payable (whether or not an application is made) and give written notice to the payee and the controlling authority.

sub_structure.3: (3) The employer must pay the gratuity within thirty days of it becoming payable.
sub_structure.3A: (3A) If not paid within thirty days, the employer must pay simple interest from the due date until payment, unless the delay is the employee's fault and the controlling authority has approved the delay in writing.
sub_structure.4a: (4)(a) If there is a dispute over the amount, admissibility, or the person entitled to gratuity, the employer must deposit with the controlling authority the amount it admits is payable.
sub_structure.4c: (4)(c)-(d) The controlling authority, after a hearing, determines the dispute and directs payment of any additional amount found due; it also pays out the deposited amount to the person entitled.
sub_structure.7: (7) An order under sub-section (4) may be appealed to the appropriate Government or a specified appellate authority within sixty days (extendable by a further sixty days for sufficient cause); an employer's appeal requires a deposit of the disputed gratuity amount.

plain_english_summary: Sets the procedure and 30-day deadline for employers to determine and pay gratuity, requires interest on late payment, and provides a dispute-resolution and appeal process before the controlling authority when there's disagreement over who is owed what.

title: Inspectors
text: The appropriate Government may appoint Inspectors for the purposes of this Act and define the areas over which their authority extends; every Inspector is deemed a public servant.
plain_english_summary: Allows the government to appoint Inspectors to oversee compliance with the Act, treating them as public servants under the Indian Penal Code.

title: Powers of Inspectors
text: Inspectors may require employers to furnish information, enter and inspect premises, examine employers/employees, and copy, take extracts from, search for and seize relevant registers, records or documents.

sub_structure.2: (2) Persons required to produce documents or give information are deemed legally bound to do so under sections 175/176 of the Indian Penal Code.
sub_structure.3: (3) Code of Criminal Procedure provisions on search/seizure under a warrant apply to searches and seizures made under this section.

plain_english_summary: Gives Inspectors investigative powers - to demand information, inspect premises, examine people, and search and seize records - to check compliance with the Act.

title: Recovery of gratuity
text: If gratuity is not paid within the prescribed time, the controlling authority, on application by the aggrieved person, issues a recovery certificate to the Collector, who recovers the amount (plus compound interest) as arrears of land revenue, after giving the employer a chance to be heard.
plain_english_summary: Provides an enforcement mechanism: unpaid gratuity can be recovered from the employer like unpaid land revenue, through the Collector, with interest (though interest can't exceed the gratuity amount itself).

title: Penalties
text: Making a false statement to avoid gratuity payment is punishable with up to six months' imprisonment, or a fine up to ten thousand rupees, or both.

sub_structure.2: (2) An employer who contravenes or defaults on the Act's provisions is punishable with imprisonment of three months to one year, or a fine of ten to twenty thousand rupees, or both; for non-payment of gratuity specifically, imprisonment is not less than six months (extendable to two years), unless the court records reasons for a lesser sentence.

plain_english_summary: Sets criminal penalties for false statements made to dodge gratuity payments and for employer non-compliance, with a stricter minimum six-month jail term specifically for non-payment of gratuity.

title: Exemption of employer from liability in certain cases
text: An employer charged with an offence may, after giving notice, have the actual offender brought before the court; if the employer proves due diligence and lack of knowledge/consent, the actual offender is convicted instead and the employer is discharged.
plain_english_summary: Lets an employer escape liability for an offence under the Act by proving someone else was the real offender and that the employer exercised due diligence and had no knowledge of the wrongdoing.

title: Cognizance of offences
text: No court shall take cognizance of an offence under this Act except on a complaint by or under the authority of the appropriate Government; if gratuity remains unpaid/unrecovered six months after the prescribed time, the Government must authorise the controlling authority to complain to a Magistrate within fifteen days.

sub_structure.2: (2) No court inferior to a Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the first class may try an offence under this Act.

plain_english_summary: Restricts prosecutions under the Act to complaints authorised by the government, and mandates that the controlling authority must file a complaint if gratuity stays unpaid six months past due.

title: Protection of action taken in good faith
text: No suit or other legal proceeding lies against the controlling authority or any other person for anything done, or intended to be done, in good faith under this Act.
plain_english_summary: Shields the controlling authority and others acting in good faith under the Act from being sued for their official actions.

title: Protection of gratuity
text: No gratuity payable under this Act (including to employees in exempted establishments) can be attached in execution of any civil, revenue, or criminal court decree or order.
plain_english_summary: Protects an employee's gratuity from being seized to satisfy a court decree or order against them.

title: Act to override other enactments, etc.
text: This Act (and rules made under it) has effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent in any other enactment, instrument, or contract.
plain_english_summary: Gives this Act overriding effect over any conflicting law, contract, or instrument.

title: Power to make rules
text: The appropriate Government may, by notification, make rules to carry out the Act's provisions.

sub_structure.2: (2) Rules made by the Central Government must be laid before both Houses of Parliament for 30 days; Parliament may modify or annul them, without affecting the validity of anything already done under the rule.

plain_english_summary: Gives the government rule-making power to implement the Act, subject to parliamentary review of any Central Government rules.

title: Short title, extent, commencement and application

sub_structure.1: (1) This Act may be called the Payment of Wages Act, 1936.
sub_structure.2: (2) It extends to the whole of India 4***.
sub_structure.3: (3) It shall come into force on such date 5 as the Central Government may , by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.
sub_structure.4: (4) It applies in the first instance to the payment of wages to persons employed in any factory, to persons employed (otherwise than in a factory) upon any railway by a railway administration or, either directly or through a sub-contractor, by a person fulfilling a contract with a railway administration , and to persons employed in an industrial or other establishment specified in sub -clauses (a) to ( g) of clause (ii) of section 2.
sub_structure.5: (5) Appropriate Government may, after giving three months‟ notice of its intention of so doing, by notification in the Official Gazette, extend the provi sions of this Act or any of them to the payment of wages to any class of persons employed in any establishment or class of establishments specified by appropriate Government under sub-clause (h) of clause (ii) of section 2: Provided that in relation to any such establishment owned by the Central Government no such notification shall be issued except with the concurrence of that Government.
sub_structure.6: (6) This Act applies to wages payable to an employed person in respect of a wage period if such wages for that wage period do not exceed twenty four thousand rupees per month or such other higher sum which, on the basis of figures of the Consumer Expenditure Survey published by the National Sample Survey Organisation, the Central Government may, after every five years, by notification in the Official Gazette, specify.

plain_english_summary: States the Act's short title, that it applies across India, that it comes into force on a date the Central Government notifies, which categories of workplaces it initially covers, and that it applies only to employees earning up to a government-notified wage ceiling (currently Rs. 24,000/month).

title: Definitions
text: In this Act, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context,— (i) “appropriate Government” means, in relation to railways, air transport services, mines and oilfields, the Central Government and, in relation to all other cases, the State Government; (ia) “employed person” includes the legal representative of a deceased employed person; (ib) “employer” includes the legal representative of a deceased employer; (ic) “factory” means a factory as defined in clause ( m) of section 2 of the Factories Act, 1948 (63 of 1948) , and includes any place to which the provisions of that Act have been applied under sub-section (1) of section 85 thereof; (ii) “industrial or other establishment” means any— (a) tramway service, or motor transport service engaged in carrying passenger or goods or both by road for hire or reward; (aa) air transport service other than such service belonging to, or exclusively employed in the military, naval or air forces of the Union or the Civil Aviation Department of the Government of India;
